title: t19113: fix(permission-broker): allow designed bounded-operation status polls through...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19113` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(permission-broker): allow designed bounded-operation status polls through OpenCode doom_loop instead of killing headless workers

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Headless workers die partway through finished work when they wait on a long `aidevops_bounded_operation` command. OpenCode's built-in `doom_loop` guard fires when the last three parts of the current assistant message are identical tool calls (for example `{"action":"status","operation_id":"op_…","wait_seconds":60}`). In OpenCode 1.19 each step is a new assistant message, so this fires only when one response fans out three identical calls in parallel; sequential polls across steps never trigger it. The OpenCode session DB shows workers doing exactly that before the rejection. The headless permission broker classifies `doom_loop` as non-grantable, rejects it, and the worker session ends with `permission_required`.

Evidence from one runner on 2026-11-18 (OpenCode 1.19.6):

- `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl`: six `permission_request_non_grantable` events with `permission=doom_loop tool=aidevops_bounded_operation` between 15:28Z and 18:18Z, on three managed-repo issues. Before today there were only three in two weeks.
- The worker failure excerpts for two of them show the worker had pushed commits (and in one case opened a draft PR), then polled the same running publish operation with identical `status` arguments. The log line `permission requested: doom_loop (aidevops_bounded_operation); auto-rejecting` is followed by `[WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS] cause=permission_required`. The completion work (publish receipt, PR finalisation) was lost and the issue went back into the queue.
- The installed OpenCode binary raises `doom_loop` with `patterns:[toolName]` and `metadata:{tool, input}`, and no call ID. So the broker can see exactly which call repeated.

Designed polling is the documented way to wait on a bounded operation. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-loops.mjs` already exempts it as `isDesignedPoll()` from aidevops' own loop detector. The status/output actions are read-only and each response reports new elapsed time, so repeating them is not a loop. GH#37625 hit the same guard with `sleep 60` and was closed with a prose-only change to `pulse-sweep.md`. A deterministic rule is needed.

## How

- NEW `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-designed-poll.mjs`: export `isDesignedPollDoomLoop(request)`. It returns true only when `permission` (or the legacy `type`) is `doom_loop`, the tool (`metadata.tool`, falling back to the single entry in `patterns`) is `aidevops_bounded_operation`, and `isDesignedPoll(tool, metadata.input)` holds, which means `action` is `status` or `output`. Reuse `isDesignedPoll` from `session-continuation-loops.mjs` and do not copy the regex.
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`: in `handlePermissionEvent` reply `once`, and in `handlePermissionAsk` set `output.status = "allow"`, for a designed-poll doom loop. Do this before the impossible-read and capture paths, and record one non-blocking `permission_designed_poll_allowed` event, the way `recordReadOnlyRootAllow` does. Everything else is unchanged: `start`/`cancel` repeats, other tools' doom loops, and every non-`doom_loop` permission keep today's capture and reject.
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`: add one test. A status or output doom loop is allowed on both the event and hook paths, with no capture file. A `start` doom loop on the same tool, and a `bash` doom loop, are still captured as non-grantable and rejected.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-designed-poll.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs
- TODO.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a headless session, a `doom_loop` ask for `aidevops_bounded_operation` with `action` `status` or `output` is answered `once` on the event path and `allow` on the hook path, and writes no permission capture.
- [ ] A `doom_loop` ask for `aidevops_bounded_operation` with `action` `start` or `cancel`, or for any other tool, is still captured as non-grantable and rejected.
- [ ] Interactive (non-headless) behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs` passes.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`
- After deploy: `rg '"permission":"doom_loop"' ~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl | rg -c aidevops_bounded_operation` stops growing, and `permission_designed_poll_allowed` events appear instead.

</details>

title: harden path-anchored source reads
body:
## What

Harden how the source-access broker opens files so path resolution is anchored to held directory descriptors end to end.

## Why

Defence in depth for the privileged reader: the open should reach exactly the file that validation approved, and a privileged read should never exceed what the requesting user could already read.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/source_access_core.py`: open source paths one component at a time from `/` with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` relative to the held parent descriptor; compare the opened identity with the anchored leaf and the full path after reading; when running as root, require an authenticated non-root requester and a file owned by that user; bind proposal identity to the opened descriptor.
- Broker-owned state reads (`source-access-helper.py` bundle recovery) use a dedicated reader that resolves root-owned platform aliases (for example `/var/run` -> `/run`) and requires the broker trust owner.
- No approval flow, prompt, allowlist or receipt schema changes.

title: test: source-access bootstrap bytecode fixture fails under Apple Python 3.9 pycache prefix
body:
## What

`test_privileged_bootstrap_rejects_unsafe_core_and_ignores_bytecode` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py` errors under Apple's Command Line Tools Python 3.9 (`/usr/bin/python3`), on `origin/main` as well as on branches.

```
File ".agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py", line 1537, in test_privileged_bootstrap_rejects_unsafe_core_and_ignores_bytecode
    bytecode_path.parent.mkdir()
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '~/Library/Caches/com.apple.python/<temp-path>/broker'
```

Apple's Python sets `sys.pycache_prefix` to `~/Library/Caches/com.apple.python`, so `importlib.util.cache_from_source()` returns a path whose intermediate directories do not exist. The fixture calls `mkdir()` without `parents=True`. Homebrew Python (3.12+) passes, because it has no prefix.

## How

- File: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py` around line 1537.
- Create the bytecode parent with `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`, or compute the path with `sys.pycache_prefix` disabled (for example by patching `sys.pycache_prefix = None` for the fixture), so the test still proves bytecode is ignored.
- Test-only change. Leave the broker's bytecode rule as it is.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`

## Verification

`gh_create_pr` should skip `--label origin:*` when the label is absent upstream and cannot be provisioned, matching `gh_create_issue` (the provisioning check that issue creation uses, around `_ensure_origin_labels_for_args`).

title: Reusable Linux procfs runtime-evidence harness for worktree observer changes (from GH#39034)
body:
## Description

Publishing GH#39034 (PR #39055) required `--testing-level runtime-verified` evidence for a Linux procfs change made on a macOS host. No reusable harness existed, so a one-off Python script was written and run in a local Docker image: as root it forked a root parent renamed `sshd` whose child drops to UID 1000 without exec (the kernel clears dumpability), plus a UID 1000 non-dumpable `gpg-agent`. It then ran `worktree_process_proc.py denied` and `cwdmap /proc` as UID 1000, against both the base and the branch scripts.

That base-vs-branch comparison was the evidence the critical-runtime-risk gate accepted. Future changes to `worktree_process_proc.py`, `worktree_process_attestation.py` or the lease census will need the same thing, and each session currently has to rebuild it.

## Proposed capability

A helper, for example `.agents/scripts/linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh`, that:

1. Runs a stock image such as `debian:stable-slim` or `ubuntu:24.04` with python3, using `docker run --rm` and mounting a scripts directory read-only.
2. Sets up named process fixtures: a privsep child (root parent, setuid child with no exec), an unattested non-dumpable same-UID process, and optionally a re-parented forged chain.
3. Runs the observer modes (`denied`, `paths`, `cwdmap /proc`) as an unprivileged UID and prints a stable, diffable report.
4. Takes `--base <dir>` and `--head <dir>` and prints a diff, so its output can be pasted into the `--testing` field.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh`, plus a fixture script next to it.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md` (add a "Runtime verification on non-Linux hosts" pointer).
- Reference pattern: the observer/attestation modules `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_proc.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_attestation.py`.

title: fix(setup): accept a native OpenCode executable at its own ~/.local/bin launcher path
body:
## What

`_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` cannot record a valid native OpenCode executable that already sits at its own launcher path (`~/.local/bin/opencode`, or `~/.local/bin/opencode2` for the isolated profile). Setup should keep a validated native executable at that path (or move it to a distinct backing path first) instead of failing the stage.

## Why

Found while triaging CodeRabbit on PR #39039 (GH#38922). When the resolved binary equals the shim path and has no managed-shim target, the function falls back to `_setup_find_valid_opencode_binary`, which skips the shim path as a candidate (`[[ "$candidate" == "$shim_path" ]] && continue`). With no other install on PATH, it returns 1, "OpenCode stable shim verification failed" is printed, and no receipt is written. The file is never modified, so nothing is damaged; the stage fails.

The limitation predates #39039: V1 uses the same binary name (`opencode`) and the same shim path, so a native V1 executable at `~/.local/bin/opencode` hits it too. #39039 adds the global-V2 path (`AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_GLOBAL_V2=1`), which inherits it.

## Reproducer

Confirmed by code path on `main` (and on PR #39039 head `991b7f900d`); not yet run as a sandbox case:

1. Sandbox `HOME`; place an executable at `$HOME/.local/bin/opencode` that prints `1.18.29` for `--version` and `opencode run [message]` for `--help` (pattern: the `SHIM` heredocs in `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`). Ensure no other `opencode` is on PATH.
2. Source the setup modules as `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` does and run `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1 setup_opencode_cli`.
3. Expected: the executable is recorded. Actual (by code): `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` → `resolved_bin == shim_path`, no managed target → `_setup_find_valid_opencode_binary` skips the shim path → return 1 → "OpenCode stable shim verification failed".

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`

1. In `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` (`rg -n "^_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim" .agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`), handle the branch where `resolved_bin` is the shim path, has no managed target (`_setup_opencode_managed_shim_target` is empty), and passes `_setup_validate_opencode_binary`. Preferred: move the native executable to a framework-owned backing path (e.g. under `~/.aidevops/`) atomically, then write the managed launcher pointing at it. Alternative: record the native executable as-is and skip the launcher write. Pick one and record the trade-off in the PR (moving keeps the launcher contract; keeping avoids touching a user-owned file).
2. Keep current behaviour for managed launchers and for executables outside `~/.local/bin`.
3. Never delete or overwrite a native executable before the replacement launcher validates (the existing temp-shim/`mv -f` pattern).

## Acceptance

- In the sandbox of `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`, a fake native executable at `$HOME/.local/bin/opencode` that prints `opencode v2.3.0`, with no other `opencode` on PATH: `setup_opencode_runtimes` exits 0, `.opencode-bin-resolved` names a path that runs that executable, and `--version` still prints `opencode v2.3.0`.
- The same case for a V1 native executable (`1.18.29`) under `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1`.
- Existing cases in `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` and `test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh` still pass; ShellCheck clean.

## Context

- Source: review comment on PR #39039 by @coderabbitai (`tool-install.sh` around `_setup_opencode_global_v2_cli`).
- `setup.sh` runs under `set -Eeuo pipefail` and calls `_time_step "$SETUP_STAGE_OPENCODE" setup_opencode_runtimes` unguarded, so a failure here aborts the rest of non-interactive setup. That makes this worth fixing, although it is rare (most installs live in npm/bun/Homebrew/`~/.opencode/bin`).

title: pre-merge-gate omits the approval command when the NMR hold reports as the maintainer-gate status
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 38953 marcusquinn/aidevops`, for an external fork PR whose only failing required check is the live `needs-maintainer-review` hold, prints:

    [ERROR] PR #38953 has terminal required-check failures at the current head

It prints no approval command. `gh pr checks 38953 --required` shows that the failing check is named `maintainer-gate` (commit-status context); every other required check passes.

`workflows/review.md` "External PR authority preflight" requires the preflight to print the mixed `sudo aidevops approve batch issue:N pr:N... OWNER/REPO` command, and forbids composing it by hand. So an external PR with a repaired head cannot get its approval command.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 38953 marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Actual output:**

    [ERROR] PR #38953 has terminal required-check failures at the current head

Steps:

1. Pick an external fork PR that has passing CI and a live `needs-maintainer-review` label (here #38953 at head `24c226d036`).
2. Run `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate <PR> <owner/repo>`.
3. It prints only the terminal-failure error line and no approval command.

Predicate check: `printf '%s' '[{"name":"maintainer-gate"}]' | jq 'all(.[]; .name == "gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate")'` returns `false`.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` `cmd_pre_merge_gate` (around line 602-607) runs `_full_loop_report_external_authority_preflight` only when every terminal failure is named exactly `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`. The gate publishes two names: the workflow CheckRun `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and the stable commit-status context `maintainer-gate` (`.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml:132-144`). Branch protection requires `maintainer-gate`, so that name is what the required-check query returns.

`pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:25-27` already treats the family as `maintainer-gate`, `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`.

## Fix

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`: accept any member of that three-name family in the authority-only diagnostic. A mix of family members still qualifies; any non-family failure still prints no command. This is diagnostic only and never turns a failure into readiness.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` `test_pre_merge_authority_check_failure`: assert that the command is printed for `maintainer-gate` and for the legacy display name, and that it is still withheld for a family member mixed with `lint`.

## Verification

    bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh
    shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh

Live: `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 38953 marcusquinn/aidevops` prints the batch approval command.

title: test-team-interface-buzz-adapter fails intermittently inside full-loop validators under host load; validator hides the assertion
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` for GH#38959 failed its Node validator twice. The failing run was `npm run test` in `.agents/scripts`, and the failing file both times was `tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs` (2.4-2.7 s; 100 passed, 1 failed). The branch does not touch team-interface code.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 38959 ...` (Node validator stage) on a host with load average about 100 on 16 cores.

**Actual output:**

    [ERROR] [validators] CHECK FAILED (exit 1): npm run test (.agents/scripts)
    ℹ tests 103 / pass 100 / fail 1 / skipped 2
    ✖ tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs (2695.387625ms)
      'test failed'

The failure is intermittent and load-dependent. It did not reproduce in six controlled runs on the same branch:

- the file alone;
- `node --test tests/*.mjs`;
- `npm run test`;
- the plugin and scripts suites concurrently, then sequentially;
- under GNU `timeout`;
- the validator's own `_run_scoped_node_checks`, sourced from `full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`.

The host load average was about 100 on 16 cores when the failures occurred. A third `commit-and-pr` on the unchanged commit passed, and created PR #39066.

The validator keeps only `tail -20` of `command-N.log` (`full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh:285-286`) and deletes the snapshot directory afterwards, so the failing assertion text was lost.

## Likely cause

Two wall-clock budgets in the test:

- `invokeAdapterRead(..., {timeoutMs: 1000})` at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs:366`, around child `plutil` and `sqlite3` reads;
- `{timeoutMs: 20}` at `:639`, which must abort before the child read completes.

Under heavy load, the 1000 ms budget can expire before the reads finish. Unverified: confirm with the captured assertion first.

## Fix

1. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`: on `CHECK FAILED`, print the `not ok` blocks with their diagnostics (or keep the log path) instead of only `tail -20`, so the next failure is diagnosable.
2. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs:366`: if the captured assertion is `adapter_timeout`, raise the success-path budget (for example 10000 ms). The success path only needs a generous upper bound. Keep the 20 ms abort test as it is.

## Verification

    node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs

Then run the same test under load, for example alongside the plugin suite at low concurrency: no failures over five runs. A deliberately failing assertion must show its message in the validator output.

title: t19114: fix(checkpoints): resume a continuation review worktree that is only ahead of...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19114` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(checkpoints): resume a continuation review worktree that is only ahead of the PR head with unpushed commits

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A stale-draft continuation worker that commits locally but exits before its single final push leaves the review worktree one or more commits **ahead** of the verified PR head. The next continuation dispatch treats that worktree as diverged and refuses to launch (`existing_review_worktree_diverged`, `retry_class=retryable_infrastructure`). The refusal repeats after every short cooldown, so the draft never moves and the linked issue stays blocked by its draft checkpoint. Every pulse round still spends a full dispatch ceremony on that issue before the draft-checkpoint block fires.

The continuation prompt already expects this case. `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` tells the worker to save a recovery bundle after each commit and "on resume keep and verify unpushed local commits, never reset them away". But `_prrts_reconcile_existing_worktree_head` in `pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh` only accepts a worktree that is behind the PR head (fast-forward). A worktree that contains the PR head plus unpushed commits fails the `merge-base --is-ancestor "$actual_head" "$head_oid"` check and is rejected as diverged.

Evidence from one runner on 2026-11-18:

- A draft PR in a private managed repository: the continuation worker launched at 18:58Z, committed one commit on top of the verified PR head at 19:25Z, and exited at 19:39Z with no push and no terminal-state command. Since 20:07Z every attempt logs `skipped — existing review worktree cannot fast-forward to verified PR head`. `git log` in the worktree shows exactly one commit ahead of the PR head, which is not diverged. An earlier draft in the same repository was in the same one-commit-ahead state and needed an interactive session to finish and merge it.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log`: 833 `outcome=existing_review_worktree_diverged` outcomes in total, and 11 refusals across 6 PRs from 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-18.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: the linked issue was re-attempted by the issue dispatcher at 371s, 40s and 70s of ceremony per attempt, each ending with `blocked:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`. Across the log, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` and `stale_draft_checkpoint` attempts used about 22 hours of dispatch ceremony time over 5.7 days.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`, `_prrts_reconcile_existing_worktree_head`: after the existing claim, dirty-state preservation, exact-head fetch and clean/branch re-check, add one case before the diverged refusal. When the dispatch is a checkpoint continuation (`_prrts_repair_linked_issue "$pr_number"` is non-empty) and `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$head_oid" "$actual_head"` holds, keep the worktree as it is, log how many unpushed commits are resumed, and return 0. The worker then starts with `AIDEVOPS_PR_REPAIR_HEAD_SHA` set to the verified remote head. Its exact-target fence and single fast-forward push still apply, and the prompt already says to keep the unpushed commits.
- Leave all other cases unchanged. A truly diverged worktree is still refused. Ordinary review-thread workers, whose prompt has no resume contract, are still refused. So are live or unverified owners and dirty state that cannot be preserved.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a checkpoint continuation whose clean, exclusively claimed worktree is ahead of the verified PR head, dispatch launches the worker in that worktree without resetting it, and the log names the resumed commit count.
- [ ] A worktree whose HEAD neither contains nor is contained by the verified head is still refused with `existing_review_worktree_diverged`.
- [ ] An ordinary review-thread dispatch (no linked issue) with an ahead worktree is still refused.
- [ ] The existing worktree tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` pass, and ShellCheck reports nothing on the edited file.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`
- After deploy: the next continuation for the affected draft logs the resume line rather than `cannot fast-forward`, and new `existing_review_worktree_diverged` outcomes in `~/.aidevops/logs/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log` are only true divergences.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: DataForSEO SERP calls: support resolve_poisoned_results and resolve_goto_urls (poisoned Google results, wrapped links)
body:
## Description

DataForSEO announced on 2026-11-16 that Google returns "poisoned" result pages to automated requests: legitimate organic listings are replaced with other results, which causes false ranking drops and wrong SERP analysis. They added `resolve_poisoned_results` to every Google Organic SERP task (Standard and Live, regular/advanced/HTML). It cross-checks organic results against Google's Web mode and replaces affected rows; replaced rows carry `from_web` in their `checks` array. It costs one extra SERP page on every task, whether or not poisoning is found ($0.002 → $0.004 for a live, normal-priority, depth-10 task).

Separately, since about 2026-11-03 Google often returns organic links as opaque `https://google.com/goto?url=<token>` wrappers with `domain: google.com`. DataForSEO's `resolve_goto_urls` returns the real address at no extra charge (adds up to 40 s; max turnaround 260 s).

The framework's DataForSEO SERP paths use neither option and the docs do not mention either problem:

- `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh` — `dataforseo_serp_organic` (lines 178-199 in 3.39.229) posts `serp/google/organic/live/regular` with `depth: 10` and no resolve flags. `serp_organic_normalized` (lines 353-357) then reads `.url` for each organic row, so `keyword-research-helper.sh serp-compare` can show `google.com/goto` wrappers for DataForSEO (they never match Serper/SerpAPI URLs) and can compare a poisoned DataForSEO page against the other providers.
- `.agents/seo/dataforseo.md` — the "SERP Results" example (lines 82-89) posts `live/advanced` without either flag and there is no note on poisoned pages, wrapped links, or the extra charge.

Observed downstream (a private project with two DataForSEO SERP tools, audited 2026-11-18): 77% of organic rows in 171 saved `live/advanced` captures were `google.com/goto` wrappers, and a rank tracker showed an exact-match brand query flipping between #1 and not ranked week to week while Google Search Console held average position 1.0-1.7. Adding both flags there was cost-neutral by dropping unused depth (20 → 10).

## Expected Behavior

1. `dataforseo_serp_organic` sends `"resolve_goto_urls": true`, so `serp-compare` gets real URLs from DataForSEO.
2. `dataforseo_serp_organic` sends `"resolve_poisoned_results": true` by default (it doubles the cost of the 10-result call), with a documented way to turn it off. Maintainer decision: default on, or opt-in flag.
3. Optionally, `serp_organic_normalized` adds `restored: true` for rows whose `checks` include `from_web`.
4. `seo/dataforseo.md` adds both flags to the SERP example and a short "Poisoned SERPs and wrapped links" section: what each flag does, the per-task charge, that `resolve_poisoned_results` cannot be combined with `udm=web`/`udm=14`, that only organic rows are replaced (PAA/AI Overview come from the original page), and a reminder that billing is per 10 results so callers should not request depth they do not read.

## Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh` — `dataforseo_serp_organic` heredoc (add the two keys); optional `from_web` mapping in `serp_organic_normalized`
- `EDIT: .agents/seo/dataforseo.md` — SERP example and new section
- Possibly `EDIT: .agents/seo/keyword-research.md:162` if the provider table should note the SERP options

`rg -n "serp/google/organic" .agents` found only these three references in 3.39.229.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh`
- One paid call (~$0.004): `keyword-research-helper.sh serp-compare "<keyword>" --provider dataforseo --json` returns no `google.com/goto` URL, and the raw response `tasks[0].data` echoes both flags.

## Sources

- DataForSEO update, 2026-11-16: https://dataforseo.com/update/detect-and-resolve-poisoned-google-results-with-dataforseo-serp-api
- Endpoint parameters (`resolve_goto_urls`, `resolve_poisoned_results`, `checks` values): https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced/

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.39.229
- **Latest version**: 3.39.229
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.3.9(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.103.3 (2026-10-26)

body:

`test-init-scope.sh` fails 2 of 47 cases on an unchanged `main`-based worktree (macOS, found while verifying GH#39023). Neither failure is caused by a product change.

Either the call shape changed or the end marker moved, so the extracted range no longer contains the call. Update the expectation to the current call. Read-only reference: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh`, `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh` (`resolve_canonical_repo_path`).

title: gh-checks-wait-helper keeps polling a PR already merged by native auto-merge, so the chained merge/release reconcile never runs
body:
## Description

`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --repo <slug> --all` keeps polling after the PR has been merged by GitHub native auto-merge. It stops only when its 1800s timeout expires.

Observed 2026-11-18 on protected release PR #39067 (v3.39.230):

- The release helper opened #39067 with native auto-merge enabled, using a merge commit.
- `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait 39067 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --all; full-loop-helper.sh merge 39067 ...` was started as the documented follow-up.
- GitHub auto-merged #39067 at 21:03:39Z. The waiter was still polling about 10 minutes later because the `--all` aggregate contexts (`Complexity Analysis`, `Framework Validation`) were still reported as non-terminal.
- The chained `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, which auto-reconciles the release lane after a merge, never ran. The lane stayed in `remote-publication` until `aidevops release reconcile 39055` was run by hand. Meanwhile another session saw `RELEASE_EXECUTOR dead` and nearly reconciled the same lane.

## Reproducer

1. Pick any PR that native auto-merge merged while at least one optional/aggregate check context was still non-terminal. #39067 is a real case: it merged at 21:03:39Z while `Complexity Analysis` and `Framework Validation` were still pending.
2. Run `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait 39067 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --all` while a context is still pending.
3. Observed: the helper keeps polling (on 2026-11-18, `ps` showed it at 29:41 elapsed, about 10 min after the merge) and does not exit until the 1800s timeout. With the documented chain `wait ...; full-loop-helper.sh merge N`, the merge/reconcile step is delayed until that timeout.

## Expected Behavior

When the PR is no longer open, the waiter stops polling:

- `MERGED`: print a terminal line such as `MERGED: PR #N merged at <time>; check wait not required` and exit 0. The chained `full-loop-helper.sh merge` then sees the merge and runs its post-merge release reconcile (that path already handles "PR already merged by native auto-merge").
- `CLOSED` (not merged): exit non-zero with a clear message.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`, in `wait_for_checks()` (the loop starts around line 832). Each pending poll, or at least each `max_interval` poll, should do one cheap state read (`gh pr view N --repo R --json state,mergedAt`, or reuse whatever `verified_head_sha` already fetches) and return before the timeout check.
- The test pattern to follow is the existing helper suite (`rg -l gh-checks-wait-helper .agents/scripts/tests/`). Add one case: a merged PR with a still-pending optional context returns 0 promptly.

## Verification

title: t19115: fix(checkpoints): a trusted terminal-blocker re-arm never releases a blocked ...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19115` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(checkpoints): a trusted terminal-blocker re-arm never releases a blocked worker draft, even for a maintainer retry

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A worker that releases an issue as `blocked` after opening a draft leaves the draft as a checkpoint. The draft then holds the issue until someone publishes a revision-bound `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line. Terminal-blocker recovery can later re-arm that issue, either for a maintainer retry directive (`trusted_retry`) or for a brief revision after the blocker (`revision_changed`). It posts its receipt and projects `status:available`. The checkpoint path ignores that re-arm. `_pcc_blocked_attention` posts or re-finds `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` and the draft stays held, even when the approval template validates (`refusal=none`).

The two opt-in policy routes in `_pcc_policy_route` do not cover this case either. `_pcc_resolve_decision` needs a `reason=decision` finding. `_pcc_unknown_pending_work` needs a `CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_TRIAGE pending_work` marker bound to the current brief, and a revised brief by definition no longer matches it. Without the policy, the unknown digest also needs that marker. So a re-armed blocked checkpoint has no route at all. A maintainer retry directive, the strongest human signal available, is silently ignored, and the issue looks healthy (`status:available`) while nothing can run.

Evidence from one runner on 2026-11-18:

- Census of open drafts held by blocked-checkpoint attention across pulse repos: 9 open. Of those, 4 already have a trusted re-arm receipt after the blocked release: 2 `trusted_retry`, 1 `revision_changed` and 1 `unevidenced_permission_window`. All 4 show `refusal=none` in the attention marker, and none has an approval. The other 5 have no re-arm.
- One worked example in a private managed repository: blocked release 14:30Z (`reason=unknown`). At 16:03Z the recovery supervisor repaired the brief and wrote "continue draft PR, do not restart; cause: environment, not brief". At 17:03Z a runner posted `terminal-blocker-rearmed` (`reason=revision_changed`). At 17:04Z it posted `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... refusal=none`. More than 50 hours later the draft is untouched and every pulse round spends a dispatch ceremony ending in `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: 35 distinct drafts reached `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS`, with zero `UNKNOWN_CHECKPOINT_APPROVED` outcomes.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh`: in `_pcc_policy_route`, call a new `_pcc_rearmed_checkpoint_route` after `_pcc_resolve_decision` and before `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`. A trusted re-arm is newer evidence than the release-time triage. The new route returns 0 only when an approval is published or already valid.
- NEW function `_pcc_rearmed_checkpoint_route` in the same file, modelled on `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`:
  1. Find the newest unedited comment, created after the blocked release `$release`, that contains both `<!-- aidevops:terminal-blocker-rearmed key=` and a `terminal-blocker-rearm-reason` line with `reason=trusted_retry` or `reason=revision_changed`. Exclude `unevidenced_permission_window` and `lifecycle_recovered`. Neither shows that the blocker was addressed.
  2. #aidevops:trust-boundary: the receipt poster, the publishing login and the checkpoint runner need current `admin|maintain|write` permission. For `trusted_retry`, also require an unedited OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive between the release and the receipt, posted by a login with write permission. For `revision_changed`, require the issue author to have write permission: only the author or a write collaborator can edit an issue body, so every revision is then trusted.
  3. Run the same gates as `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`: `_pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible`, then open/unassigned/`auto-dispatch`/no protective hold on the issue. Generate the template with `_pcc_approval_template` and check that its `head` and `brief_sha256` match the current head and brief.
  4. Reserve `refs/aidevops/checkpoint-rearm/<issue>/<receipt>` atomically: two runners publishing would leave an ambiguous approval. Then publish through `_pcc_publish_policy_approval` and print `REARMED_CHECKPOINT_APPROVED pr=… head=… release=… reason=… receipt=…`.
  5. On by default, matching the re-arm's own trust decision. A repo opts out with `checkpoint_policy.auto_continue_rearmed: false`. Do not touch `_pcc_unknown_digest`.
- EDIT `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: add a short "Re-armed blocked checkpoints" subsection covering the evidence, authority, gates and bounds.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh`, following the `test_unknown_pending_policy` pattern. Cover `trusted_retry` and trusted `revision_changed` publishing exactly once, and a lost reservation not republishing. None of these may publish: a receipt from a non-write poster, a non-write retry or issue author, a COLLABORATOR or edited retry, an older or edited receipt, permission-window and lifecycle reasons, an assigned or held issue, a moved head, or an opted-out repo.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh
- .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-unknown-digest.sh
- .agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A blocked worker draft whose issue has a newer, write-authorised `trusted_retry` re-arm receipt and a validating template gets exactly one `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line through `gh-write-helper.sh`, with or without checkpoint policy. The next dispatch round continues the exact head through `dispatch-approved`.
- [ ] A `revision_changed` re-arm publishes the same way when the issue author has write permission; with an outside author it never publishes.
- [ ] No approval is published for: a receipt, retry or brief from a login without write permission; a receipt older than the blocked release; `unevidenced_permission_window` or `lifecycle_recovered` reasons; an assigned or held issue; a template whose head or brief no longer matches; or a repo with `auto_continue_rearmed: false`.
- [ ] Existing checkpoint suites pass: `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh` and `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`. ShellCheck is clean on the edited files.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-unknown-digest.sh`
- After deploy: `rg -c 'REARMED_CHECKPOINT_APPROVED' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` grows. The two `trusted_retry` drafts from the census get approvals and continuation launches within one pulse round.

</details>

title: keyword-research: detect_weaknesses reads wrong JSON path, always reports 0 for DataForSEO SERP data
body:
## What

`detect_weaknesses` in `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh:40-70` always reports 0 weaknesses for DataForSEO SERP data. Extended keyword research (the weakness and score columns) is therefore silently wrong.

## Why

The caller at `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh:582-586` passes the raw `dataforseo_serp_organic` response, shaped `{"tasks":[{"result":[{"items":[...]}]}]}`. `detect_weaknesses` reads top-level `.items[]?`, which matches nothing, so every count falls back to 0. Two more problems on the same path:

- `domain_score`/`page_score` (`:594-596`) read `items[0]`, which may be a non-organic item (featured snippet, PAA) rather than the top organic result.
- `main_domain_rank` and `backlinks_count` may not exist on `serp/google/organic/live/regular` items at all. Confirm the field names in the current DataForSEO docs (on `advanced`, rank data may sit under `rank_info`).

Found while reviewing #39070, which changes the same request builder. This defect exists independently of that change.

## How

1. In `detect_weaknesses`, select organic rows from the envelope: `.tasks[0].result[0].items[]? | select(.type == "organic")`. This is the same selection `serp_organic_normalized` uses in `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh:355`.
2. In the score lookups at `:594-596`, use the first organic row instead of `items[0]`.
3. Check every field read (`main_domain_rank`, `backlinks_count`, `page_rank`) against the current DataForSEO SERP response. Map each to the correct field, or remove the checks whose data `live/regular` does not return. Do not invent fields.

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh` — `detect_weaknesses` (`:40-90`) and the extended-research score lookups (`:582-606`)

## Reproducer

Offline, no API call. A minimal DataForSEO envelope with one non-HTTPS organic row:

```bash
printf '%s' '{"tasks":[{"result":[{"items":[{"type":"organic","url":"http://example.com/","rank_group":1}]}]}]}' \
  | jq -c '{current_path: ([.items[]? | select(.url | startswith("http://"))] | length),
            envelope_path: ([.tasks[0].result[0].items[]? | select(.type=="organic") | select(.url | startswith("http://"))] | length)}'
# => {"current_path":0,"envelope_path":1}
```

`current_path` is the selector `detect_weaknesses` uses at `:67`. It misses the row.

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh`
- Offline: pipe a saved DataForSEO `live/regular` response (or a minimal hand-built envelope with one `organic` item that has `url` starting `http://`) into `detect_weaknesses` and confirm a non-zero count.
- Optional paid check (cost per keyword, see #39070): run extended research for one keyword with DataForSEO and confirm the weakness column is populated.

title: pulse-merge defers forever to a stale native auto-merge request on a CLEAN, all-green PR
body:
## Observed

When a PR's GitHub native auto-merge request was enabled while the PR was `BLOCKED`, GitHub may never fire it after the blocker clears. Clearing a blocker by changing a branch ruleset does not raise a check or push event. The deterministic merge pass then defers to GitHub on every cycle, indefinitely.

Evidence from one managed repo (private, so no name here):
- Auto-merge was enabled on 2026-11-15T16:40Z while a ruleset required a stale check name, so the PR was `BLOCKED`.
- An admin fixed the ruleset. For about 3 days after that, the PR read `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` with every required check `SUCCESS`, and it stayed unmerged.
- Each cycle `pulse.log` logged `worker-briefed auto-merge ... passed all gates`, then `auto_merge already set, deferring to GitHub (t3070)`.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge N SLUG --squash` merged it on the first try.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` around line 1817-1843: when auto-merge is already set and all required checks pass (`pending_count == 0`), the function always logs the t3070 deferral and returns 0. Nothing checks for a request that is older than a threshold while the PR is `CLEAN`.

## Fix

In that branch, when `pending_count == 0`, `mergeStateStatus == CLEAN`, and `autoMergeRequest.enabledAt` is older than a threshold, do not defer. Two options:
- fall through to the normal guarded merge path, the same call `full-loop-helper.sh merge` makes;
- or disable and re-enable auto-merge once per head SHA, to re-trigger GitHub.

The threshold could reuse `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_AUTO_MERGE_STUCK_SECONDS` or a sibling knob (for example 30 min). All existing gates still apply.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` (the auto-merge-set branch near the t3070 log line)
- tests beside the existing t3070/t3567 merge-process tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/`

## Verification

A fixture PR has `autoMergeRequest.enabledAt` older than the threshold, all required checks `SUCCESS` and `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. The pass must attempt the merge instead of logging `deferring to GitHub (t3070)`. With checks pending it must keep the existing t3567 behaviour.

title: issue-triage-gate caller template pins the reusable workflow to @main, failing hash-pin security gates
body:
## Observed

`.agents/templates/workflows/issue-triage-gate-caller.yml` calls the reusable workflow at `@main` and passes `aidevops_ref: main`. A repo whose security gate enforces hash-pinned actions fails every PR as soon as `aidevops sync-workflows --workflow issue-triage-gate --install-missing` installs the caller. The gate in question is zizmor `unpinned-uses` (blanket policy), which reports HIGH.

Evidence from managed repos: the caller was installed in six repos of one org on the same day. On the first PR after that, the repo's scan gated on exactly one finding:

    [zizmor] HIGH zizmor/unpinned-uses unpinned action reference: action is not pinned to a hash (required by blanket policy) (.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml:13)

The PR itself changed only a docs page. Worker tokens cannot push `.github/**`, so an automated fix cannot clear the gate; a person has to hand-edit six repos.

## Fix

Let the managed caller be pinned to a commit:
- `sync-workflows` (and `check-workflows`) accept a pin mode, or detect a repo hash-pin policy, and render `uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate-reusable.yml@<40-hex-sha> # main` with `aidevops_ref: <same sha>`. The template comment already requires the two refs to match.
- `check-workflows` treats a SHA-pinned caller as current, not as drift, and can report how far behind the pinned SHA is, so pinning does not cause churn.

## Files

- `.agents/templates/workflows/issue-triage-gate-caller.yml`
- the sync/check-workflows implementation that renders managed callers (path unknown from here; find it with `rg -n "issue-triage-gate" .agents/scripts`)
- the same change likely applies to the other managed caller templates in `.agents/templates/workflows/`

## Verification

Render the caller in pin mode. Running `zizmor` (or `actionlint` plus a hash-pin check) on the output reports no `unpinned-uses`. `check-workflows` reports the pinned caller as in sync.

title: t19116: perf(pulse): reserve a dispatch slot at the claim, not at ceremony start, so rejection checks run in parallel
body:
## Task


perf(pulse): reserve a dispatch slot at the claim, not at ceremony start, so rejection checks run in parallel

`_dispatch_max_loop` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`) reserves a worker slot for every in-flight ceremony: `while ((successes_so_far + ${#_pids[@]} >= effective_slots))`. `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase` also clamp ceremony concurrency to the slot budget, and a 1-slot phase falls back to the serial `_dispatch_floor_loop`. A ceremony holds that reservation for its whole run, but most candidates are rejected by read-only dedup layers well before the first persistent write (the layer-7 claim in `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`). When few slots are free, which is the steady state on a busy runner, rejections are evaluated one at a time. Free slots stay idle while 80-110 candidates wait.

Evidence from one runner, 2026-11-17 00:00Z to 2026-11-18 22:30Z (`~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`, `pulse.log`, `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`):

- Worker occupancy averaged about 6-7 concurrent workers against `simultaneous_target_final=20`. 22% of the last 600 `Dispatch_capacity` samples had `active_workers=0`, and the median was about 6.
- Each round had plenty of candidates: `Dispatch_max: available=10..20, candidates=86..116`. Over the last 30 rounds, 743 candidates were processed and 203 dispatched (27% yield).
- `dedup.ceremony_total` averaged 233.6s (n=967). Rejected candidates spent 10-180s in `dedup.dedup_check` first.
- One 80-minute cycle (`20261118T183602Z-76726`) ran from about +3200s to +4900s in strict sequence. Each next candidate started when the previous one ended (for example, busy 34s then gap 38s, busy 33s then 28s, busy 38s then 32s). 37 candidates went through serially and 9 launched.
- REST-core serial mode is not the cause: 1 of the last 45 rounds ran `mode=serial`, and REST headroom was 3,567/5,000.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

perf(pulse): reserve a dispatch slot at the claim, not at ceremony start, so rejection checks run in parallel

`_dispatch_max_loop` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`) reserves a worker slot for every in-flight ceremony: `while ((successes_so_far + ${#_pids[@]} >= effective_slots))`. `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase` also clamp ceremony concurrency to the slot budget, and a 1-slot phase falls back to the serial `_dispatch_floor_loop`. A ceremony holds that reservation for its whole run, but most candidates are rejected by read-only dedup layers well before the first persistent write (the layer-7 claim in `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`). When few slots are free, which is the steady state on a busy runner, rejections are evaluated one at a time. Free slots stay idle while 80-110 candidates wait.

Evidence from one runner, 2026-11-17 00:00Z to 2026-11-18 22:30Z (`~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`, `pulse.log`, `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`):

- Worker occupancy averaged about 6-7 concurrent workers against `simultaneous_target_final=20`. 22% of the last 600 `Dispatch_capacity` samples had `active_workers=0`, and the median was about 6.
- Each round had plenty of candidates: `Dispatch_max: available=10..20, candidates=86..116`. Over the last 30 rounds, 743 candidates were processed and 203 dispatched (27% yield).
- `dedup.ceremony_total` averaged 233.6s (n=967). Rejected candidates spent 10-180s in `dedup.dedup_check` first.
- One 80-minute cycle (`20261118T183602Z-76726`) ran from about +3200s to +4900s in strict sequence. Each next candidate started when the previous one ended (for example, busy 34s then gap 38s, busy 33s then 28s, busy 38s then 32s). 37 candidates went through serially and 9 launched.
- REST-core serial mode is not the cause: 1 of the last 45 rounds ran `mode=serial`, and REST headroom was 3,567/5,000.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`:
  1. Add a launch-slot semaphore. `_dispatch_max_loop` creates a private directory holding `budget=effective_slots`. `_dispatch_launch_slot_acquire <issue> <repo>` takes `slot.N` atomically with `mkdir` and records `held.<key>`. `_dispatch_launch_slot_settle <issue> <repo> <rc>` keeps the slot on success, keeps it on 124 (worker state unknown after the per-candidate timeout kill) and releases it otherwise. `_dispatch_launch_slots_free` returns budget minus taken slots. Without a slot directory, as in the serial loop and direct callers, acquire returns success and nothing changes.
  2. In `_dispatch_max_loop`, when the gate is active, replace the reservation loop condition with "no launch slot free". Stop the round when none is free and nothing is in flight. `_dispatch_max_spawn_candidate` settles the slot after `_dispatch_process_candidate` returns.
  3. Add `_dispatch_eval_parallel_cap <slots>`, which returns `slots × DISPATCH_EVAL_OVERSUBSCRIBE` (default 3). Use it instead of the bare slot clamp in `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase`. `DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL` (default 6), the throttle file, a forced floor and REST-core serial mode keep their existing caps.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: in `_dispatch_launch_worker`, acquire a slot immediately before `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`. With no slot, return `_DISPATCH_CYCLE_BUDGET_DEFER_RC` (75). That rc already flows through `dispatch_with_dedup` and `_dispatch_with_timeout` to `_dispatch_record_and_cache_block`. That function clears the attempt-recency stamp and records a defer, with no claim, no fast-fail and no negative cache.
- Opt-out: `DISPATCH_LAUNCH_SLOT_GATE=0` restores the ceremony-start reservation and the slot clamp exactly.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` with one focused case: a 1-slot budget whose candidates all pass evaluation launches exactly one worker, and the rest defer with rc 75. Also check that a failed holder releases its slot to a later candidate.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh

## Acceptance

- Launches in a round never exceed `effective_slots`. The slot is the only claim-time reservation.
- A 1-slot or 2-slot round evaluates candidates concurrently (up to `min(DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL, slots × DISPATCH_EVAL_OVERSUBSCRIBE)`), not serially.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` and the dispatch suites that source `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` pass, and ShellCheck is clean.
- After deployment, `Dispatch path=max: loop body finished ... mode=parallel(N)` shows N above the free-slot count in low-slot rounds, and hourly worker occupancy rises.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`; `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`; then `rg 'loop body finished' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail` and the occupancy census over a 12-hour window.

title: feat(diagnostics): reusable load-reproduction helper for flaky tests
body:
## Observed

Diagnosing GH#39068 (an intermittent `tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs` failure in the full-loop Node validator) needed an ad-hoc load-reproduction harness. The failure did not reproduce in six controlled single runs. It reproduced only when 40 copies ran concurrently:

    seq 1 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} sh -c 'node tests/<file>.mjs > "$out/run-{}.log" 2>&1 || echo FAIL {}'

followed by manual `grep` across the per-run logs to pull out the failing assertion.

- Before the fix: 5 of 40 runs failed (assertion `runtime timeout must abort the adapter child read`).
- After the first fix: a second race appeared (`adapter_timeout`, 4 of 120 runs).
- After both fixes: 120 of 120 passed at load average 58-75.

PR #39076 shows the full sequence. Each round needed a hand-written shell loop and manual log triage, and the next flaky-test diagnosis will need the same thing.

## Proposed capability

A small helper, for example `.agents/scripts/test-load-repro-helper.sh run --runs N --concurrency P [--rounds R] -- <test command...>`, that:

1. Runs the command N times at concurrency P (optionally for R rounds), with each run's output in its own log under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}/test-load-repro/<timestamp>/`.
2. Records the host load average before and after each round.
3. Prints a summary: pass/fail counts per round, then failures grouped by their first error headline (reuse the failure-record pattern from `_validator_print_failure_log` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`), with one example log path per group.
4. Exits 0 only when every run passed.

Reference patterns: `_validator_print_failure_log` (failure-record extraction and pipefail-safe capping) and the existing `*-helper.sh` command/usage conventions in `.agents/scripts/`.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/test-load-repro-helper.sh`
- Docs pointer: `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md` (the flaky-findings item near line 122). Add one short line pointing to the helper.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/test-load-repro-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/test-load-repro-helper.sh` passes with zero violations, and the script parses under Bash 3.2.
- A deliberately flaky probe, for example a Node script that fails when `Math.random() < 0.2`, run with `--runs 20 --concurrency 10`, reports a non-zero failure count grouped under the probe's assertion message and exits non-zero.
- An always-passing command reports 20/20 and exits 0.

title: source_access_blocked releases are labelled needs-credentials and routed to 'aidevops secret set', contradicting the worker contract
body:
## Problem

`source_access_blocked` releases are labelled `needs-credentials`, and the release text routes the maintainer to "provision on a runner with `aidevops secret set NAME`". The worker contract says this class must never mean missing credentials. Maintainers therefore get the wrong fix, and the `/decisions` credentials queue fills with items no secret can resolve.

Workers also use the class for questions that one named person can answer, such as "has this programme retired?". Those should be `input_required` with a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION`.

## Evidence (one managed project repo, 2026-11-18)

- `scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:654`: `source_access_blocked | credentials | missing_secret)` maps to `$BLOCKED_NEEDS_CREDENTIALS`.
- `scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:173-182`: `source_access_blocked` covers external refusals (HTTP 403, bot challenge, DNS, TLS or origin failure, removed page), and "Never use it for missing local credentials or runner-local account failures".
- 10 open issues in that repo carry `needs-credentials` from a `source_access_blocked` release (same blocker fingerprint across different runners and hosts). None needs a secret:
  - Cloudflare 525 origin TLS failure: 2 issues. This is a host outage and fits a time-based revisit.
  - HTTP 403 anti-bot or paywall: 3 issues. These need a permitted capture or an alternative source.
  - Programme identity question: 1 issue. The official URL redirects to the organiser's working awards index, and the worker's dossier reopen condition was "a maintainer confirms the programme's current official site, or confirms it has been retired". One maintainer comment answered it.
  - Official root loads (HTTP 200) and the denial was on another page: 3 issues.
  - No official URL in the brief: 1 issue.

## Proposed fix

1. `scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh`: route `source_access_blocked` to its own hold label (for example `needs-source-access`, with colour and description in `scripts/label-sync-helper.sh`), or to an existing non-credentials hold. Give it release text such as "Needed: a permitted capture, an alternative official source, or the host recovering. Owner: access owner." Keep `credentials | missing_secret` on `needs-credentials`.
2. Update every consumer of the hold-label set: `scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (lines ~108 and ~1302), `scripts/maintainer-decisions-helper.sh` (`MD_HOLD_LABELS`), `scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:108`, `scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1586`, `scripts/issue-sync-helper-labels.sh:223`, `scripts/backfill-status-available.sh:55`, `scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh:147-155`. Existing labelled issues need a one-time migration, or must keep working under the old label.
3. `scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh` (around line 176): when the reopen condition is a question one named person can answer, such as programme identity, retirement or the canonical site after a redirect to a working page, emit `input_required` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER` and `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION`, not `source_access_blocked`. A redirect to a working page is not an access refusal.
4. Consider letting `terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh` revisit host-outage source blocks (5xx/525/DNS) on its normal backoff. Line 160 of `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` currently says source-access holds are never revisited, so a host that comes back stays blocked until someone notices.

## Verification

- `scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-claim-release-retry.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` pass, with cases added for the new mapping.
- A synthetic `source_access_blocked` release produces the new label and release text. A `missing_secret` release still produces `needs-credentials`.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed scripts.

title: Model availability probe reports no-key on OpenCode 2 (no auth.json), blocking all Pulse dispatch
body:
## Summary

On OpenCode 2.x, `model-availability-helper.sh` reports every provider as `no-key`, so Pulse can never dispatch a worker: `resolve standard` / `resolve thinking` fail with "No available model for tier ... (configured candidates and extended chain exhausted)".

## Evidence

- aidevops v3.39.225 (also checked `model-availability-helper.sh` at tag v3.39.232: same code path), OpenCode v2.3.0, macOS.
- `opencode auth list` shows `Anthropic  OAuth  stored`.
- `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` does not exist on this install; OpenCode 2 keeps credentials in its own store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`).
- `~/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json` has 1 healthy Anthropic account (`model-accounts-pool status`: available 1, auth errors 0, token endpoint OK).
- `model-availability-helper.sh probe anthropic --force` → `anthropic: no API key configured`; `status` → anthropic/openai/opencode-go all `no-key`.
- Pulse log every cycle: `dispatch_triage_reviews: thinking and standard model resolution failed`; `Dispatch_capacity: ... provider=unknown provider_accounts_total=0`.

## Root cause

`resolve_api_key` Source 4 (`model-availability-helper.sh` ~L387-420) only reads `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`. OpenCode 2 no longer writes that file, and the OAuth pool (`oauth-pool.json`) is only used as a cooldown/auth-error *blocker* (`_probe_oauth_pool_cooldown_gate`), never as a positive credential source.

## Suggested fix

Treat a provider as `oauth-refresh-available` (healthy, skip HTTP probe) when either:
1. `opencode auth list` (or the OpenCode 2 credential store) reports an OAuth credential for the provider, or
2. `oauth-pool.json` has at least one non-errored, non-cooling account for the provider.

Do not recommend writing a token-less `auth.json` as a workaround: OpenCode 2 may import a legacy `auth.json` and overwrite the stored credential.

## Verification

- `model-availability-helper.sh probe anthropic --force` → healthy via OAuth.
- `model-availability-helper.sh resolve standard` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-*`.
- Next pulse cycle shows a non-empty provider in `Dispatch_capacity` and dispatches an `auto-dispatch` issue.

**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh`. Add a `nginx-http2` case next to `"health" | "fleet-health")`, reusing `health_check`'s server lookup (`jq .servers.<name>.ip/ssh_port` from `$CONFIG_FILE`) and its `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` pattern.
- The remote side is a small embedded script installed to `/usr/local/sbin/aidevops-nginx-http2` and run by `/etc/cron.d/aidevops-nginx-http2` (every 2 min). The `apply` mode:
  - edits only when `http2\s+on\s*;` or `listen[^;]*\shttp2` is present;
  - backs up the real directory (0600, keeping 10);
  - appends legacy-listen files to `/var/lib/aidevops-nginx-http2/legacy-listen-files.txt`;
  - runs `nginx -t`, restoring the backup if it fails, otherwise reloads;
  - logs via `logger -t aidevops-nginx-http2`.
- `status` prints KEY=VALUE: `h2_on_files`, `h2_off_files`, `legacy_listen_recorded`, `cron`, `sctp_blocked`, `sctp_loaded`, and `running_new_binary` (`/proc/<nginx master>/exe` not `(deleted)`).
- The `on` (revert) mode:
  - removes the cron;
  - turns `http2 off;` back into `http2 on;`;
  - restores the `http2` parameter after `ssl` on `listen ... 443 ssl` lines of recorded files only (yielding `listen ... 443 ssl http2`);
  - runs `nginx -t` (rollback on failure), then `systemctl restart nginx`.
- `--patched-marker CVE-ID` (optional): `apply` becomes a no-op once `zgrep -q <CVE> /usr/share/doc/nginx-common/changelog.Debian.gz` matches, and `on` refuses until it matches unless `--force`.
- Reference implementation (private, working, ShellCheck-clean): the session's host script had `apply|status|revert` modes with exactly the above logic. Re-derive from this brief; do not copy host-specific paths.
- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`. In "nginx security releases" (added by t19117), point the mitigation bullets at the new subcommand, and add it to the Quick Reference `Commands` list.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh`
- `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add a reusable `cloudron-helper.sh nginx-http2 <off|on|status> <server>` subcommand that turns HTTP/2 off on a Cloudron host's managed nginx during an HTTP/2 CVE window, keeps it off when Cloudron regenerates configs, reports state, and restores HTTP/2 exactly afterwards. Optionally `--sctp-block` / `--sctp-unblock` for the SCTP escalation step.

## Why

During the nginx2root response (advisory `nginx2root-2026-11`, t19117 / GH#39093) the interim mitigation had to be invented by hand per host. Observed traps that a one-line `sed` gets wrong, all on Cloudron 10.1.6 / Ubuntu 26.04:

- Vhosts in `/etc/nginx/applications/<app-id>/*.conf` use both `http2 on;` and the legacy `listen 443 ssl http2;`. The legacy form enables HTTP/2 for the whole address:port.
- Cloudron rewrote 1–2 vhosts per host about 2 minutes after a reboot, so a one-off edit reverts silently. A guarded re-apply from `/etc/cron.d` every 2 minutes was needed.
- `/etc/nginx` is a symlink into Cloudron's `platformdata/nginx`. `tar -C / etc/nginx` archives only the link, so the backup must target `readlink -f /etc/nginx`.
- An exact revert needs a record of which files used the legacy listen form. `box` regeneration after reboot does not rewrite every vhost.
- The `turn` container (coturn) holds kernel SCTP sockets, so SCTP blocking needs a modprobe.d entry plus a reboot.

Next nginx/HTTP/2 CVE, users should run one command instead of rebuilding this.

## Acceptance

- `cloudron-helper.sh nginx-http2 status <server>` prints the KEY=VALUE state, read-only.
- `off` leaves zero files matching either HTTP/2 form, installs the cron, and `nginx -t` passes. External `curl -sI --http2 --resolve <fqdn>:443:<ip> https://<fqdn>/` shows `HTTP/1.1`.
- `on` restores both forms byte-identically for recorded files (diff against the pre-`off` backup shows no `listen`/`http2` differences) and removes the cron.
- ShellCheck zero violations; every function has explicit `return`; `local var="$1"` style.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh`
- Run `status` against a test Cloudron server, or run the embedded remote script against a scratch copy of `applications/*.conf` (both forms). Confirm `off` → `on` round-trips byte-identically.
- `npx --no-install markdownlint-cli2 .agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-briefed-trust-parity.sh` exits non-zero on `main` without printing a `FAIL` line. The last output is `PASS missing/malformed PR metadata fails closed` (line ~219). title: setup.sh aborts at update_codex_config on macOS stock Python 3.9 (no tomli), skipping scheduler install
body:
## What happens

On macOS with the stock `/usr/bin/python3` (3.9.6, no `tomli`), `./setup.sh --non-interactive` exits 1 at the `update_codex_config` stage:

```
Codex MCP migration requires Python 3.11+ or tomli; config unchanged
[INFO] Finished setup stage: update_codex_config (0.05s, exit=1)
[ERROR] ./setup.sh:1723 exit 1
```

Every later stage is skipped, including the scheduler stage. On this install that left `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper` (the daily quality sweep) uninstalled with no further warning, even though the supervisor pulse is installed and `_should_setup_noninteractive_stats_wrapper` would have installed it.

## Where

- `.agents/scripts/lib/codex_mcp_toml.py:14` raises the error when neither `tomllib` nor `tomli` imports.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/config.sh` `update_codex_config` / `_deploy_codex_mcps` call bare `python3` and return 1 on failure.
- `setup.sh:1723` runs the stage under `_time_step`, so one optional runtime's config failure aborts the whole deploy.

## Suggested fix

1. Treat a Codex config failure as a warning: log it and continue to the remaining stages (scheduler install in particular).
2. Prefer a Python that has `tomllib` (for example Homebrew or uv-managed 3.11+) when the default `python3` is older, or print the exact remedy (`python3 -m pip install --user tomli`).

With `tomli` installed for `/usr/bin/python3`, `python3 .agents/scripts/codex-mcp-config.py` and `python3 .agents/scripts/codex-setup.py all` both exit 0. Without it, rerun `setup.sh --non-interactive` and confirm the stats-wrapper launchd job is still installed and setup exits 0 with a warning.

title: Cloudron commits-mode standing policy still rejects upstreamLicense.url full-SHA bumps (GH#38359 half-fixed)
body:
## What

A commit-mode (`upstream_mode: "commits"`) standing release policy still cannot authorize a real routine bump of a commit-tracked Cloudron package. Every such bump also moves `upstreamLicense.url` (`https://github.com/<upstream>/blob/<full sha>/LICENSE`), and the predicate rejects any manifest change beyond `version`/`upstreamVersion` in commits mode.

GH#38359 reported both halves (full-SHA Dockerfile pin and license URL). PR #38363 fixed only the pin half and explicitly kept `upstreamLicense` under canonical equality; the issue was closed as complete. GH#38739 later added license URL substitution, but only via `release_identity` or `license_version_url`, which are semver-mode features.

Observed on the public package repo `marcusquinn/cloudron-opendesk-app`: signed commits-mode policy #120, worker release PR #122 (0.2.27 -> 0.2.28, upstream `f43d956` -> `76fa2b1`). The only non-routine change is the license URL full-SHA substitution:

```
cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo marcusquinn/cloudron-opendesk-app --issue 123
PR #122: standing policy #120 does not apply (NOT_ROUTINE: manifest changes beyond version and upstreamVersion)
```

Result: r924 files a per-release approval request (#123) for every routine upstream bump, so the standing policy has never released this repo autonomously.

## How

Keep the signed-text contract: a widened predicate must not silently extend existing signatures. Follow the `license_version_url` opt-in pattern.

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh` `policy-request ... commits <upstream>`: add a signed opt-in field for commits mode (for example `"license_commit_url": true`), state it in the policy body text ("`upstreamLicense.url` may differ only by the proven full-SHA substitution"), and require a new signature. `release_policy_metadata()` must validate the field shape.
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py` `check_manifest_fields()` (around line 200): when `upstream_mode == "commits"` and the opt-in is set, add `{upstream_proof.base: upstream_proof.head}` (and the combined mapping with `{old_up: new_up}`, as `pinned_mappings` does at line 277) to `license_mappings`. Every other `upstreamLicense` key stays exact.
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh` `_cloudron_monitor_policy_allows_license_url()` (line 417): mirror the new opt-in so finding briefs tell workers the license URL may move.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`: commits-mode fixture with full-SHA Dockerfile pin plus SHA-bearing `upstreamLicense.url` returns `ROUTINE_BUMP` with the opt-in; returns `NOT_ROUTINE` without the opt-in, when the URL SHA differs from the proven head, or when another `upstreamLicense` key changes.
- After deploy and re-signing a regenerated policy, `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo marcusquinn/cloudron-opendesk-app` reports `standing policy #<N>` for the next routine bump instead of NOT_ROUTINE.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron_routine_bump.py`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh`

title: Pulse: skip a cycle of worker dispatch when the systemd worker backend probe fails at cycle start
body:
## What

When the selected systemd worker backend is unavailable at pulse cycle start, the pulse should skip worker dispatch for that cycle (and say why once) instead of claiming issues and failing every launch.

Follow-up split out of #39028, which fixes the cause: the sudo approval kick started an unmanaged pulse without the user session bus. This issue is the defence in depth for any other way a pulse can start without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` / `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`.

## Why

Evidence in #39028: one cycle with no user bus made five launches fail across three issues in about 10 minutes. Each one claimed the issue, failed with `manager_probe_failed`, and rolled the claim back. That is wasted claim/comment churn, and that pulse also held the lock that the timer pulse needed.

## Reproducer

From #39028 (Ubuntu, systemd user-service pulse, v3.39.228): a pulse started with `sudo -u <user> -H -- pulse-wrapper.sh`, with no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, held the pulse lock and logged on every dispatch:

    [dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: selected systemd backend unavailable for #<n> (reason=manager_probe_failed rc=1 ...); detached fallback suppressed
    [dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: worker spawn failed for #<n> rc=1; no worker submitted (GH#36390)

To reproduce locally on Linux: `env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` with an eligible `auto-dispatch` issue queued.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`

The cycle-level caller may live in a different `pulse-dispatch-*.sh` file. Confirm it with the `rg` command below and record the actual path.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh:240-273` `_dlw_systemd_user_service_available` already classifies the backend (`manager_probe_failed`, `missing_systemctl`, ...). Reuse it as is.
- Call it once per cycle before the dispatch phase claims anything, only when the selected backend is systemd. Find the dispatch-phase entry with `rg -n "dispatch_worker_launch|_dlw_launch_systemd_worker" .agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh`; the exact caller path must be found that way.
- On failure, log one line, for example `[pulse] dispatch skipped this cycle: systemd worker backend unavailable (reason=...)`, skip claim/launch for the cycle, and still run the non-dispatch phases (merge, housekeeping). Do not fall back to detached launches: that is suppressed on purpose.
- Do not change launchd/macOS behaviour.

## Acceptance

- With `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset on Linux under the systemd backend, one pulse cycle logs the skip line once, makes no dispatch claims, and produces no `worker spawn failed` lines.
- With a working bus, dispatch is unchanged (`launched via systemd-run transient user service`).

## Verification

- ShellCheck is clean on the changed files.
- Extend the existing systemd launch tests (`rg -l "_dlw_systemd_user_service_available" .agents/scripts/tests`) with one probe-fails case: assert no claim and the single skip log line.

title: t19123: linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh: add a sudo/user-session-bus fixture so approval and pulse kicks can be runtime-verified from macOS
body:
## What

Add a `--sudo-session` fixture mode to `.agents/scripts/linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh` that reproduces a real `sudo` environment reset for a non-root user who owns `/run/user/<uid>` and a live session-bus socket, and reports the user and session env that approval-triggered pulse kicks receive for the `--head` and `--base` trees.

## Why (observed evidence)

GH#39028 (PR #39126) is critical-risk, so `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` blocked PR body generation until runtime-verified evidence existed. The Linux evidence had to be composed ad hoc: a throwaway Debian `python:3-slim` container that installs `sudo jq procps git`, creates user `alice` (uid 1000), binds a unix socket at `/run/user/1000/bus`, replaces `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` with an env recorder, optionally puts a `systemctl` recorder on PATH, then runs `su alice -c "sudo bash -c 'source <tree>/.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh; <kick fn>'"` for the PR tree and `origin/main`. It showed main kicking the pulse with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<unset> DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=<unset>` and the fix carrying `/run/user/1000` and `unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus`. The same need will recur for sudo/approval, systemd user unit, or session-bus changes (e.g. #39118).

Gotchas: `approval-helper.sh` refuses to source without `git` on PATH (`BLOCKED: native Git unavailable on PATH`), so the image needs git; the recorder log must be world-writable because the kicked process runs as the real user.

## Reference pattern

Model on the existing `linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh` structure: its docker preflight (`command -v docker`, `docker info`), the `docker run --rm --init --cidfile --pids-limit 512` invocation, read-only `--head/--base` tree mounts, diffable per-case report, and exit codes 0 ok / 1 runtime unavailable / 2 container failure.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

## Acceptance

- `linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh --sudo-session --head DIR --base DIR` prints, per case (permission kick spawn fallback via `_kick_pulse_after_permission_approval`, issue-approval `--merge-only` kick via `_kick_pulse_after_approval issue`, permission kick with a `systemctl` recorder present), the user and session env the kicked process received.
- Against a pre-GH#39028 tree it reports unset session env; against current main it reports `/run/user/<uid>` values and, with the systemctl recorder, `systemctl --user start --no-block aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service`.
- Existing procfs fixture behaviour is unchanged; exits 1 with a clear message when docker is unavailable; shellcheck clean.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` Runtime Testing Gate gains one pointer line for runtime-verifying critical/high sudo/systemd changes from macOS with this mode.

## Verification

Run the new mode locally with OrbStack/Docker using `--base` = a commit before PR #39126 and `--head` = current main, and compare the reports; rerun the default procfs mode to confirm it is unchanged.
