title: fix(validators): reduce plugin test concurrency under moderate host load (follow-up to GH#35499)
body:
## What

The full-loop plugin validator still fails on timing-sensitive process tests when the host is busy but below the serialization threshold from GH#35499. Lower or graduate the threshold so moderately loaded hosts get reduced concurrency instead of default `node --test` parallelism.

## Why

`_validator_plugin_test_concurrency` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh:332` serializes only when the 1-minute load average exceeds 4 per CPU (64 on a 16-CPU Mac). It samples once, before the suite starts, and the suite itself then adds about 15 parallel test files that each spawn process trees.

On 2026-11-19, while running `commit-and-pr` for PR #39132 (a pricing/docs change), the "running plugin tests serially" line never appeared, and each run failed in a different unrelated test:

- `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:53` — `wait-aware status ...` got `'failed'` where `'succeeded'` was expected (4.4 s, against 1.9 s when run alone)
- `tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs:406,420` — `blocker logger exited 1` (parallel appenders)
- `tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs:129` — `termination_cause` was `'post_exit_cleanup'` where `null` was expected, at a load average of about 58 (3.6 per CPU, just under the threshold)
- two runs hit `TIMEOUT after 300s` and `TIMEOUT after 900s`

Each failing file passes alone. The full suite passed directly once the load dropped. The validator then passed on the first try with `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY=4`.

## Reproducer

On a 16-CPU host with other workers running (1-minute load about 40-64, i.e. below 4 per CPU), run `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue <N> ...` on a branch that touches `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`.

- Observed: the plugin tests run at default concurrency, and one or more of the timing tests above fail, or the suite hits the validator timeout.
- Expected: reduced concurrency is selected and the suite passes.
- Confirmation: `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY=4` on the same host makes it pass.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` `_validator_plugin_test_concurrency`: graduate by load per CPU. For example, above 4 → 1 (unchanged), above 1.5 → `max(2, floor(cpus/4))`, otherwise unset. Print the chosen value. Respect an existing caller-set `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY`.
- Keep the GH#35499 rule: never extend timeouts or budgets.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` clean.
- With a stubbed load (or `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY` preset), the helper prints the selected concurrency, and `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` receives `--test-concurrency=<n>`.
- Run `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` on a plugin-touching branch while other workers are active (load 2-4 per CPU); the plugin validator passes without manual env overrides.

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` should run `.agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh` against the generated title, PR body and changed-file list before creating the PR, and accept an optional `--regression-evidence TEXT` that `_build_pr_body` renders as a `## Regression Evidence` section. ## Why (observed evidence)

PR #39126 (GH#39028, title `fix(approval): ... sudo approvals`, no repository test change, Linux runtime evidence under `## Runtime Testing`) opened cleanly via `commit-and-pr`, then the required CI job `Platform Fix Regression Evidence` failed: `Platform-fix PRs must change a repository test ... or include a non-empty "## Regression Evidence" rationale`. Repair needed a hand-written body edit via `gh pr edit --body-file`; a `gh run rerun --failed` then failed again because reruns replay the original `pull_request` payload (old body). Only the `edited` event run passed, and the stale failed check stayed in the rollup. The generator already knows the title, body and files, so the gate is deterministic and cheap to run before publication. `test-platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh` already shows `## Runtime Testing` narrative does not satisfy the gate (`testing is not regression rationale` case).

## Reference pattern

Model on the existing runtime-risk pre-publication block in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` (the `PR body generation blocked` checks around line 520-535), which validates evidence before PR creation, and on `_build_pr_body` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` (around line 1046) for section rendering.

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-commit-and-pr-partial-success.sh`

title: t19125: Reset-aware OAuth pool rotation: prefer the account whose quota resets soonest
body:
## Task


Rotation over Anthropic OAuth seats with equal priority prefers the seat whose usage window (weekly first) resets soonest, provided that seat still has usable quota. In effect it is earliest-deadline-first, so quota that would expire unused gets spent before quota with more runway. When no reset/usage data is known for a seat, behaviour falls back to today's priority-then-LRU ordering unchanged.

## Done when

- [ ] With two equal-priority Anthropic seats where seat A has a known reset sooner than seat B and both have quota above the floor, every selection path (`selectPoolAccount`, `getAvailableAlternates`, proxy `getAvailableAccounts`, CLI rotate) picks seat A.
- [ ] When no seat has usage data, ordering is identical to today (priority desc, then LRU), and an explicit higher `priority` still wins over reset ordering.
- [ ] A seat whose remaining quota is at or below the floor, or whose reset time has passed (stale data), is not preferred on reset grounds.
- [ ] `model-accounts-pool list` shows the known reset time and remaining percentage per Anthropic seat, or `unknown`.
- [ ] The PR body records the chosen data source with evidence and the rejected alternatives; no token or auth header value is logged.
- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`).

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool.mjs:91-154` (comparator + `selectPoolAccount`) and `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-retry.mjs:22-152` (only place a reset time is seen today).
- **Load only if:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs:197-231` when changing mid-session 429 rotation; `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_rotate.py:89-109` when changing CLI rotation.
- **Why:** these are every place that orders seats; they must agree.
- **Stop when:** a verified data source is chosen and every comparator below is routed through one shared ordering rule.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool.mjs:96-101` — `compareAccountPriority`: within equal priority, order by soonest known reset of a seat that still has quota, then LRU.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-pool.mjs:63-68` — `getAvailableAlternates` sorts by LRU only (it ignores priority today). Route it through the shared comparator.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-retry.mjs:35-42` — `sortAccountsByPriority` (priority, then seat key). Use the shared rule. Also persist `rate_limit_info` data (line 146) rather than keeping it only in the in-memory `rateLimitedAccounts` map.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_rotate.py:89-109` — `_select_rotation_candidate`: same ordering for Tier-1 candidates.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-storage.mjs:25-40` — document any new per-seat fields in the account typedef.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-display.mjs` — show known reset time / remaining quota per seat in `model-accounts-pool list`, so ordering is explainable.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `selectPoolAccount` (oauth-pool.mjs:140) → `injectPoolToken`, `selectRuntimePoolAccount` (V2 path, v2-provider-auth.mjs:169); `getAvailableAlternates` → provider-auth.mjs:76,216,272; `getAvailableAccounts` (claude-proxy-retry.mjs:78); CLI `oauth-pool-helper.sh rotate` → pool_ops_rotate.py.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `patchAccount` (oauth-pool-storage.mjs) is the only writer to use for new fields; `handle429Recovery` (provider-auth.mjs:213) already writes `cooldownUntil`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/tests/test_pool_ops.py`, `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh`; offline diagnostic `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs`.
- **Schemas/config:** pool account entries documented by the typedef in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-storage.mjs` (new optional fields; absent = unknown).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copies under `~/.aidevops/agents/` via `setup.sh --non-interactive`; no generated sources.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the new fields are optional and populate as data arrives; searched `oauth-pool-storage.mjs` and found no schema version to bump.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because reverting the PR is sufficient; evidence: old comparators in `oauth-pool.mjs` read only `priority`/`lastUsed`, so leftover fields are ignored.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Decide the data source with evidence (blocking decision).** Do not guess endpoints or header names. Candidates to verify against live traffic or installed code:
   (a) Anthropic API response headers seen by the provider-auth fetch wrapper (log header names only, never values tied to tokens);
   (b) Claude CLI stream-json `rate_limit_event.rate_limit_info`, which already carries `status` and `resetsAt` (claude-proxy-retry.mjs:144-147). Check whether it also carries window type or utilisation on non-rejected events;
   (c) the usage endpoint the Claude CLI uses for its usage display, only if its URL is found in installed Claude CLI code or official docs.
   Record the chosen source, its rejected alternatives and the evidence in the PR body. If no source gives the reset time before exhaustion, settle for (b) on any rate-limit event. Record the gap.
2. Persist per seat: `usageResetAt` (epoch ms), `usageRemainingPct` (0-100 or null), `usageObservedAt`, written via `patchAccount`. Treat data older than the reset time, or older than a freshness bound you choose and justify, as unknown.
3. Add one shared ordering helper and use it from all four comparators. Rule: explicit `priority` stays primary (a manual pin wins). Within equal priority, seats with a known future reset and remaining quota above a small floor (e.g. 5%) sort ascending by reset time. Seats with unknown data sort after known-good seats, ordered by LRU. Mirror the rule in Python for pool_ops_rotate.py.
4. Show reset/remaining in `model-accounts-pool list` output.
5. Run the existing pool tests and the offline rotation probe; deploy with `setup.sh --non-interactive` and confirm with `model-accounts-pool list`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** writes go through `patchAccount`/`withPoolLock`. Do not add a separate write path.
- **Migration/rollback:** optional fields; old code ignores them; rollback = revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** the Python CLI and JS plugin can run different versions. Both must treat missing fields as unknown and fall back to priority+LRU.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated observations overwrite with the newer `usageObservedAt` only.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if usage capture fails, selection behaves exactly as today. Never block auth on usage data.
- **Security:** never log tokens or raw auth headers. Log only seat labels, reset times and percentages.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs
python3 -m pytest .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/tests/test_pool_ops.py
bash tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** rotation probe covers JS selection; pytest covers `_select_rotation_candidate`; helper test covers CLI rotate; lint covers all changed files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: commands above
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: reset-aware oauth pool ordering`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — scoped to pool selection

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** Do not change OpenAI/Google/Cursor selection semantics beyond what the shared comparator implies for missing data (must be identical to today). Do not fetch any URL not verified in step 1.

**AI brief owner:** maintainer interactive session.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-pool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-retry.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-storage.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-display.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs`

title: routine-log-helper: create-issue persists multi-line issue_number (stderr mixed into URL capture)
body:
## Bug

`routine-log-helper.sh create-issue` stores a multi-line `issue_number` in `cron/<id>/routine-state.json`, e.g. `"issue_number": "37993\n18"` instead of `"18"`. Observed on every core routine (r901-r914) on v3.39.232 after `init-routines`.

## Cause (verified in source)

`.agents/scripts/routine-log-helper.sh:1031-1033` captures the issue URL with `issue_url=$(gh_create_issue ... 2>&1)`, so stderr lines from the wrapper are mixed into the value. Line 1041 then runs `grep -oE '[0-9]+$'`, which matches a trailing number on every line, producing a two-line result. The value is persisted without validation (around line 1054) and returned as the existing issue on later calls. `init-routines-helper.sh` survives only because it takes `tail -1` of the output; the run-update paths (`gh_issue_edit_safe "$issue_number"` and similar) receive the raw multi-line value, so routine tracking issues likely never receive run results.

## Fix

1. Drop `2>&1` from the capture (log stderr separately) and extract only the last `/issues/<n>` match.
2. Refuse to persist any `issue_number` not matching `^[0-9]+$`.
3. Normalise to the last numeric line on read, so existing broken state heals without manual edits.

## Verification

```bash
for f in ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/cron/r9*/routine-state.json; do
  jq -e '.issue_number|tostring|test("^[0-9]+$")' "$f" >/dev/null || echo "BAD $f"
done   # expect no output
```

Acceptance: every state file holds a numeric issue number; tracking issues update after a run; a second `create-issue` does not create a duplicate issue (negative).

Core routine r924 (Cloudron releases, every 30 minutes) fails on every run on hosts with no registered Cloudron packages, which is most users. Observed on v3.39.232 with `repos.json` containing zero `app_type: cloudron-package` entries.

title: research-only subagent cannot read registered repos outside the session directory
body:
## Problem

The `research-only` subagent cannot read repositories registered in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` when they live outside the parent session's directory. Build+ guidance routes all research-only discovery to `research-only` ("never `general` or `explore`"), so multi-repo audits from a hub session fail: every Read/Grep/Glob on a sibling repo returns `Permission denied: external_directory`.

Observed on v3.39.232 / OpenCode 2.3.0: a hub session delegated read-only audits of two registered sibling repos outside the hub directory; both research-only children were fully blocked, while an `explore` child read the same files without issue (the global config allows them).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/build-plus.md`
- `.agents/reference/research-staging.md`

> Maintainer edit: the reporter scoped `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs`. The maintainer review moved the scope to the guidance files. See "Maintainer resolution" below.

## Cause

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs` `addResearchStagingPermissions()` (around line 289) sets the research-only profile's `external_directory` to `{ "*": "deny" }` plus only the research-staging directory. Registered repos are never added.

## Proposal

Allow read-only `external_directory` access for the `path` of every repo in `repos.json` (and their linked worktrees under `worktree_base_dir`), keeping the existing credential-name denies (`.env`, `.env.*`, `.npmrc`, `credential*`, etc.) applied under each allowed root. Optionally gate with a config key (e.g. `research_only.registered_repos: true`, default on).

## Acceptance

- A research-only child can Read/Grep/Glob any registered repo path from a session rooted elsewhere.
- `.env`, `.npmrc`, `credential*` and the other denied names remain blocked inside those roots (negative).
- Unregistered paths under `~/` remain denied (negative).

## Maintainer resolution (supersedes Proposal and Acceptance above)

The defect is real, but it sits in the routing guidance, not in the permission profile. The `research-only` deny-all `external_directory` envelope is a deliberate boundary: GH#28703 / #28768, `reference/research-staging.md`: "All sibling external directories remain denied". Do **not** change `config-agent-profiles.mjs` or `tools/ai-assistants/research-only.md`. The contradiction is in `.agents/build-plus.md:92`, which sends *all* read-only discovery to `research-only` and offers no route for targets outside the session root.

### Implementation

1. `.agents/build-plus.md:92`: limit the rule to what the profile can reach, and point to the cross-repo route. Replacement for the first sentence:

   ```markdown
   Research-only discovery inside the session root or staged artifacts uses
   `research-only`, never `general` or `explore`; for other repositories follow
   `reference/research-staging.md` "Cross-repository research".
   ```

2. `.agents/build-plus.md:98` (Deliberation bullet): change "launch at most 2 focused Explore agents" to "launch at most 2 focused `research-only` agents". The bullet currently contradicts line 92.
3. `.agents/reference/research-staging.md`: add a `## Cross-repository research` section before `## Independent code review`, with this content (wording may be tightened, semantics may not change):

   ```markdown
   ## Cross-repository research

   `research-only` cannot read registered repositories or linked worktrees
   outside the session root; this is intentional and must not be widened per
   repository. For read-only discovery in another repository:

   1. Search it directly from the primary session (`rg`/`git -C <repo> grep`,
      then targeted Read).
   2. To delegate bounded analysis, stage regular files or a
      `review-evidence-helper.sh bundle` output into a task child here and pass
      that path, or pass excerpts to `ai-research` via `files`.
   3. For a whole-repository audit, run it from a session rooted in that
      repository.

   Do not substitute `general` or `explore`; they are not fail-closed.
   ```

### Acceptance

- `rg -n "research-only|Explore" .agents/build-plus.md` shows no instruction that routes out-of-root discovery to `research-only` and no remaining "Explore agents" routing.
- `reference/research-staging.md` documents the three cross-repo routes. The existing "All sibling external directories remain denied" boundary statement is unchanged.
- Negative: `git diff --stat origin/main` touches only the two files in Files Scope. `config-agent-profiles.mjs` and `research-only.md` are unchanged.

### Verification

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` (markdown checks) passes for the two files.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-research-only-profile.mjs` still passes. This proves the permission envelope is untouched.

- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because reverting removes capture only; evidence: `usableResetAt` in `oauth-pool-ordering.mjs` treats stale data as unknown after reset or 8 days.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Verify header names (blocking).** Temporarily log only the *names* of response headers whose names contain `ratelimit` from one live `anthropic` OAuth response, plus their values for those headers only (never `authorization`, cookies or tokens). Record the observed names, value formats (epoch seconds vs ISO, fraction vs percent) and which window each covers in the PR body. Remove the temporary log before committing. If no reset/utilisation headers exist on successful responses, record that. Then capture only on 429 responses that carry a reset value, and note the gap.
2. Implement `usagePatchFromResponseHeaders` beside `usagePatchFromRateLimitInfo`, reusing `toMs` and the same remaining-percent clamping. Prefer the weekly window when several are present (match `WINDOW_RANK`).
3. Add a best-effort `recordSeatUsageFromResponse(seatKey, response)` (model on `recordAccountUsage`: try/catch, `shouldReplaceUsage`, `patchAccount`). Call it from both provider paths. Skip if `seatKey` is null.
4. Deploy with `setup.sh --non-interactive`, make one Anthropic request, and confirm `model-accounts-pool list` shows `resets in …` for the active seat.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** `patchAccount` uses the pool lock; a write per response is acceptable, but skip the write when `shouldReplaceUsage` returns false to avoid lock churn.
- **Migration/rollback:** no schema change; revert removes capture only.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older Python CLI ignores or already understands the fields from PR 39143.
- **Idempotency/retry:** replacement is newest-observation-wins within a window rank; repeated responses are harmless.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** any parse error leaves the response untouched; never consume or clone the body for this.
- **Security:** never log token-bearing headers; the permanent code logs nothing beyond seat label and reset time.

- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not read or clone response bodies; do not log auth headers; do not change OpenAI/Google/Cursor paths.

title: fix(routines): preserve user enabled/disabled state for core routines across routines TODO.md regeneration
body:
## What

Keep a user's enabled/disabled choice (`- [x]` / `- [ ]`) for **core** routines when `init-routines-helper.sh` regenerates the routines repo `TODO.md`.

## Why

`_write_todo_md()` (`.agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh:55-100`) keeps the `## User Routines` tail, but rewrites every `## Core Routines (framework-managed)` line from `get_core_routine_entries`, using the framework default `enabled` field. Every setup or `aidevops update` runs `scaffold_repo` → `_write_todo_md` (directly for new repos, or through `_publish_routines_scaffold` for existing remotes, `init-routines-helper.sh:565-650`). That publishes the default `[x]` back over the user's `[ ]`.

This contradicts the generated header comment ("Edit only the enabled/disabled state here") and the documented pause path (`init-routines-helper.sh:852-853`: "Change `- [x] ${rid}` to `- [ ] ${rid}` in the routines repo TODO.md"). Found while reviewing #39145. There, a user could not turn off a routine that failed on every run, because their pause was reverted on the next setup.

## Reproducer

Reproduced against `main` @ `83390d35d1`. A scratch dir contains a `TODO.md` with `- [ ] r924 Cloudron releases ...` in the core section and `- [x] r001 Example ...` under `## User Routines`. Run:

```bash
source .agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh
DRY_RUN=false
_write_todo_md "$scratch"
grep -E '^- \[( |x)\] r924 |^- \[( |x)\] r001 ' "$scratch/TODO.md"
```

Output:

title: fix(runtime): detect output-limit (finish: length) responses and steer to sectioned writes
body:
## What

Detect when an assistant response hits OpenCode's request output limit (`finish: length`, with the in-flight tool call aborted) and tell the model why it stopped, so it switches to sectioned writes instead of losing the work or repeating it.

## Why

OpenCode caps each response at 32,000 output tokens (`HOST_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs:87`). When a model tries to write a large file in one Write call, the response ends with finish reason `length`. The tool call is aborted as `Tool execution aborted` and nothing is saved. Headless `opencode run` then exits silently.

Evidence:

- Fable 5.2 scene build, 2026-11-17: two `length` responses saved nothing and cost $3.05 of the run's $8.59 API-equivalent cost. The fix was a raised limit plus sectioned writes (now documented in `.agents/tools/design/blender-scripted-scenes.md`, but only Blender work reads that guide).
- This project's interactive session DB alone shows 17 `length` finishes across 12 sessions and 5 models (claude-haiku-5-5 ×9, gpt-5.6-sol ×4, claude-fable-5-2 ×2, gpt-5.5 ×1, claude-opus-5-5 ×1).
- No framework code detects this. `rg -i "finish.{0,20}length"` across the plugin and `.agents/scripts` finds nothing. In `headless-runtime-helper.sh:519`, `premature_exit` resumes with a generic completion contract that does not mention the output limit, so the resumed model can hit the same limit again.

## Reproducer

Trigger: in any OpenCode session, ask the model to write one file of more than about 2,500 lines in a single Write call.

**Symptom command:** `sqlite3 -readonly -header -column <data>/opencode.db "select data->>'modelID' model, count(*) length_finishes, count(distinct session_id) sessions, round(sum(data->>'cost'),2) cost from message where data->>'role'='assistant' and data->>'finish'='length' group by 1 order by 2 desc"`

**Actual output** (project interactive DB, 2026-11-19):

```text
model             length_finishes  sessions  cost
claude-haiku-5-5  9                5         1.13
gpt-5.6-sol       4                4         0.0
claude-fable-5-2  2                1         3.05
gpt-5.5           1                1         0.0
claude-opus-5-5   1                1         0.82
```

**Expected:** after a `length` finish, the next turn or headless resume is told the cause and writes in sections. Currently nothing tells it, and the Write tool part shows `Tool execution aborted` with no file saved.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-turn-state.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh` (scope recovery: the premature-exit resume prompt is built here, in `_handle_cmd_run_continuation_attempt`; the helper cannot change it without this one-line hook)
- ADD: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-output-limit-notice.mjs`

1. **Plugin, interactive and headless.** On `message.updated` for an assistant message with `finish === "length"`, record a one-shot flag for the session. Follow the existing per-session state pattern in `session-turn-state.mjs`. On the next system transform for that session, inject one short note: "Your previous response hit the 32K output-token limit and its tool call was discarded; nothing was written. Write large files in sections of under ~120 lines (Write, then Edit appends)." Clear the flag after injecting.
2. **Headless resume.** Where `premature_exit` → `resume_session_with_completion_contract` is chosen (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:519`), detect a final `length` finish from the session (DB query or exported messages). Classify it as `output_clamp` and add the sectioned-write instruction to the resume prompt.
3. Do **not** raise `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX` by default. OpenCode compacts at context minus this limit (`model-limits.mjs:93-104`), so raising it costs compaction headroom and only moves the cliff. Keep it as the documented opt-in for deliberate long-output delegations.

## Verification

- Plugin: a unit test in the existing session-turn-state test style. A synthetic `message.updated` with `finish: "length"` produces exactly one injected note on the next transform and none after that.
- Headless: the `output_clamp` classification is chosen for a session whose last assistant message has `finish: length`, and the resume prompt contains the sectioned-write instruction.
- `node --test` for the touched plugin tests; ShellCheck clean on `headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

title: project-node-runtime: worker prelaunch ignores /usr/local/bin and unversioned Homebrew node that satisfy engines
body:
## What

`_project_node_bin` in `.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh` aborts worker prelaunch with `project_node_environment_failure` even when an installed Node satisfies the project's `engines.node`, because it never considers the official macOS installer location `/usr/local/bin/node` (unless that happens to be first on PATH).

## Observed

- macOS arm64. PATH resolves `node` to a v22.22.3 copy in `~/.local/bin` (installed by another tool). `/usr/local/bin/node` is v24.13.0 from the nodejs.org pkg installer.
- Project pins `.node-version` 22.23.5 and `engines.node: ">=22.23.4"`.
- `headless-prelaunch.log`: `prelaunch_abort ... cause=project_node_environment_failure` for two workers in a row; the issues stayed queued.
- Candidates scanned (lines ~92-107): current `node`, fnm, nvm, volta, mise, `<brew>/opt/node@*/bin/node`, n. Plain `/usr/local/bin/node` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/node` (unversioned `node` formula) are not candidates, so pass 2 ("any hard-compatible runtime") cannot find v24 even though it satisfies `>=22.23.4`.
- Workaround applied: `brew install node@22` (then `brew unlink` to keep the user's default PATH), after which the resolver returns `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin`.

## Proposed fix

Add the standard system install locations to the candidate list after the version-manager caches: `/usr/local/bin/node`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/node`, `${HOMEBREW_PREFIX}/bin/node`, and `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` (deduplicated, `-x` checked). Pass 1 still prefers exact pins; pass 2 can then pick any installed runtime that satisfies `engines`.

## Verification

Extend the existing project-node-runtime test with a fake `/usr/local`-style prefix (overridable like `AIDEVOPS_NODE_BREW_PREFIXES`) containing a satisfying node while PATH holds an older one; the resolver should print that bin dir and return 0.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh

title: t19128: fix(pulse-merge): hand stale origin:interactive draft PRs to workers instead of skipping them forever
body:
## What

A stale `origin:interactive` **draft** PR (no live claim, owning session idle or gone, PR idle past the handover window) is handed to the worker pipeline the same way a stale non-draft interactive PR already is (GH#23425 / t2189 `_interactive_pr_is_stale`), instead of being skipped forever as "draft PR not eligible for auto-merge".

## Why

`gh_create_pr` defaults every interactive-origin PR to draft (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` `_gh_create_pr_should_default_draft`); full-loop marks it ready at the end. When the interactive session ends early, the draft stays parked. `_check_interactive_pr_gates` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:365`) returns on `is_draft == true` before `_interactive_pr_auto_merge_allowed` ever reaches the stale check, so no automation revisits the work and the maintainer has to notice it.

Evidence (pulse.log, 2026-11-18/19): `marcusquinn/aidevops` PR #35518 (draft since 2026-10-23, now CONFLICTING) and #37733 (draft since 2026-11-11, MERGEABLE) each logged 200+ merge-pass "draft PR not eligible" skips with no handover. The sync-workflows instance of the same draft default is fixed separately in t19126 (GH#39153).

## How

### Reference pattern

Model on the non-draft stale path in `_interactive_pr_auto_merge_allowed` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:337-348`), which calls `_interactive_pr_is_stale` and `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue`.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:365-383`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-author-checks.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`

### Approach

- `_check_interactive_pr_gates`: when `is_draft == true` and no `hold-for-review`/`no-takeover` label, call `_interactive_pr_is_stale` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh:416`). Stale → route to the existing handover (`_interactive_pr_trigger_handover`, same file) so a worker continues the branch, finishes the remaining work, and marks it ready. Not stale → keep today's skip.
- Decide (and record in the PR body) whether the handover marks the PR ready immediately or leaves readiness to the continuation worker; prefer the worker deciding, because a draft means the author did not declare it complete.
- Drafts without a linked issue (e.g. #37733 uses `Ref #37552`) must follow the same orphan-recovery path `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue` already uses for non-draft interactive PRs.
- Keep the draft-protection in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh:1126` (no CONFLICTING-close of drafts).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh` pass; extend them only if needed to cover the stale-draft branch.
- `shellcheck` on changed files.
- After deploy: pulse.log shows a handover line for a stale interactive draft instead of the "draft PR not eligible" skip.

## Acceptance

- Stale interactive drafts without `hold-for-review`/`no-takeover` get exactly one handover; fresh drafts and opted-out drafts are skipped as today.

title: t19129: fix(checkpoint-continuation): treat temp_dir_recovery releases as stall-class so draft checkpoints continue instead of parking for attention
body:
## What

A `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=temp_dir_recovery` release on an issue with a worker draft checkpoint PR is treated as a stall-class release, so the draft gets an immediate exact-head continuation instead of a `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` record that parks it for the 12h attention re-arm window.

## Why

`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1400-1409` (GH#35128) releases the claim as `temp_dir_recovery` when the OpenCode permission broker stops a worker for writing outside the project (e.g. host `/tmp`). Its comment states the intent: "owned recovery (use AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR); no maintainer hold. Release the claim so the issue is redispatched." Without a draft PR that is what happens. With a draft checkpoint, `temp_dir_recovery` is missing from every stall-release list, so `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` falls through to `_pcc_completed_attention` and posts `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... reason=temp_dir_recovery`. Ordinary redispatch then stays blocked (`worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`) until the 43200s re-arm, so a runtime-only interruption costs 12h+ per occurrence.

Evidence (2026-11-19): three open issues in a private managed repo (one with a draft checkpoint PR parked since 2026-11-18) carry `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... reason=temp_dir_recovery`; 46 issues across managed repos have had `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=temp_dir_recovery`. The runtime, not the worker, ended these attempts, so no worker decision about completeness exists — the same condition as the existing stall classes (`watchdog_kill:*`, `worker_incomplete_exit`).

## How

### Reference pattern

Model on how `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` / `worker_incomplete_exit` are listed as stall-class releases in all four mirrors below; keep the four lists consistent (their comments already say they mirror each other).

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:77` — add `temp_dir_recovery` to `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:138-142` — add `"temp_dir_recovery"` to the jq `validator_stall` list.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py:111-114` — add `"temp_dir_recovery"` to `STALL_RELEASE_REASONS`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh:48` — add `temp_dir_recovery` to `_PDCU_RELEASE_REASON_PATTERN`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-attention.sh` — one case: a `temp_dir_recovery` release on a draft checkpoint yields a continuation, not `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_POSTED`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-attention.sh`

### Hazards

- Trust boundary: stall-class releases must still name their own poster (`checkpoint_release_fields`, `#aidevops:trust-boundary`); do not relax that.
- Loops: a worker that keeps writing to host `/tmp` is bounded by the existing per-PR fuse `_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES` (default 6); do not add a new fuse.
- Existing attention records for the three open issues are not rewritten; they re-arm on the existing schedule.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-attention.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-selfhold.sh`
- `python3 -m pytest .agents/scripts/tests -k checkpoint_events` if a pytest file covers `pr_checkpoint_events.py`; otherwise the shell suites above.
- `shellcheck` on changed shell files.

## Acceptance

- A trusted, self-attributed `temp_dir_recovery` release on a draft checkpoint routes to exact-head continuation; `blocked`, `push_policy_timeout`, `network_policy_timeout` and `worker_ownership_lost` behaviour is unchanged.

## What

The pre-merge snapshot ignores a non-required check run that has been pending longer than `PULSE_MERGE_STALE_NONREQUIRED_PENDING_SECONDS` (default 3600) when every required context is completed with `success`, `neutral` or `skipped`.

title: Worker PRs open against main when the repo default branch is dev; guard the PR base
body:
## What

Worker PRs in managed repos whose default branch is `dev` are sometimes opened against `main`. Guard `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` (and the merge pass) so a worker PR targets the remote default branch unless `--base` names a genuine stacked parent.

## Observed evidence (one runner, 2026-11-18..19)

- Three worker PRs in two private managed repos (default branch `dev`, a release-only `main` with a ruleset `update` restriction) were created with base `main`.
- Effects: (1) the PR diff carried the dev/main divergence (one showed 58 files including two `.github/workflows/*` files it never touched, so the merge pass skipped it with "modifies workflow files but token lacks workflow scope"); (2) `Resolves #N` did not link, because closing keywords only apply on the default branch; (3) `full-loop-helper.sh merge` failed with "the base branch policy prohibits the merge" while all required checks were green; (4) unrelated CI failures from the divergence were routed to CI fix-workers.
- Retargeting with `gh pr edit N --base dev` fixed each one: the diff shrank to the PR's own commits and one PR merged immediately.
- Root cause of the `main` base is NOT established. `_resolve_pr_base_branch` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` (lines ~252-262) uses the remote default branch unless `FULL_LOOP_STACK_BASE` is set by `--base` (added for stacked PRs, GH#37578). Candidates: a worker passing `--base main`, a raw `gh pr create --base main`, or a `branch.<name>.gh-merge-base` config. No `Stacked PR: base is origin/main` line was found in the runner logs, so the path is unknown.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_validate_stack_base`: refuse `--base` when it names a long-lived branch that is not a stacked parent (for example any branch other than the default that matches the repo's protected/ruleset branches, or `main`/`master` when the default branch differs), with an error naming the default branch.
2. Merge pass (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` gate chain): when a worker-origin PR's `baseRefName` differs from the repo default branch and the head branch is not a stacked child of another open PR, retarget to the default branch with an audit comment (or route it once with that diagnosis) instead of routing CI fix-workers.
3. Add one log line in `commit-and-pr` stating the chosen base and its source (default / `--base` / gh config) so the root cause is visible next time.

## Verification

- Existing stacked-PR tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/` around `commit-and-pr --base`) still pass.
- A fixture repo with default `dev` and a `main` branch: `commit-and-pr --base main` without a stacked parent fails with the new error; with no `--base` the PR targets `dev`.

title: browser-qa-helper screenshot exits 1 on Linux without sips/magick even when images are within max-dim
body:
## Observed

On Linux without ImageMagick, `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot` captures every screenshot and prints valid JSON results, then exits 1 with:

```text
[ERROR] No supported image tool found for guardrails (need sips or magick)
[ERROR] Screenshot guardrail enforcement failed
```

This happened even though every capture was already within `--max-dim 1568` (375x667 and 1440x900 viewports, no `--full-page`). Callers that trust the exit code treat a successful visual check as a failure.

Reproduce (any public URL, Linux host with neither `sips` nor `magick` on PATH):

```bash
browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url https://example.com --pages / --viewports mobile,desktop --max-dim 1568 --output-dir "$AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR/qa"
echo $?   # 1, though the PNGs and JSON are fine
```

## Expected

When no resize tool is available, read the PNG dimensions (the IHDR header is enough: bytes 16-23) and pass if every image is within `--max-dim`. Fail only when an image actually exceeds the limit and cannot be resized. Optionally fall back to Python Pillow or Playwright's own `clip`/viewport sizing before failing.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh`: the screenshot guardrail step that looks for `sips` or `magick`.
- `.agents/reference/screenshot-limits.md`: document the Linux fallback.

## Verification

Run the reproduce command on a Linux host without ImageMagick: it should exit 0 with the same JSON. Then pass a `--full-page` capture taller than 1568px: it should still fail with a clear message naming the oversized file.

1. Replace lines 486-488. `env` applies the later duplicate assignment, so the appended values override `runtime_env`:

```

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none. This is a test-local env array and `tmp_dir` is a per-run `mktemp -d`.

- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** product code is unchanged, and the `chromium` override contract from #36329 stays as it is.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the test is deterministic, and `tmp_dir` is removed at the end of the function.

```

**Hard boundaries:** do not change `.agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs`, because its precedence is intentional (GH#36325). Do not add a CI workflow for this test in this task. Wiring it into CI is a separate maintainer decision, since it would be a new CI test gate.

The failing case is `runtime-check accepts a valid configured executable` (`configured=0, unset=1, invalid=1, stale=1`). The #39043 PR body said this failure was "tracked separately", but no tracking issue exists (searched `runtime-check configured executable` and `test-browser-qa-helper runtime-check`).

## What

Make the `runtime-check accepts a valid configured executable` case in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` test the current executable-precedence contract, so the suite passes again on `main`.

## Why

The product behaviour is intentional; the test drifted:

title: fix(worker-contract): state the PR-less consolidation-task exception so workers stop blocking on parent writes and self-closure
body:
## What

The headless worker contract tells workers to finish a pulse `consolidation-task` with no PR, but it never says so. Add an explicit consolidation exception. Also reconcile the worker scope rule with the consolidation brief's required writes on the parent issue.

## Why

The runtime already accepts a PR-less consolidation finish: `_hrw_consolidation_terminal_complete` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` (called from `_hrw_pr_less_terminal_complete`) checks for a closed task, a `Consolidation complete. Parent: #P → New: #N` receipt, a closed `consolidated` parent and a successor with `Supersedes #P`. The worker-facing contract in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh` lists PR-less exceptions for review-triage, report-only, data-only and already-satisfied work. It has no consolidation exception. `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Worker scope enforcement (t1894)" also forbids writes on any issue except the dispatched one. The consolidation brief from `pulse-triage-dispatch.sh` requires those writes: comment on, relabel and close the parent, then repoint dependants.

Observed on one runner (2026-11-18/19, aidevops v3.39.228–v3.39.232, one model route). The same model failed on three consolidation tasks in a managed project repo:

- Two tasks were dispatched in the same minute. Both exited `BLOCKED` about 80 seconds after launch, before any successor existed. One was released as `permission_required` and the other as `unknown`. A maintainer finished the first one interactively.
- The third task did all the work: it created the successor, closed the parent and repointed dependants. It then declined to close itself and stated: "The headless continuation contract requires a PR or an explicitly marked PR-less completion contract; this operational task has neither, so self-closure remains unresolved". It was released as `unknown` / `needs-ai-recovery`.

Over the same period, consolidation tasks on other model routes completed and released as `worker_complete`. Workers on a model that follows the contract literally therefore stop on a runtime-supported outcome. Each stop parks the task under `needs-ai-recovery`, and the parent stays on `needs-consolidation`.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh`, add a "Consolidation exception" next to the other PR-less exceptions (around the report-only/already-satisfied lines). It applies only when the dispatched issue is trusted, carries `consolidation-task` and has a `## Consolidation target: #P` line. In that case the brief's parent writes (comment, `consolidated` label, close, dependency repoint) are in scope. The worker then posts the exact `Consolidation complete. Parent: #P → New: #N` receipt, closes the task as completed and emits FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE with no PR. Mirror the predicates in `_hrw_consolidation_terminal_complete`.
2. In `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`, add one line under "Worker scope enforcement (t1894)" and one subsection under "PR-less completion contracts". Point both to the runtime predicate so the docs and the classifier stay aligned.
3. Optional: in `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`, have the consolidation brief name this contract exception in its step 4/5 text.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh
- EDIT: .agents/reference/worker-discipline.md
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

title: fix(worker-activity): three corrupt log lines make the activity summary report zero workers
body:
## Symptom

`worker-activity-helper.sh summary` reports that no workers ran at all, while pulse is running
normally and the metrics log is being appended to every few minutes:

```
headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl (canonical worker outcomes; scope: global):
  Raw attempt/events:          0
  Terminal session outcomes:   0
  Rate-limited:                0
  Other failure:               0
  Result classes:              {}
  Timing ms (avg/max/samples): 0/0/0
```

The true figure for the same window is **326 worker events**, newest 4 minutes before the report:

```
newest worker event: 2026-11-19T06:42:11Z
worker events in 24h: 326
  173  success
   77  post_pr_handoff
   28  watchdog_stall_continue
   27  blocked
   11  premature_exit
    6  failed
    4  watchdog_stall_killed
```

This is the worst possible failure mode for a diagnostic: it does not report "log unreadable", it
reports a confident, well-formatted zero. Anyone reading it concludes pulse is dead and starts
debugging a healthy dispatcher — or, worse, restarts it. The blocker section of the same report
keeps working, because it uses a different code path, so the output looks internally consistent.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `worker-activity-helper.sh summary`

**Actual output:**

```
headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl (canonical worker outcomes; scope: global):
  Raw attempt/events:          0
  Terminal session outcomes:   0
  Result classes:              {}
```

**Expected output:** 326 worker events for the same 24h window, newest `2026-11-19T06:42:11Z`.

Supporting commands and their actual output:

**Symptom command:** `stat -c '%y %s' ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`

**Actual output:** `2026-11-19 06:42:11.652162309 +0000 6989074` — the log is being appended to
within minutes of the zero report.

**Symptom command:**

```bash
jq -rn --argjson cutoff 1794984350 \
  '[inputs | select(.role == "worker" and (.ts // 0) >= $cutoff)] | length' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl
```

**Actual output:**

```
jq: error (at <metrics-log>:2071): Invalid literal at line 2071, column 646
```

**Expected output:** `326`. This is the helper's own filter with stderr left visible, which is what
the helper suppresses.

Three malformed lines out of 6808 are enough to zero the whole report:

```
lines total: 6808
lines malformed: 3
  line 2071: 2025 bytes: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 644 (char 643)
  line 5209: 1191 bytes: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 2 column 1 (char 1191)
  line 5212: 1848 bytes: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 677 (char 676)
```

A tolerant reader that skips exactly those three lines produces the 326-event summary above, so no
data beyond the three records is actually lost.

## Cause, part 1 — the reader fails open to zeros

`_wah_aggregate_metrics` in `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh:326` ends with:

```bash
result=$(_wah_jq_with_objective_outcomes -rn ... "$jq_program" <"$metrics" 2>/dev/null) || result="0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0"
```

`jq`'s `inputs` aborts the entire stream on the first malformed record, `2>/dev/null` discards the
diagnostic, and the `||` branch substitutes zeros that are then printed as if they were measured.
The comment at `:295` states the intent explicitly — "Fail-open to zeros if jq fails (stale/corrupt
jsonl)" — so this is deliberate, but fail-open is the wrong direction for a measurement: a count of
zero is not a safe default, it is a false statement about the fleet.

`_wah_metric_details` at `:353` suppresses stderr the same way and needs the same treatment.

## Cause, part 2 — the writer corrupts lines under concurrency

The three bad records are spliced, not truncated: the parse fails mid-object and line 5209 contains
an embedded newline. That is the signature of interleaved concurrent appends, which is expected
here — at the time of this report ten `pulse-wrapper.sh` and `pulse-merge-routine.sh` processes
across two users were appending to their own logs, and records are 1.2–2 KB.

Fixing only the reader leaves a log that keeps accumulating damage; fixing only the writer leaves
every existing log able to zero a report. Both halves are needed, and they are independently
testable, so they can be split into separate PRs if that is easier.

## Fix

**Reader** — distinguish "no events" from "cannot read events":

- Parse the log tolerantly: `jq -rn --seq` style recovery is not enough with `inputs`, so either
  pre-filter with a line-oriented pass that drops unparseable records, or read with
  `jq -R 'fromjson? // empty'` so one bad line costs one record instead of the whole file.
- Count and surface what was dropped, e.g. `malformed records skipped: 3`, so corruption stays
  visible instead of being silently tolerated.
- Make a genuine read failure — missing file, unusable `jq` — report as unknown rather than zero.
  The report already prints `?` for GitHub delivery stages it did not measure; the same convention
  applied here would have made this obvious immediately.
- Remove `2>/dev/null` from both call sites, or route stderr into the diagnostic the helper prints.

**Writer** — make concurrent appends atomic:

- Locate every producer of this log (`git grep -n 'headless-runtime-metrics'`) and ensure each
  record is written with a single `O_APPEND` write of one line under 4096 bytes, or serialise the
  append with the repository's existing lock helper.
- If records can legitimately exceed `PIPE_BUF`, locking is mandatory rather than optional, since
  `O_APPEND` atomicity does not extend past that size.

Do not repair the three existing bad lines by hand as part of the fix; a tolerant reader makes that
unnecessary, and hand-editing an append-only audit log is worse than skipping three records.

## Verification

```bash
# Tolerant reader: real numbers, corruption disclosed, exit 0
worker-activity-helper.sh summary | head -20

# Negative case: an unreadable log must not report zeros
WAH_METRICS_FILE=/nonexistent worker-activity-helper.sh summary | head -10

# Writer: concurrent producers must not splice records
# (append from several subshells in parallel, then re-scan for malformed lines)
shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh
```

The decisive check is that a log containing a deliberately corrupted line still yields the correct
count for every other record, and that the report says so.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh` — `_wah_aggregate_metrics` at 272-340 (fail-open at
  326), `_wah_metric_details` at 353, summary printer at 728
- producers of `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` — to be enumerated with
  `git grep -n 'headless-runtime-metrics'`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — documents this helper as the starting point for
  worker triage, so the zero case is load-bearing guidance

title: feat(gh-write): anchored brief-section insert for supervisor brief repairs
body:
## What

Add a `gh-write-helper.sh issue brief-section <N> --repo <owner/repo> --anchor "<exact line>" --section-file <file>` action (or an equivalent helper). It fetches the live issue body, inserts or replaces one marked brief-owner section before an exact anchor line, keeps every other byte, and writes the result through the signed `_issue_edit_signed` path.

## Why

Terminal-blocker recovery (`reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`, steps 2 and 4) asks the pulse supervisor to make a "minimal issue-body revision" so the circuit re-arms. No helper does this:

- `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit` takes only a whole replacement body.
- The supervisor's OpenCode Bash forbids redirects, so it cannot save the live body to a file with `gh ... > file`.
- Retyping a long body by hand is unsafe. Consolidation-task bodies run past 30K characters and inline verbatim parent text that `consolidation-contract-validator.py` checks, so one changed character breaks validation.

In the 2026-11-19 pulse-sweep, the supervisor had to write an ad-hoc Python script to fetch the body, insert at an exact anchor and write a file. It then ran that script through a bounded operation for two awards issues: a 4K brief and a 35K consolidation-task brief.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: add the action and dispatch it in `main()`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`: fetch the body (`gh api repos/<repo>/issues/<N> --jq .body`), insert at the anchor with `awk` or `jq`, and fail closed unless the anchor occurs exactly once.
- Make the section idempotent with a `<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=... -->` marker. When the marker already exists, replace that section instead of adding a second copy.
- Optional `--scope-add "<line>" --after "<exact line>"` adds one Files Scope entry.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`: in "Terminal-blocker recovery" step 2, name the helper.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inserting at an anchor that occurs exactly once keeps the rest of the body byte-identical (diff the old and new bodies).
- [ ] An anchor that is missing or occurs more than once exits non-zero, with no write.
- [ ] Re-running with the same marker replaces the section; the body never gets two copies.
- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero violations.

## Verification

`shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. Then run against a disposable issue and compare the body before and after with `gh api ... --jq .body`.

**Task ID:** `t19134` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `performance` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(gh-shim): remove per-call bash forks from instrumentation, path resolution and cooldown preflight

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `gh shim fork overhead gh-api-instrument _gh_append_v2 command substitution performance` → 0 hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: prework-discovery found no open PRs or claimed issues on the target files; precedent #38896/#39002 (git-shim per-call cost) and #33062 (gh-shim REST overhead).
- [x] File refs verified: all target paths exist at `HEAD`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — mechanical, behaviour-preserving fork removal in hot-path shell helpers; existing focused tests cover record format.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (productivity mission: pulse/worker throughput)
- **Conversation context:** Host-load investigation of slow dispatch ceremonies (mean 231 s per launch). The runner averaged load 36–74 on 16 CPUs for five days, ~1,178 process spawns/s, with ~half of busy CPU in short-lived processes. Every `gh` call goes through the aidevops shim.

## What

Cut per-invocation bash forks in the `gh` shim hot path without changing any record, verdict or output:

1. `gh-api-instrument.sh`: `_gh_append_v2`, `gh_record_call`, `gh_record_attempt` and `gh_new_logical_id` sanitise each field through `$(...)` (one subshell fork per field, ~20 per record, two records per call). Assign through fork-free helpers (`printf -v`) instead. `_gh_now_ms` spawns perl twice per call; use bash `EPOCHREALTIME` when available, falling back to the current perl/python/seconds chain.
2. `gh-native-transport-lib.sh`: `_shim_canonical_path` runs `$(dirname)`/`$(basename)` per PATH candidate; use parameter expansion while keeping the `cd -P` physical resolution.
3. `shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh`: `_gh_secondary_cooldown_now` (`date`), `_gh_secondary_system_boot_ts` (`sysctl | sed | sed`) and file-path getters fork per call; use builtins (`printf '%(%s)T'`, bash regex) with the existing fallbacks.

## Why

Measured on the production runner (2026-11-19, 16 CPUs): one REST read costs 0.66 s wall / 58 ms CPU via native `gh` but 1.24 s wall / 391 ms CPU through the shim; an xtrace shows 102 bash forks per call, 39 of them in `_gh_append_v2`. The runner makes ~12,000 logical `gh` calls/hour (~3.4/s), so shim overhead alone is ~1.1 cores and ~0.6 s added latency per call on the dispatch critical path. Fewer forks lower host load (which inflates every Pulse stage) and shorten each ceremony gate.

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh` — fork-free field sanitisation and ms clock.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh` — `_shim_canonical_path` builtins.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh` — builtin clock/boot-time/path getters.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh` — shim startup path resolution without `dirname`/`basename` execs (added during implementation: 3 forks per call).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh` — REST timing via `_gh_now_ms_into`; skip `cat` of an empty error file (added during implementation).

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_gh_safe_text_into <var> <value> <fallback>` / `_gh_safe_number_into <var> <value>` (assign via `printf -v`), keep the stdout helpers for existing callers, and switch `_gh_append_v2` to them. Same for caller resolution and default pool/auth.
2. `_gh_now_ms`: if `EPOCHREALTIME` is set, derive ms with pure arithmetic; otherwise keep the current chain.
3. `_shim_canonical_path`: replace `dirname`/`basename` execs with parameter expansion (same `.`/`/` edge semantics).
4. Secondary cooldown: builtin `now`, regex-parsed boot time, direct variable reads.

### Hazards and Compatibility

Bash 3.2 must keep working (`printf -v` is 3.1+; `%(...)T` and `EPOCHREALTIME` need runtime guards with existing fallbacks). Log record bytes must stay identical (tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An xtrace fork count of one shim REST read (`PS4='+${BASHPID} ' bash -x .agents/scripts/gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .state`) drops from 102 to at most 60 distinct bash PIDs.
- [ ] Existing focused tests pass unchanged: `test-gh-api-instrument.sh`, the gh shim tests, and the secondary-cooldown tests; ShellCheck is clean on the three files.
- [ ] Negative/regression: log records (field order, sanitisation, enum allowlists) are unchanged, and Bash 3.2 (`/bin/bash`) still sources and runs the helpers.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh` — shim entry point.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh` — record-format tests.

title: t19136: fix(pulse-dispatch): parse macOS kern.boottime sec, not usec, so the post-boot dispatch ramp engages
body:
## Task


Make `_dispatch_ramp_system_boot_ts` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` return the real boot epoch on macOS when `_gh_secondary_system_boot_ts` is not loaded, so the dispatch boot ramp (default 180 s via `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DISPATCH_RAMP_BOOT_SECS`) actually applies after a reboot.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `kern.boottime usec boot ramp macOS` → 0 relevant hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue/PR covers the macOS boot-time parse (searched 2026-11-19).
- [x] File refs verified: paths below exist at `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — replace one sed pipeline with the already-reviewed builtin parse.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (found while implementing GH#39187)
- **Conversation context:** `sysctl -n kern.boottime` prints `{ sec = 1794166500, usec = 274703 } <date>`. The greedy sed `.*sec = ([0-9]+).*` matches the *last* `sec = `, which is inside `usec`, so it returns the microseconds (274703) instead of the boot epoch. GH#39187 fixes this in `_gh_secondary_system_boot_ts`; the Pulse dispatch fallback still has the same pipeline.

## What

Make `_dispatch_ramp_system_boot_ts` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` return the real boot epoch on macOS when `_gh_secondary_system_boot_ts` is not loaded, so the dispatch boot ramp (default 180 s via `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DISPATCH_RAMP_BOOT_SECS`) actually applies after a reboot.

## Why

With the boot epoch parsed as ~274703, `now - boot` is always huge, so the post-boot dispatch stagger never engages on macOS when the fallback path runs. After a reboot, Pulse can launch a full dispatch wave into a cold host and cold GitHub caches, which is the burst the ramp exists to prevent.

## Tier

`tier:simple`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:1529-1560` — `_dispatch_ramp_system_boot_ts` fallback branch.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace the `sysctl | sed | sed` pipeline (around line 1550) with the builtin parse that GH#39187 introduced in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh` `_gh_secondary_system_boot_ts`: capture `sysctl -n kern.boottime` once, then match `^\{[[:space:]]*sec[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*([0-9]+)`.
2. Optionally use the same `while read` loop for the `/proc/stat` `btime` branch (line ~1543) to drop the sed execs there too.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`

title: t19137: fix(pulse-dispatch): log the settled worker PGID after setsid instead of the pre-exec pulse PGID
body:
## Task


Make the launch log line in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` report the worker's settled PGID, and turn a genuine isolation failure into an explicit WARN.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `worker PGID setsid log race dispatch_worker_launch` → 0 relevant hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: no open or closed issue covers the launch-log PGID race (searched 2026-11-19).
- [x] File refs verified: paths below exist at `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — copy an existing bounded-await loop into one function.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (Pulse throughput investigation)
- **Conversation context:** All 400 most recent `[dispatch_worker_launch] ... worker PID=N PGID=M (setsid detached from pulse PGID=M ...)` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` show worker PGID equal to the pulse PGID, which reads as "worker isolation broken". Live `ps -o pid,pgid` shows those same workers (e.g. PID 2947, 16720, 25930) are their own group leaders (`pgid == pid`). Isolation works; the log samples too early.

## What

Make the launch log line in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` report the worker's settled PGID, and turn a genuine isolation failure into an explicit WARN.

## Why

`setsid nohup cmd &` forks a child that still has the pulse PGID until it execs `setsid` and calls `setsid()`. The `ps -o pgid=` read at line ~976 runs immediately after `$!`, so it almost always sees the pulse PGID. Every diagnostic session that reads this line concludes worker isolation is broken (the GH#21102 failure mode, where a pulse restart kills workers) and spends time disproving it. A real regression would also be invisible, because the line looks identical either way.

## Tier

`tier:simple`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:971-980` — the `setsid` branch of the worker launch.

### Reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:649-679` `_sandbox_await_child_pgid` (GH#38858) solves the same race: re-read the PGID up to 25 × 0.02 s until `pgid == pid` or the child is gone.

### Implementation Steps

**Task ID:** `t19138` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(worker-watchdog): defer no-output kills while the worker's isolated DB shows live tool output

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `watchdog no_output_stall tool output heartbeat isolated db` → 0 relevant hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue/PR covers DB-visible tool activity in the worker watchdog (searched 2026-11-19).
- [x] File refs verified: paths below exist at `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — kill-policy change in the worker lifecycle.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (worker throughput investigation)
- **Conversation context:** In 24h on one runner, 84 worker attempts ended in `watchdog_stall_*` (about 27 worker-hours). For 18 of them (about 8 h) the worker's bash tool was alive and printing a heartbeat every 2 s while it waited for a repository-level exclusive lock. OpenCode `run --format json` emits a tool event only when the tool part completes, so the output file the watchdog watches does not grow; tree CPU stays under 2% and there is no HTTPS socket, so none of the existing deferrals fire. The watchdog kills at 600 s, the session resumes, the lock queue position is lost and the wait starts again.

## What

Give `worker-activity-watchdog.sh` one more liveness signal: recent row updates in the worker's isolated OpenCode DB. While a tool runs, OpenCode rewrites the running tool part (`state.metadata.output`) as output streams; measured live, `part.time_updated` stayed about 1 s old while the heartbeat printed. On a confirmed output stall, a part update within the activity window defers the kill as `tool_output_active`, the same way CPU, network and CI-wait deferrals work. The hard-kill cap is unchanged.

## Why

Workers that are working (long tests, lock waits, builds that print) are killed and resumed in a loop, wasting slots and resume tokens and losing lock-queue order. The signal is exact: it reflects tool output and part updates, not a guess from CPU or sockets.

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` — new `--worker-db` arg, `_watchdog_db_part_activity`, deferral in `_monitor_handle_confirmed_stall`, classification in `_monitor_enforce_hard_kill`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh:425-430` — pass `--worker-db "${_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH}"` when set.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh` — a functional case for the new deferral.

### Reference pattern

- `_monitor_defer_stall "network_active" ...` in `_monitor_handle_confirmed_stall` (same file).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A quiet worker whose isolated DB has a part updated within the window is deferred with `tool_output_active`, not killed.
- [ ] A quiet worker with no recent part update and no CPU/network evidence is still killed at the stall timeout.
- [ ] Missing, unreadable or locked DB fails open to existing behaviour (no deferral, no error).
- [ ] Existing watchdog tests pass; ShellCheck clean.

title: t19140: fix(sqlite-transport): flush queued writes on process exit instead of discarding them
body:
## Task


Queued `sqliteExec` writes must land when the process exits normally. Today `hookProcessExit` in `.agents/scripts/sqlite-transport.mjs:55-61` calls `stopTransport`, which sends `SIGTERM` to the `sqlite3` child immediately after `stdin.end()` and sets `transport.queue = []`. Every write not yet acknowledged is discarded. The child is spawned lazily on the first write, so a one-shot run often kills it before it has opened the database.

Repro, deterministic on `main`:

```js
import { setDbPath, sqliteExec, sqliteExecSync } from "./.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs";
setDbPath(process.argv[2]);
sqliteExecSync("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t (n integer);", 5000);
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i += 1) sqliteExec(`INSERT INTO t VALUES (${i});`);
process.exit(0);
```

`node repro.mjs /abs/path/test.db`, then `sqlite3 /abs/path/test.db "SELECT count(*) FROM t;"` prints `0`; expected `20`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `sqlite transport exit queue observability llm_requests` → 0 relevant hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue or PR covers dropped queued writes at process exit (searched 2026-11-19).
- [x] File refs verified: paths below exist at `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — shared transport used by the plugin and scripts; needs care around exit ordering.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (worker throughput investigation)
- **Conversation context:** An error census of `llm_requests` read zero provider errors for a day with real failures. Cross-checking the OpenCode DB over 7 days found that root sessions with a single assistant message lose their `llm_requests` row 44% of the time when the request succeeded (124 of 284) and 88% of the time when it failed (61 of 69). Multi-message sessions keep 498 of 500 sampled messages. Short headless runs, and runs that fail on their first request, are under-reported.

## What

Queued `sqliteExec` writes must land when the process exits normally. Today `hookProcessExit` in `.agents/scripts/sqlite-transport.mjs:55-61` calls `stopTransport`, which sends `SIGTERM` to the `sqlite3` child immediately after `stdin.end()` and sets `transport.queue = []`. Every write not yet acknowledged is discarded. The child is spawned lazily on the first write, so a one-shot run often kills it before it has opened the database.

Repro, deterministic on `main`:

```js
import { setDbPath, sqliteExec, sqliteExecSync } from "./.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs";
setDbPath(process.argv[2]);
sqliteExecSync("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t (n integer);", 5000);
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i += 1) sqliteExec(`INSERT INTO t VALUES (${i});`);
process.exit(0);
```

`node repro.mjs /abs/path/test.db`, then `sqlite3 /abs/path/test.db "SELECT count(*) FROM t;"` prints `0`; expected `20`.

## Why

`llm_requests`, tool-call and runtime-event rows feed cost reports, routing feedback and worker diagnostics. Losing the final rows of short runs hides exactly the failures that matter most, such as entitlement rejections on the first request (see GH#39200).

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sqlite-transport.mjs` — the exit hook must flush, not discard. The `exit` handler is synchronous, so: (1) keep the SQL of the in-flight query on the transport (e.g. `transport.currentSql`); (2) in the exit path, collect in-flight plus queued SQL and run it once with `execFileSync("sqlite3", ["-cmd", ".timeout <ms>", dbPath], { input, timeout })`, using a bounded timeout of about 2–3 s so exit never hangs; (3) do not `SIGTERM` the child before that flush. Re-running the in-flight INSERT could duplicate a row the child already committed, so either end the child's stdin and let it finish on EOF without killing it, or flush only the never-sent queue. Pick one and document it.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/` — a focused regression in an existing sqlite-using test file (e.g. `test-runtime-events.mjs`), running the repro above in a child process and asserting all rows land.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/sqlite-transport.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-runtime-events.mjs`

### Reference pattern

- `sqliteExecSync` in `.agents/scripts/sqlite-process.mjs:119-130` (synchronous `sqlite3` invocation with timeout).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The repro prints `20` (all rows present) on 10 consecutive runs.
- [ ] Exit never blocks longer than the flush timeout when `sqlite3` is missing or the DB is locked (fails open with one stderr line).
- [ ] No duplicate rows for the in-flight query.
- [ ] Existing plugin tests that import `sqlite-process.mjs` / `sqlite-transport.mjs` pass (`node --test` on the files under `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/` that reference them).
- [ ] After deploy, one-assistant-message sessions are recorded at ≥95% (re-run the cross-check against the OpenCode DB).

</details>

**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(worker-lifecycle): accept pulse merge closeout marker as MERGE_SUMMARY evidence for merged worker PRs

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `merged_missing_summary MERGE_SUMMARY closeout worker false failure` → 0 hits.
