## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (worker throughput investigation)
- **Conversation context:** `~/.aidevops/state/objective-evidence.jsonl` holds 28 `worker_merged_missing_summary` attempt outcomes in the 24 h before 2026-11-19T09:50Z. Each is recorded `effective_outcome=failed`, `next_action=narrow_redispatch`, although the worker's exact-head PR merged and closed its issue. They are the largest share of the 49-row `other-failure` family in `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 24h`. `pulse-check-report.jq` excludes that family from autofiled findings, so no detector reported it. Public example: PR #38889 (issue #38850, closed as completed). Its comment `6960653803` was created at 20:51:32Z as the worker's `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->`. The deterministic merge closeout rewrote it at 21:22:58Z to `<!-- PULSE_MERGE_CLOSEOUT:PR#38889 -->` with the marker stripped, and the worker attempt was then recorded as failed.

## What

Accept the merge pass's closeout marker as evidence that the PR's MERGE_SUMMARY exists. A merged worker PR whose summary the merge pass already consumed should then resolve as `merged`, not `merged_missing_summary`.

## Why

`_pm_upsert_pr_closing_comment` (`pulse-merge-pr-closeout.sh:253`) rewrites the worker's MERGE_SUMMARY singleton in place, and `pulse-merge.sh:1867` strips the marker. After every deterministic merge, the worker's own post-exit probe `_pr_handoff_has_merge_summary` finds no marker. The probe then returns `merged_missing_summary` and the worker:

- records a false `failed` outcome with `narrow_redispatch`, which feeds failure families, terminal health, failure feedback and next-dispatch prompts;
- retains its claim (`headless-runtime-worker.sh:1867-1871`) instead of releasing it as `worker_complete`;
- for a signal-less exit, is routed to a premature-exit continuation instead of the post-PR handoff gate (`headless-runtime-result.sh:181-186`).

All of these cost worker attempts and metric accuracy on work that is already delivered.

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:212-223`. In `_pr_handoff_has_merge_summary`, count a comment whose body contains `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` or `<!-- PULSE_MERGE_CLOSEOUT:PR#<pr_number> -->`. Use a null-safe `(.body // "")` and cite this issue.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification-head-vs-search.sh:174-179`, `:404-429`. Let the `gh` stub print an optional `STUB_COMMENTS_JSON`. Assert that a merged exact-head PR whose only summary comment carries the closeout marker resolves as `merged|332`, and that a closeout marker for a different PR does not count.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification-head-vs-search.sh`

### Reference pattern

- `_pm_select_pr_closeout_comment_id` (`pulse-merge-pr-closeout.sh:91-130`) already treats the two markers as the same singleton.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification-head-vs-search.sh` passes, including the new closeout-marker assertions; the existing `merged_missing_summary` case (no summary and no closeout) is unchanged.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests-finish.sh` pass.
- [ ] ShellCheck reports no warnings for the changed shell files.

body:
**Task ID:** `t19142` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(pulse-check): size the daily apply routine's collection budgets so worker history and the queue scan complete; drop duplicate r-pulse-check

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse-check budget timed_out history queue coverage routine` → 0 relevant hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue or PR changes `pulse-check-helper.sh` budgets or the `r-pulse-check` routine (searched 2026-11-19).
- [x] File refs verified: paths below exist at `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. Mode-dependent defaults in one helper, plus removal of a duplicate routine entry.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (worker throughput investigation)
- **Conversation context:** r915 (`pulse-check-helper.sh apply`, daily 06:20) is the routine that should turn recurring worker failure families into self-improvement issues without a human. Across the last 13 runs in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-routines-tick.log`, the 24 h worker-history collector timed out at its 10 s component budget 6 times, including both runs on 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 (`"history":{"state":"timed_out","exit_code":124,"elapsed_seconds":10}`). The queue scan covered all 70 repos in only 2 runs; the latest covered 3/70 with `queue_budget_exhausted`. Every run ended `pulse-check: no autofile findings above thresholds`. The same 24 h summary completes in 3 s on an idle host but exceeds 10 s at 06:20 with 17/20 workers running. The routine is documented as `~5m` (`routines/core-routines.sh:936`), yet it runs with the interactive `report` budget (45 s total, 10 s per component, 20 s queue). Separately, the `marcusquinn/aidevops` `TODO.md` still holds a repo-local `r-pulse-check` entry (added with r915 in #26100) that runs the same `pulse-check-helper.sh apply` at the same slot, so pulse-check runs twice a day on this repo's host.

## What

1. Give `apply` (the scheduled routine) budgets sized for the routine: 300 s total, 60 s per component, 210 s queue scan (a full 70-repo scan measured 136 s on a loaded host on 2026-11-19; 210 s leaves ~50% headroom inside the `~5m` routine estimate). Keep `report`/`json` at 45 s / 10 s / 20 s. Explicit `--budget`, `PULSE_CHECK_REPORT_BUDGET_SECONDS`, `PULSE_CHECK_COMPONENT_BUDGET_SECONDS` and `PULSE_CHECK_QUEUE_BUDGET_SECONDS` still win.
2. Remove the duplicate `r-pulse-check` routine from `TODO.md`; r915 is the framework-managed entry that reaches every install.

## Why

When history times out, failure-family evidence is empty and nothing is ever autofiled. Recurring worker regressions then wait for a human to notice them in an interactive session, the dependency this routine exists to remove. Running the helper twice per slot doubles its API and CPU cost and lets two writers race on the same dedupe marker.

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh:34`, `:105-128`, `:151-153`. Leave `REPORT_BUDGET_SECONDS` empty unless set by env or `--budget`. After argument parsing, resolve it and new `COMPONENT_BUDGET_SECONDS` / `QUEUE_BUDGET_SECONDS` defaults from `APPLY_MODE`. `_run_json_helper` uses `${_PULSE_CHECK_COMPONENT_BUDGET:-$COMPONENT_BUDGET_SECONDS}`; `_scan_auto_dispatch_queue` uses `QUEUE_BUDGET_SECONDS`. Update `--budget` help text.

title: t19145: fix(ci): affected-test selection runs vacuous sourced modules instead of their parent suites
body:
## Task


`.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh:52-60` selects every `tests/test-*.sh` whose text contains a changed script's basename. Split suites keep their cases in sourced-only modules (header `# Sourced by ...`; 36 such files today). A changed library is usually named only in the module, so the module is selected and the runnable parent suite is not. Running a module on its own just defines functions: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests-recovery.sh` exits `0` with 0 output lines. The gate therefore reports a vacuous pass.

Make selection resolve each selected test file that another test file sources (`source`/`.` line naming its basename) to the root suite(s) that transitively source it, and run those roots instead of the module. Report each module→root mapping and every suite omitted by `--max` on stderr, so the CI step summary shows what did not run.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. One embedded Python selector change plus a stderr report.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive session (worker throughput investigation, GH#39209 follow-up)
- **Conversation context:** GH#39167 (`3baf2eeeb0`) changed `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` and `.agents/scripts/shared-pr-base.sh`. Its CI affected-test gate passed, but on `main` afterwards `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` aborted at `rc=1` before printing `Tests run`/`Failures`. Its orphan-recovery fixtures still stubbed `gh repo view` while the new resolver reads `gh api repos/<slug>` (fixed in GH#39209). Regressions like this reach workers and then need interactive sessions to diagnose.

## What

`.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh:52-60` selects every `tests/test-*.sh` whose text contains a changed script's basename. Split suites keep their cases in sourced-only modules (header `# Sourced by ...`; 36 such files today). A changed library is usually named only in the module, so the module is selected and the runnable parent suite is not. Running a module on its own just defines functions: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests-recovery.sh` exits `0` with 0 output lines. The gate therefore reports a vacuous pass.

Make selection resolve each selected test file that another test file sources (`source`/`.` line naming its basename) to the root suite(s) that transitively source it, and run those roots instead of the module. Report each module→root mapping and every suite omitted by `--max` on stderr, so the CI step summary shows what did not run.

## Why

The CI gate (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml:49`, `affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/${BASE_REF} --compare-base`) is the only automated test run for most PRs. A vacuous pass lets shared-library regressions merge green. Workers then hit them in production paths or red local suites, and interactive sessions have to diagnose them, which is the user-time cost aidevops exists to remove.

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh:50-64`. After computing `selected`, build a sourcer map over `tests`: for each test file, the set of other test basenames named on lines matching `^\s*(source|\.)\s+`. Replace each selected file that has sourcers with its root sourcers (files no other test sources), using a visited set against cycles. Print `module <m> -> <roots>` lines and an `omitted by cap: <names>` line to stderr.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh`

### Reference pattern

- Parent/module sourcing: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh:115` sources `test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`, which sources `-finish.sh` and `-recovery.sh` at `:793`/`:796`. Other examples: `test-gh-shim.sh:461`, `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:161` (sources via `${TEST_SCRIPT_DIR}`).

### Non-goals / known limits

- Transitive non-test sourcing (a changed library sourced by another script that tests name) stays out of scope: `shared-constants.sh` would select every suite.
- Per-suite timeout: the default `--timeout 240` is below the ~440s the headless parent suite takes locally. A suite that times out on head and base is classed `pre-existing`. Record a timeout as its own visible class only if it stays small; otherwise file a follow-up.

title: t19146: fix(pulse-merge): close PRs whose non-closing issue is completed and whose diff is empty or a stale planning row
body:
## Task


When the merge pass meets a PR whose only issue reference is non-closing (`For`/`Ref`) to an issue that is closed with `state_reason: completed`, close the PR with an evidence comment in either of two cases:

1. **Zero diff:** `GET repos/{slug}/pulls/{n}/files` returns `[]` at the pinned head. Main already contains the change.
2. **Stale planning row:** every changed file is `TODO.md` or `todo/**/*.md`, and the diff only adds task rows and briefs for that closed issue's task. Merging would plant an open row for finished work.

All other cases keep today's GH#38496 behaviour: label, comment once, and exclude from the backlog count. Never close when the issue closed as `not_planned`/`duplicate` but the PR has a non-planning diff, or when the head moved between reads.

## What

When the merge pass meets a PR whose only issue reference is non-closing (`For`/`Ref`) to an issue that is closed with `state_reason: completed`, close the PR with an evidence comment in either of two cases:

1. **Zero diff:** `GET repos/{slug}/pulls/{n}/files` returns `[]` at the pinned head. Main already contains the change.
2. **Stale planning row:** every changed file is `TODO.md` or `todo/**/*.md`, and the diff only adds task rows and briefs for that closed issue's task. Merging would plant an open row for finished work.

All other cases keep today's GH#38496 behaviour: label, comment once, and exclude from the backlog count. Never close when the issue closed as `not_planned`/`duplicate` but the PR has a non-planning diff, or when the head moved between reads.

## Why

These PRs stay open forever. Pulse re-evaluates them on every merge pass, spending REST calls, and a human has to find and close them. That is user attention the system exists to save. Today's rate: 1 of 24 plan PRs closed unmerged and 2 left open in 7 days, plus one worker PR.

```text
[SAFETY] worker PR body has ambiguous or missing explicit issue identity; keep one standalone `For #N` line; move other references under `## Related`.

<details>

## Task Brief

## What and why

Since 2026-11-06 every protected `TODO.md` publication from the Issue Sync workflow fails. The deterministic issue-sync planning PR is created with `--label origin:worker`. Its body has no standalone `For #N` line: the linkage section uses `- Ref #N` bullets, which the explicit-identity parser does not read. GH#36877 (`b910d5b91d`, merged 2026-11-06 09:58) added `_gh_validate_pr_worker_identity` to `gh_create_pr` for `origin:worker` bodies. It rejects this body before the PR exists:

Follow GH#37222 (`.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh:119-124`). title: t19153: fix(gh-failure-miner): mine failed post-merge and repo-level workflow runs from the Actions runs API

title: fix(terminal-blocker): window re-arm overrides a recorded human_decision on permission_required holds
body:
## What

A `permission_required` terminal-blocker hold is re-armed every backoff window (`unevidenced_permission_window`) even after the pulse brief owner has recorded `wake=human_decision` for it, re-held it with `status:blocked` + `needs-maintainer-input`, and posted the canonical ask. Each re-arm puts the issue back to `status:available`. Any later worker run can only end in the same block, and the next supervisor pass has to re-hold it again.

## Observed (private managed repo, issue `<N>`)

- Day 1: worker exits BLOCKED with `reason=permission_required`. The only files in scope are `.github/workflows/*.yml`, and the worker token cannot push `.github/**`.
- Day 2, 20:25Z: automated re-arm, `reason=unevidenced_permission_window observed_rev=X current_rev=X` (revision unchanged).
- Day 2, 20:54Z: the brief owner (pulse supervisor) posts the decision comment, sets `status:blocked` + `needs-maintainer-input`, and records `integration-recovery-helper.sh decision ... wake=human_decision`.
- Day 3, 14:04Z: another automated re-arm with the same reason and the same `observed_rev=X current_rev=X`. The issue goes back to `status:available` with no maintainer reply, no brief revision and no new worker result.

GH#36342 limits the window re-arm to "until that re-arm repeats the same result". Here no worker ran between the two re-arms, so no repeated result was ever produced, and the recorded `human_decision` did not suppress the second re-arm.

## Expected

A trusted brief-owner `human_decision` decision (or a brief-owner decision comment newer than the last re-arm) suppresses `unevidenced_permission_window` re-arms. Only the GH#38311 wake signals should release the hold: a plain OWNER/MEMBER reply, a brief revision, or a trusted retry directive.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: the `rearm` pass and its `unevidenced_permission_window` reason
- `.agents/scripts/integration-recovery-helper.sh`: the `decision` record that should be consulted
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`: "Terminal-blocker recovery", step 5

## Workaround applied

The supervisor added `no-auto-dispatch` alongside the decision so the loop stops. The cost is that the hold is now manual until a maintainer removes the label.

## Verification

Using a fixture issue with a `permission_required` observation, one window re-arm and then a recorded `human_decision`, the next `rearm` pass leaves `status:blocked` in place. A plain OWNER/MEMBER reply then releases it.

title: t19154: perf(gh-transport): revalidate explicit-pagination pages with ETags so unchan...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19154` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(gh-transport): revalidate explicit-pagination pages with ETags so unchanged comment lists cost no REST quota

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

Interactive productivity mission session (Pulse/worker throughput). Evidence from the local REST ledger `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` on 2026-11-19.

## What

Explicit REST pagination pages (route `explicit-rest-pagination`, issued by `.agents/scripts/gh-rest-pagination-lib.sh`) never send `If-None-Match`, so every page is a full-cost 200. Allow the conditional cache (GH#38566) to store and replay these page frames when replay is provably exact.

## Why

- In the 38 minutes from 14:15Z, the shim recorded 3,517 quota-costing REST attempts, against GitHub's 5,000/hour primary limit. 1,402 of them (40%) were `explicit-rest-pagination` with **0** 304 responses. Over the same window, ordinary governed GETs (`rest-response-owned`) returned 304 for 1,246 of 2,524 attempts (49%).
- The hottest paginated reads are issue-comment lists used by Pulse, dispatch dedup/claim, and the headless runtime (~740 attempts in that window). They change rarely between reads.
- Pulse's merge routine and dispatch defer at the REST progress floor, so wasted quota delays throughput directly.

Root cause: `_ghrp_build_base_args` adds `--include` to read the `Link` header, and `gh_conditional_request.eligible()` rejects all `--include` requests.

## How (Approach)

- `gh-rest-pagination-lib.sh`: mark page requests with `AIDEVOPS_GH_PAGINATION_INCLUDE_OWNED=1` only when the loop, not the caller, added `--include`.
- `gh_conditional_request.py`: page frames that the loop owns are eligible. A stored frame may answer a later 304 only if either:
  - it links onward (`rel="next"`), or
  - it is a final raw JSON array with fewer items than the effective `per_page`, which is the query value capped at 100, or 30 when no value is given.
  
  A 304 carries no `Link` header, and the list ETag tracks the page body. An unchanged full final page therefore cannot reveal a newly appended page, so such frames are never stored. Frames filtered with `--jq` keep the onward-link rule only. Field-encoded queries and notification endpoints use the same rule.
- `gh_conditional_cache.py`: in frame mode, store and replay the whole included stdout (headers plus body) so the page loop reads the original `Link`. Quota telemetry still comes from the real 304 headers.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-rest-pagination-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_conditional_request.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_conditional_cache.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A second identical paginated read of an unchanged non-full single page sends `If-None-Match`, gets a 304 at cost 0, and returns the same bytes.
- An unchanged full final page is never replayed (no truncation when a later page appears).
- A caller-requested `--include` stays ineligible.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh` and the pagination shim tests pass. ShellCheck reports nothing on the edited shell file.
- After deploy, the ledger shows a non-zero 304 count for `explicit-rest-pagination`.

</details>

title: t19157: feat(session-bus): issue watches relay worker/runner progress to interactive sessions; cross-runner who hint; worker dependency pointers
body:
## Task


Close three session-bus blind spots so interactive sessions and pulse workers see each other's progress:

1. **Issue watches (relay for interactive sessions):** a root session can watch `owner/repo#N` (issue or PR) for 7 days. The 2-minute relay sends it one batched `info` pointer per pass when a watched item changes status label, assignees, state (closed/reopened/merged), or gains non-bot comments (worker comments included). Issues filed by an interactive session through `claim-task-id.sh` are watched automatically.
2. **Cross-runner visibility:** when `who` finds no local session on `#N`/`PR#N`, it says that workers on other runners are not on this bus, and names the GitHub command that shows their claim. Watches report pickup by any runner as assignee and status changes.
3. **Worker-initiated pointers:** headless rules tell a worker to flag a dependency or overlap in a comment on its own issue, which watchers receive. When `aidevops sessions who` shows a live local session on the other item, the worker also sends that session a one-line `aidevops sessions send` pointer.

## Done when

- [ ] A live interactive session can `watch-issue` an issue or PR; headless sessions are refused; `--off` removes the watch; `watches` lists it.
- [ ] One relay pass sends one batched pointer per subscriber for status-label, assignee, state and new-comment changes, and nothing when nothing changed. A `--new` watch reports a pickup that happened before the first pass.
- [ ] `claim-task-id.sh` run from an OpenCode interactive session watches the issues it creates, and stays silent and non-fatal everywhere else.
- [ ] `who #N` with no local match prints the cross-runner hint.
- [ ] full-loop headless rules include the worker pointer rule.
- [ ] Regression guarantee: the existing worker relay behaviour, `watch-release` and the `test-session-bus.mjs` suite are unchanged and pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-issue-watch.mjs`: watch records under `issue-watch/<session>/<owner>@<repo>@<n>.json`. Covers add, remove, list and prune, reject headless subscribers, cap at 50 per session and expire after 7 days. Model on `session-bus-release.mjs`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs`: add `issueWatchDir` and prune watches in `pruneBusFiles`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs` + `NEW: session-bus-cli-watch.mjs`: add `watch-issue <owner/repo#N|#N> [--repo] [--new] [--off]` and `watches [--all] [--json]`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs`: add the `watch-issue` action and the who-miss hint.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs`: add the who-miss hint for the CLI.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh` (sourced) + `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh`: an issue-watch pass that makes one issue listing per repo, diffs labels, assignees and state against per-watch state, reads comments only when the count rose, and sends one batched message per subscriber.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`: best-effort `watch-issue <slug>#N --new` after issue creation (5 s budget, silent).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md` (Headless Dispatch Rules): add the cross-session pointer rule.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/session-bus.md`: document issue watches, the who hint and worker pointers.

### Verification

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs
shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh

aidevops sessions watch-issue marcusquinn/aidevops#39234 --new
.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh relay && aidevops sessions inbox
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs`

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19, interactive session (maintainer asked for every parallel-session blind spot found in a session-bus audit to be fixed: "work on all these gaps here. full-loop please").
- **Evidence:** #39234 was filed by this interactive session and then implemented and closed at 15:25Z by a worker on another runner (`vladimirdulov`). `aidevops_sessions who #39234` returned "No other live session is working on #39234", and the filing session got no bus notice. Workers can only answer an `ask` (`session-bus-format.mjs:110-116`), and no worker instructions say how to flag a dependency to a live session.

## What

Close three session-bus blind spots so interactive sessions and pulse workers see each other's progress:

1. **Issue watches (relay for interactive sessions):** a root session can watch `owner/repo#N` (issue or PR) for 7 days. The 2-minute relay sends it one batched `info` pointer per pass when a watched item changes status label, assignees, state (closed/reopened/merged), or gains non-bot comments (worker comments included). Issues filed by an interactive session through `claim-task-id.sh` are watched automatically.
2. **Cross-runner visibility:** when `who` finds no local session on `#N`/`PR#N`, it says that workers on other runners are not on this bus, and names the GitHub command that shows their claim. Watches report pickup by any runner as assignee and status changes.
3. **Worker-initiated pointers:** headless rules tell a worker to flag a dependency or overlap in a comment on its own issue, which watchers receive. When `aidevops sessions who` shows a live local session on the other item, the worker also sends that session a one-line `aidevops sessions send` pointer.

## Why

Interactive sessions file worker-ready issues, then lose sight of them. Outcomes and blockers from workers on other machines arrive only if someone polls GitHub. That wastes the human attention the framework is meant to save, and leaves follow-ups such as release sweeps or dependent work stalled.

**Task ID:** `t19158` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

perf(gh-transport): replay counted-list page frames (total_count) so unchanged check-run and status reads cost no REST quota

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

Interactive productivity mission session, follow-up to GH#39233 / PR #39238. Evidence comes from the local REST ledger `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` on 2026-11-19.

## What

PR #39238 lets the conditional cache replay explicit-pagination page frames in two cases: the frame links onward, or it is a final raw JSON array with room left. Counted-list endpoints return an object such as `{"total_count": N, "check_runs": [...]}` or `{"total_count": N, "statuses": [...], "state": ...}`. Their final pages never qualify, so every read stays a full-cost 200.

Add a third exact-replay rule. An unfiltered page whose JSON body is an object with an integer (non-boolean) `total_count` may be stored and replayed, whatever its length.

## Why

- Between 12:20Z and 13:40Z on 2026-11-19, the ledger recorded 5,723 quota-costing REST attempts, against GitHub's 5,000/hour primary limit. The 13:19Z and 13:36Z Pulse cycles then ended `blocked` on `rest-core-quota` with 0 dispatches (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`).
- In that window `pulse-merge-routine.sh` sent 692 explicit-pagination reads for `repos/:o/:r/commits/:id`, all page 1 and all full cost. The source is `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:728` (`commits/<sha>/check-runs?per_page=100 --paginate --slurp`). Check runs for a settled PR head are stable between merge-routine passes.
- Why this is exact: any added or removed item changes `total_count`, which changes every page body and therefore its ETag. A page that would need to reveal a new next page cannot be answered by a 304. Each requested page is still validated on its own.
- Live check: `commits/<sha>/check-runs?per_page=2` returned `total_count: 202` with `rel="next"`, and `commits/<sha>/status` returns `total_count` plus `statuses`.

## How (Approach)

- `.agents/scripts/gh_conditional_request.py`: extend `_final_page_has_room` (or add a sibling helper called from `page_frame_replayable`) to accept a parsed JSON object with an integer `total_count` that is not `bool`. Keep the existing guards: `_FINAL_PAGE_FILTERS` (`--jq`/`--template`/`--field` final pages stay ineligible, because the stored stdout would not contain `total_count`), the notifications exclusion, and the `per_page` validity checks. Update the module docstring to state the counted-list rule.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`: add cases modelled on the existing page-frame tests (`rg -n "page_frame|full final" .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`):
  - a full final counted-list page (`{"total_count": 2, "check_runs": [a, b]}` with `per_page=2`) is replayed on 304;
  - an object without `total_count`, and one with `"total_count": true`, are not replayed when full and final;
  - a `--jq` final counted-list page is not replayed.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh_conditional_request.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py` passes, including the new cases.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-batch-prefetch-conditional-rest.sh` pass.

- After deploy, ledger rows for `caller=pulse-merge-routine.sh`, `route=explicit-rest-pagination`, `endpoint=repos/:o/:r/commits/:id` show a non-zero 304 count.

title: t19159: fix(bounded-operation): completion-mode drain test reports failed under host load (GH#33747 test)
body:
## Task


Find out why a completion-mode bounded operation is reported as `failed` when its command exits 0 and leaves a SIGTERM-ignoring detached listener, then fix the root cause. The fix may be in the product or in the test's timing assumptions, whichever is wrong. The test must pass reliably under host load, and the GH#34047 receipt contract must hold: `post_exit_descendants_terminated` is true only for completion-triggered cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


1. In `completion` mode the manager sets `disposition = code === 0 && operation.commandStarted ? "succeeded" : "failed"` (`bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:237-246`). So either the supervisor exited non-zero or by signal, or the `command_started` IPC message (`bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs:52-65`, applied in `bounded-operation-termination.mjs:45-48`) had not been applied when `close` fired.
2. Leading hypothesis: under load, the post-exit drain of the detached listener (`ownedTreeDrained`, `bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs:111+`) escalates through `state.terminate` (`:84-95`). With `killGraceMs: 50` that path ends in `process.exit(1)` or the supervisor's own-group SIGKILL, not in an exit carrying the command's 0. Confirm this by logging `processExit`, `processSignal`, `terminationCause` and `commandStarted` on the failing receipt (`result.process_exit`, `result.termination_cause`, `result.command_execution`).
3. Reproduce under load. For example, run the single test in a loop while `yes >/dev/null` workers saturate CPU, or run the whole plugin suite with the validator's concurrency setting. Fix whichever side is wrong. Once the command has exited 0, escalating survivors must not change the command's success result. Alternatively the test's grace or wait budget is unrealistic and should scale the way GH#35499 did.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`: if the post-exit escalation path is the cause, preserve the observed command exit after survivors are escalated.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`: only if disposition depends on IPC ordering (for example, `command_started` applied after `close`).
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`: only if the cause is the test's timing (`killGraceMs: 50`, 3 s listener wait, 5 s terminal wait).

### Verification

```bash
cd .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops
node --test --test-name-pattern "detached test servers are drained" tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs
# Under load: repeat 20x while CPU is saturated; 0 failures expected.
npm run test
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-termination.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`

### Scope Boundaries

- Do not weaken the GH#33747 drain guarantee or the GH#34047 `post_exit_descendants_terminated` contract.
- Do not just raise validator concurrency limits or add retries; GH#39133 already covers concurrency.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19, interactive session (full-loop for #39240 / PR #39246).
- **Evidence:** `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` ran the plugin validator (`npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`) on a busy macOS host while parallel workers ran. One test failed: `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:419` "detached test servers are drained on completion, cancellation and expiry (GH#33747)". It failed after 1512 ms, at `:436`, with `AssertionError: 'failed' !== 'succeeded'` in `completion` mode. The same test passed when run alone (about 3.4 s), and the next full validator run passed. PR #39246 does not touch the bounded-operation modules. GH#35499 (t18764) and GH#39133 (PR #39135, merged 2026-11-19 03:44Z) already reduced plugin-test concurrency under host load. This failure came after that fix, so concurrency control alone does not cover it.

## What

Find out why a completion-mode bounded operation is reported as `failed` when its command exits 0 and leaves a SIGTERM-ignoring detached listener, then fix the root cause. The fix may be in the product or in the test's timing assumptions, whichever is wrong. The test must pass reliably under host load, and the GH#34047 receipt contract must hold: `post_exit_descendants_terminated` is true only for completion-triggered cleanup.

## Why

The validator runs before every full-loop PR. A flaky required test blocks PR creation, costs a full rerun (about 9 minutes here), and teaches sessions to dismiss real failures as flakes. If the product is at fault, a user operation can report `failed` after its command succeeded.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: a focused diagnosis across the supervisor, manager and test. It needs runtime reproduction under load, not new infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The failing receipt's cause is identified with runtime evidence (exit code, signal, termination cause, command evidence) and stated in the PR.
- The test passes 20 consecutive runs under CPU saturation on macOS.
- `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` passes.

</details>

body:
**Task ID:** `t19160` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-19
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): partial-continuation revisit walks past merged PRs that target a different issue

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

Interactive productivity mission session, 2026-11-19. Evidence from a read-only dry run and a guarded real-write drain of stranded `status:in-review` issues in a managed product repository (private; name withheld).

## What

`_pmpc_revisit_in_review_issue` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`) walks an in-review issue's merged cross-referenced PRs newest first. It skips PRs that close a sibling issue (GH#38869), but it stops at the first non-closing PR and hands it to `_pm_restore_partial_continuation`. When that PR only mentions the issue — `For #<other>`, a prose mention, or an `origin:interactive` PR about other work — the guard returns silently and the walk ends. The older worker partial that really targets the issue is never examined, so the issue stays `status:in-review` with no owner and no open PR.

Make the walk skip any merged PR that provably does not target the revisited issue, and stop only at a PR that closes or targets it (or whose metadata is unreadable or ambiguous). Bound the walk.

## Why

- One stranded issue's newest merged cross-reference was a PR whose body said `For #<other issue>` and only mentioned the stranded issue in prose. The walk stopped there, and the older partial for the issue was never revisited.
- In the product repository, 133 open `status:in-review` issues existed and 109 were not referenced by any open PR (sample median idle 1.1 days). A bounded drain that walks past silent guard returns restored issues through the unchanged `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` guard. Workers picked them up again, which Pulse would have done unaided if the walk were correct.
- Each such issue otherwise waits for a person to start an interactive session, which is the friction this framework exists to remove.

## How (Approach)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`:
  - Add `_pmpc_pr_may_own_issue <pr> <repo> <issue>`. It reads the PR body once and returns 1 (skip) when the PR closes another issue, or when its explicit `For`/`Ref` target is absent or another issue and its title cannot corroborate this issue (`^(t|GH#)<issue>`). It returns 0 (hand to the guard) when the PR closes or targets this issue, has a closing reference in an unparsed form, or any read is unreadable or ambiguous (fail closed).
  - In `_pmpc_revisit_in_review_issue`, replace the closing-only sibling check with this helper, keep the GH#38869 log line for skipped PRs, and cap walked PRs with `PULSE_PARTIAL_REVISIT_MAX_PRS` (default 10).
  - Leave `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` unchanged. It still re-reads all issue, PR and comment state and makes the decision.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`: add cases next to the GH#38869 block (`rg -n "GH#38869" .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`):
  - the newest merged PR is non-closing with `For #<other>`, and the older partial restores;
  - the newest merged PR's body is unreadable, so there is no restore;
  - the walk cap stops before an eligible PR beyond the cap.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` passes, including the new cases.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` reports no findings.
- After deploy, a Pulse revisit pass restores a stranded issue whose newest merged cross-reference targets a different issue. The evidence is a `kind=merged-partial-continuation` marker naming the older PR.

body:
**Task ID:** `t19162` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-19
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(full-loop): privacy pre-scan is stricter than the pre-push hook and blocks already-public content

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

Interactive productivity mission session, 2026-11-19. Evidence from three headless workers that finished a starter-template core sync, committed it locally, and were then blocked by the full-loop privacy pre-scan, so no PR was opened.

## What

Make `_commit_and_pr_privacy_scan` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` call `privacy_scan_public_diff` with the same public head (`$4`) and target slug (`$5`) that the authoritative pre-push hook passes (`.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh`, `rg -n "privacy_scan_public_diff" .agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh`). The pre-scan is meant to preview the hook before running expensive validators. Because it called the scanner with only three arguments, it had no public-tree exemption, so it blocked terms the target repository's own verified public default branch already contains.

## Why

- 2026-11-19: `wpallstars/seoprostack#1712`, `wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#220` and `wpallstars/seoprocustom#33` each synced core files from a public starter template, passed lint and smoke tests, committed, and stopped at `[privacy-guard] Scanning public diff before validators...` → `[privacy-guard][BLOCK]`. The workers correctly refused `PRIVACY_GUARD_DISABLE=1` and labelled each issue `needs-maintainer-input`, so each one waited on the maintainer for a false positive.
- Reproduced against the blocked seoprostack commit using the deployed helper:
  - three-argument call (the pre-scan): `rc=1`, 62 hit lines;
  - four-argument call with the target's public default tip (the hook's view): `rc=0`, 0 hits.
- Calling `_commit_and_pr_privacy_scan` itself on that commit: the deployed library gives `rc=1` (62 block lines); the fixed library gives `rc=0`.

## Scope decision

An earlier draft of this task proposed a new same-owner sibling-repo disclosure exemption in `privacy-guard-helper.sh`. Reproduction showed it is unnecessary: the existing target-tree exemption already clears this content once the pre-scan passes the same arguments as the hook. The guard's trust boundary does not change. The public head is used only when the target is verified public (`privacy_is_target_public`) and the fetch remote is the push target, the same condition the hook applies.

## How (Approach)

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_commit_and_pr_privacy_scan`: derive `target_repo` from the push URL. When the fetch URL resolves to the same repository, resolve `refs/remotes/origin/<base>^{commit}` as `public_head`. Pass both to `privacy_scan_public_diff`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` is clean.
- Existing suites pass: `test-privacy-guard.sh`, `test-privacy-guard-shim.sh`, `tests/test-privacy-diff-fast-path.sh`, `tests/test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh`. Terms absent from the target's public tree stay blocked, as already covered by the "Only a verified public tree" case in `test-privacy-guard.sh`.
- On the blocked seoprostack commit, the fixed `_commit_and_pr_privacy_scan` returns 0.
- After deploy, the three blocked starter-sync issues are released for redispatch and reach PRs without any guard bypass.

## Outcome

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

Interactive productivity mission session, 2026-11-19. While checking the maintainer decision queue for three blocked starter-sync issues, those issues did not appear in it.

## What

`maintainer-decisions-helper.sh list` (the `/decisions` queue) must spread its `--max` classification budget across every managed repo, so that no repo's holds are hidden by another repo's volume.

## Why

- `_md_list` sorted all discovered refs lexicographically (`refs=$(_md_discover | sort -u)`) and stopped after `MD_MAX` (default 300). With more than 300 open holds in the alphabetically first repository, every other repository's holds were never classified.

The queue exists to replace opening each issue, so a silently truncated queue leaves those holds waiting with nobody seeing them.

## How (Approach)

- `.agents/scripts/maintainer-decisions-helper.sh`:
  - Add `_md_interleave_refs`. It dedupes refs, orders them oldest issue first within each repo, and interleaves round-robin across repos (awk rank + sort; Bash 3.2 compatible).

title: t19164: fix(headless): resolve the OpenCode runtime profile through the profile document, not only AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE
body:
## Task


Headless worker code chooses the OpenCode runtime profile with the same resolver that setup and Pulse use (`aidevops_opencode_profile_id`). An explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` still wins. When it is unset, the `"default"` in `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json` decides, exactly as it already does for setup.

## Done when

- [ ] With `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` unset and a profile document whose `"default"` is `v2`, `_headless_opencode_binary_name` prints `opencode2`, the version validator expects major 2, and `headless-runtime-invoke.sh` inserts `--log-level warn`.
- [ ] Regression: with the shipped document (`"default": "v1"`) and the env var unset, the headless binary, validator major, log level (`WARN`) and model argument are the same as on `main` before this change. With `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1` and a v2-default document, the result is v1.
- [ ] Regression: the existing tests listed under Verification pass unchanged, and nothing on the headless path exports `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE`.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:1413-1415` — make `_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2` resolve through `aidevops_opencode_profile_id` when the env var is unset; add explicit returns
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh:272`, `:372` — call `_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2` instead of reading the env var
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:630` — same

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2` callers listed under Why (`rg -n "_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2|_headless_opencode_binary_name" .agents/scripts`). Direct env readers on the headless path: `headless-runtime-invoke.sh:272`, `:372`, `headless-runtime-model.sh:630` (`rg -n 'AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE:-v1' .agents/scripts`). Out of scope, and intentionally env-only because they describe the *current* runtime the `opencode2` shim exports: `gh-signature-helper-detect.sh:83`, `:124`, `aidevops-update-check.sh:33`, `:283`. Already document-aware: `setup/_services.sh:128`, `setup/modules/tool-install.sh:698`, `aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh:348`. `setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh:897` uses installed-binary detection by design (`tools/opencode/opencode.md:60-64`) and stays unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none. The profile is read-only here. Do not export a resolved value: an exported `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` would turn into an explicit override for child setup runs (`opencode-runtime-profile.py:95-104`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh` set `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` explicitly, so the explicit path must keep its current behaviour.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json` is read, not changed. `"default"` stays `v1` in this task.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`. No generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A, with evidence. The three edited sites only read `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` and the profile document through `opencode-runtime-profile.py get`/`default`, which has no write command (`opencode-runtime-profile.py:132-139`). No state file, database or config is written, so nothing persisted needs ordering or a backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** trivial revert of three files. With `"default": "v1"`, behaviour is identical before and after.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace `_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2` with an env-first, document-fallback resolver. Keep the explicit env var as the fast path (tests and the `opencode2` shim set it). Cache the document lookup in a non-exported variable so `python3` runs at most once per shell process:

```bash
_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2() {
	if [[ -n "${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE:-}" ]]; then
		[[ "$AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE" == "v2" ]] && return 0
		return 1
	fi
	if [[ -z "${_HEADLESS_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROFILE:-}" ]]; then
		if declare -F aidevops_opencode_profile_id >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			_HEADLESS_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROFILE=$(aidevops_opencode_profile_id 2>/dev/null) || _HEADLESS_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROFILE="v1"
		fi
		_HEADLESS_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROFILE="${_HEADLESS_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROFILE:-v1}"
	fi
	[[ "$_HEADLESS_OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROFILE" == "v2" ]] && return 0
	return 1
}
```

2. In `headless-runtime-invoke.sh:272` use `_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2 && log_level="warn"`. At `:372` use `_headless_opencode_profile_is_v2 || return 0`. In `headless-runtime-model.sh:630` derive `opencode_profile` from the same predicate. Confirm each file can see the function in its normal sourcing order (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:30` sources `shared-constants.sh`). If a file can run without `headless-runtime-lib.sh`, keep a local env fallback instead of a hard dependency.
3. If PR #39097 has merged by the time you start, also route `opencode2_oauth_pool_auth_available` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh` through the same predicate. Otherwise leave that file alone.
4. Run ShellCheck and the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** read-only lookup. No shared state. The cache variable is per shell process and is not exported.
- **Migration/rollback:** none needed. With `"default": "v1"`, every branch resolves to v1 as it does today. Revert is file-level.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1|v2` keeps its current meaning, so the `opencode2` shim, tests and existing opt-in installs behave as before. Without `python3` or the helper, `aidevops_opencode_profile_id` prints `v1` (`shared-constants.sh:247-258`). This is today's default.
- **Idempotency/retry:** pure function of env plus the profile document. A retried launch resolves the same profile.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the lookup fails, the result falls back to `v1`, which is today's behaviour. It never fails the launch.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh
# Runtime probe through the real resolver: write a copy of the profile document with "default": "v2"
# to a temp path, then with AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE unset, AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD/.agents" and
# AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE_FILE=<that copy>, source shared-constants.sh + headless-runtime-lib.sh
# and print _headless_opencode_binary_name (expect opencode2). Repeat without the override file (expect opencode),
# and with AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1 plus the v2-default copy (expect opencode).
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck and `--changed` cover the three edited files. `test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh` covers the resolver contract. `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` and `test-tool-version-check-opencode.sh` cover the explicit-env path, the validator major, and the log-level and argv shape (regression criterion). The runtime probe covers the positive and override criteria.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. There is no shared config, root tooling or release change.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: the runtime probe plus `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: headless profile resolves via profile document`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required (see above)

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change `"default"` in `.agents/configs/opencode-runtime-profiles.json`. Do not export the resolved profile. Leave the env-only readers that describe the current runtime unchanged (`gh-signature-helper-detect.sh`, `aidevops-update-check.sh`).

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

title: t19165: fix(gh-write): refuse an interactive PR comment that would stale a verified PR approval
body:
## Task


`gh-write-helper.sh pr comment <N>` checks whether PR N has a currently verified signed approval before posting. If it does, the helper refuses with exit 2 and a message pointing to the linked issue, where locked continuity tolerates trusted comments. An explicit `--allow-approval-stale` flag posts anyway. In both cases the PR approval state changes only when the caller asked for it.

## Done when

- [ ] Positive: `gh-write-helper.sh pr comment <N>` on a PR whose approval verifies exits 2 and prints the refusal that names the linked issue. The PR comment count is unchanged, and `approval-helper.sh verify pr <N>` still prints `VERIFIED` afterwards.
- [ ] Positive: the same call with `--allow-approval-stale` posts the comment.
- [ ] Regression: on a PR with no signed approval, or when verification errors, the helper posts exactly as before. `gh_pr_comment` callers outside `gh-write-helper.sh` are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh:282` — before `gh_pr_comment`, resolve the PR number and `--repo` from the arguments, the same way the `issue:edit` branch (`:240-252`) parses its target. Run `approval-helper.sh verify pr <N> <repo>`. On `VERIFIED` without `--allow-approval-stale`, print the refusal and return 2. Strip the flag before delegating.
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md` "Approval sequencing" — add one line: after a PR approval is signed, post later review notes on the linked issue, not the PR (pointer to `reference/auto-merge.md:75`).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `rg -n 'gh-write-helper.sh" pr comment|gh-write-helper.sh pr comment' .agents/scripts` finds `pulse-macos-verification.sh:34`. Check whether it can run after approval. If it can, decide with evidence whether it should pass `--allow-approval-stale` or skip. Pulse and other automation that source `shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh:1481` `gh_pr_comment` directly are not affected.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the only write is the PR comment POST, made by `gh_pr_comment` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh:1481`, which `gh-write-helper.sh:282` calls. The new guard adds a read (`approval-helper.sh verify pr`, which reads the comments, reviews and timeline APIs used by `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh:488-594`) before that write, and adds no write of its own. Approval comments themselves are written only by `approval-helper.sh` under `sudo`, which this task does not touch.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-verify-state.sh` covers the verify output contract. `approval-helper.sh verify pr` is the production check.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A, with evidence: no config keys. The flag is CLI-only, and `gh-write-helper.sh usage` must list it.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` and `.agents/workflows/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/`. No generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A, with evidence: the guard runs only at write time and stores nothing.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** trivial revert. An already-staled approval is re-signed with `sudo aidevops approve pr N owner/repo`, as today.

### Implementation Steps

1. Parse the target and repo in the `pr:comment` branch, using the `issue:edit` target-parsing loop as the pattern. Unknown or unparseable targets fall through to the current behaviour, so the guard never blocks on a parse gap.
2. Call `approval-helper.sh verify pr "$n" "$repo"` and capture stdout and the exit code. Treat only an exact `VERIFIED` as "approved". `STALE_APPROVAL`, unsigned or API uncertainty all post as today, because they have no approval to protect. Log one stderr line if verification errored.
3. Print the refusal: `PR #N has a verified signed approval; a new PR comment would stale it. Post on the linked issue, or pass --allow-approval-stale.` Then return 2.
4. Add the one-line rule to `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` "Approval sequencing".
5. ShellCheck, then run the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** approval can change between verify and post. That window only costs what happens today (a stale approval), so there is no new hazard.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. File-level revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** callers that do not pass the flag and target an approved PR now get exit 2. Only `pulse-macos-verification.sh:34` uses this path; handle it as described in the write surface. Unapproved PRs behave exactly as before.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a refused call has no side effects, so a retry with the flag is safe.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if verification fails (API error), the helper posts as today and warns on stderr. The guard fails open by design: it protects approvals and is not a security gate.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-verify-state.sh
# Production path, read-only: pick a PR whose approval verifies (approval-helper.sh verify pr <N> <repo> -> VERIFIED),
# then run gh-write-helper.sh pr comment <N> --repo <repo> --body-file <tmp> and expect exit 2 with no comment created
# (gh pr view <N> --json comments --jq '.comments|length' unchanged, and verify still VERIFIED).
# Repeat against an unapproved PR you own (or a dry-run stub of gh_pr_comment) and expect the normal post path.
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck and `--changed` cover the edited script and workflow. The production-path run covers both acceptance criteria. The verify-state test covers the verify output the guard parses.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change `gh_pr_comment` in `shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`, because automation depends on it. Do not change approval snapshot semantics.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (interactive maintainer session)

- [x] Duplicate search: `gh issue list --search "pr comment stale approval snapshot" --state all` found no equivalent. Related closed items are about specific canonical comment shapes (GH#36902, GH#38006), not a pre-write guard
- [x] File refs verified at `0a0095d5c9`: `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh:282`; `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh:183-275` (PR snapshot binds every non-bot comment); `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md:75`; `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md:243-262`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-19
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (observed failure during the maintainer re-review of PR #39097)
- **Evidence:** on 2026-11-19 an interactive `/review` posted a re-review with `gh-write-helper.sh pr comment 39097`. Before the comment, `approval-helper.sh verify pr 39097` returned `exact-snapshot` / `VERIFIED`; after it, `stale-or-unproven-continuity` / `STALE_APPROVAL`. Deleting the comment restored `VERIFIED`. The same text posted on the locked linked issue left both approvals verified.

## What

`gh-write-helper.sh pr comment <N>` checks whether PR N has a currently verified signed approval before posting. If it does, the helper refuses with exit 2 and a message pointing to the linked issue, where locked continuity tolerates trusted comments. An explicit `--allow-approval-stale` flag posts anyway. In both cases the PR approval state changes only when the caller asked for it.

## Why

`reference/auto-merge.md:75` already says "any non-bot comment stales the PR approval snapshot", but the review workflow tells reviewers to post reviews and comments on PRs (`workflows/review-issue-pr.md` "Approval sequencing", "CLI Commands"). After the maintainer has signed, one re-review comment silently invalidates a root-signed approval, and recovering it needs another `sudo` round. This is a deterministic rule, so it belongs in the write path, not in prompt text (`.agents/AGENTS.md` "Deterministic prompt rules should migrate to hooks/validators").

## Tier

`tier:standard`.

## Context & Decisions

- Issue approvals already tolerate trusted post-approval comments (locked continuity, GH#33089). PR approvals deliberately keep exact-snapshot semantics (`reference/task-lifecycle.md:298`), so the fix guards the write instead of relaxing the snapshot.

title: updown-helper.sh: private checks, update/recipients/status-page commands, API key off argv
body:
## Problem

`updown-helper.sh` resolves only one key, `UPDOWN_API_KEY` (`load_config`, `.agents/scripts/updown-helper.sh:43-67`). Operators who keep one updown.io account per site (for example, so each site can be sold or handed over with its own monitoring) store keys such as `UPDOWN_<SITE>_API_KEY` and cannot use the helper. OpenCode's Bash policy blocks setting the env var from a secret inline, so the interactive session had to write a one-off curl wrapper to create a check.

## Proposed fix

Add a key-secret override like `purelymail-helper.sh`'s `PURELYMAIL_TOKEN_SECRET`:

- `UPDOWN_KEY_SECRET=NAME` env and/or a global `--key-secret NAME` option; `load_config` resolves `NAME` through `aidevops_resolve_secret`, falling back to `UPDOWN_API_KEY`.
- Send the key as an `X-API-KEY` header read from stdin (`curl -H @-`) rather than in the URL query string, so it stays out of process arguments.
- Document the per-site pattern in `.agents/services/monitoring/updown.md` (or wherever the helper is documented; find with `rg -l updown-helper .agents`).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/updown-helper.sh`
- With two secrets stored, `UPDOWN_KEY_SECRET=UPDOWN_SITE_A_API_KEY updown-helper.sh list` lists only site A's checks; with no override, it still uses `UPDOWN_API_KEY`.
- `ps` during a call does not show the key.
