Each comment below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue with a wontfix rationale. **Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/39053 --- ### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule) This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `AGENTS.md` "AI-Generated Issue Quality"). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting. You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do analysis. #### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue 1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below). 2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a comment in this shape: > **Premise falsified.** \. \ actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>. > Not acting. No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next session reading this thread and the noise filter. #### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR 1. Verify the bot's premise as above. 2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement. 3. Open a PR with a `Resolves` closing reference in the body using THIS issue's actual number, not the source PR's, so merge auto-closes it. 4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate, merge, postflight). #### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply: the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision comment** with exactly these fields: - **Premise check:** one line, confirming the finding is real. - **Analysis:** 2-4 bullets on the trade-offs. - **Recommended path:** the option you would take if the decision were yours, with rationale. - **Specific question:** the single decision the human needs to make (yes/no or pick-one, not open-ended). Then exit `BLOCKED` as `input_required` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=maintainer` and stop; the answer in this issue body re-arms dispatch. Never label this issue or your own PR `hold-for-review`: nothing lifts it when the answer arrives (GH#36138). The human wakes up to a ready-to-approve recommendation, not a blank task. > **Ambiguity about scope or style is not Outcome C.** Per > `AGENTS.md` "Reasoning responsibility", the model does the > thinking and delivers a recommendation. Only escalate what is genuinely > a maintainer-only decision. ### Worker Guidance **Files to modify:** - _(No file paths in inline comments — see PR review summaries below for context)_ **Implementation steps (Outcome B path):** 1. Read the `diff` block under each inline comment below — it shows the exact code the bot was flagging. Open the file only if you need surrounding context beyond what the diff tail shows. 2. Read the bot's full comment below the diff — it contains the rationale and any suggested change. 3. Verify the premise before implementing (see Outcome A). If the premise is wrong, switch to Outcome A instead of burning iterations trying to satisfy a wrong suggestion. 4. If multiple comments target the same file, group your edits into one logical commit. 5. Run `shellcheck` / `markdownlint-cli2` / project tests as appropriate. **Verification:** - Open the new PR with `Resolves #` so this followup is auto-closed on merge. - If the bot's suggestion was incorrect, close this issue with a Outcome A comment — do not open a no-op PR. ### Inline comments _(none)_ ### PR review summaries #### coderabbitai[bot] review summary [View review](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/39053#pullrequestreview-5963661103) > > > > >
> Minor comments: 1

> > `230-231`: ** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Poor tradeoff** > > **Keep stale-cache demotion from delaying resumed-walk PRs.** > > The sort reads cached check state for demotion. `_pmu_pr_has_negative_verdict` receives the PR object from `_pmp_prepare_enriched_pr_backlog`, which reuses cached check rollups for any exact number and head match. A PR whose cached checks failed can still match its stored no-op fingerprint after its checks pass. The new `negative_priority` tier then sorts that PR after clean PRs. > > Demotion can also move the PR out of the resume lane's reach. `_pmp_resume_cursor_with_priority_lane` refreshes only candidates before the cursor. For example, with `[A, B]` and the cursor on B, A can be refreshed and promoted. After demotion the order becomes `[B, A]`. B is now at index 0, so the lane finds no candidate before the cursor and A is not refreshed. If the pass budget runs out on B, the cursor stays on B, and A is not evaluated in that pass. The same order can recur on the next resume. > > The effect is limited to paused walks. A completed walk clears the advisory cache. > > Preserve bounded refresh eligibility for demoted candidates, or validate their advisory check state before applying the demotion. title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #31068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

**Task ID:** `t19205` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-20
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(setup): reinstall the systemic CI failure miner on pulse hosts during non-interactive setup

## Done when

- [ ] Non-interactive setup installs the miner on a pulse-enabled host where it is absent.
- [ ] Hosts with pulse disabled still do not get the miner.
- [ ] Failed default-branch push runs older than the newest 100 repository runs are mined.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh`
- `setup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t19205-brief.md`

### Implementation Steps

1. In `.agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh`, add `_should_setup_noninteractive_failure_miner`, modelled on `_should_setup_noninteractive_stats_wrapper` / `_should_setup_noninteractive_complexity_scan`: return 0 when the miner is installed on any backend, else when `_should_setup_noninteractive_supervisor_pulse` returns 0.
2. In `setup.sh` non-interactive scheduler block, replace the generic `_should_setup_noninteractive_scheduler "Failure miner" ...` call with the new helper.
3. `setup_failure_miner` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh`) already installs only when `PULSE_ENABLED` is `true` and uninstalls otherwise, so no change is needed there.
4. Discovered during verification: a dry run over the outage window found no cluster. `emit_workflow_run_events` read one unfiltered page of 100 runs, but aidevops had 2,500 runs in 11 h, so the page covered ~25 minutes. Add `fetch_repo_level_runs_json`, which queries only the events `select_current_workflow_failures_json` keeps (`push` with `branch=<default>`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`, `issues`, `pull_request_target`), server-side, merged and de-duplicated by run ID.

### Verification

- `shellcheck setup.sh .agents/scripts/setup/_runtime_helpers.sh .agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-failure-miner-signature-noise.sh` (GH#39228 selection assertions unchanged)
- `gh-failure-miner-helper.sh collect --repos marcusquinn/aidevops --since-hours 11` lists the failed default-branch `review-bot-gate.yml` push runs.
- `setup.sh --non-interactive` on a pulse host without the miner plist installs `sh.aidevops.routine-gh-failure-miner` (`launchctl list | rg gh-failure-miner`).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- Created: 2026-11-20, interactive aidevops throughput session.
- Evidence: the `review-bot-gate.yml` outage (merged 05:29Z by #39427, fixed 15:14Z by #39460) blocked every aidevops merge for ~9.5 h. It was first reported by an interactive session at 14:50Z (#39458); no automated issue was filed.

## What

Give the systemic CI failure miner (`sh.aidevops.routine-gh-failure-miner` / `aidevops-gh-failure-miner`) the same pulse-dependency escape hatch that stats-wrapper (t2418, GH#20016) and complexity-scan (GH#24841) already have. Non-interactive setup (`aidevops update`) currently reinstalls the miner only if it is still installed, so an install that lost it once never gets it back.

## Why

- On the maintainer runner the miner last ran 2026-04-08 (`~/.aidevops/logs/routine-gh-failure-miner.log` mtime); its plist is absent while the supervisor pulse, stats-wrapper and every other pulse-owned scheduler are installed.
- Until then it filed `Systemic CI failure: <workflow> (N events)` auto-dispatch issues hourly (threshold 2).
- Today both default-branch push runs of `review-bot-gate.yml` (05:29Z, 05:43Z) failed and stayed the newest runs, which meets the miner's selection rule (`select_current_workflow_failures_json`) and threshold.
- Pulse's per-PR zero-job remediation (`pulse-merge-rest-state.sh` `_pmrs_rerun_zero_job_run`) only logged `rerun request failed ... no further automatic reruns` on five PRs.

## Tier

tier:standard — one helper function plus one call-site change, following an existing in-file pattern.

title: t19207: secretlint-helper: add content-free summary mode (scanned/excluded/rule counts) for AI sessions
body:
Secretlint JSON output embeds full file contents; add a safe summary mode. See brief.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add a content-free Secretlint summary mode to `secretlint-helper.sh` that runs with the repository's own `.secretlintrc.json` and `.secretlintignore` but returns only scanned file paths, excluded paths and per-file rule IDs and counts. Also stop advertising raw `json` output as a normal AI-facing format.

## Why

An aidevops user asked whether there is a supported way for an AI session to have Secretlint use protected configuration internally and verify scanned or excluded files while seeing only safe summaries. There is no such mode today.

Evidence (checked locally with secretlint 11.7.1 and a throwaway benign fixture; the CLI shape is the same in 13.x):

- `@secretlint/formatter` `formatters/json.js` returns `JSON.stringify(results)`. Each result includes `sourceContent`, so `secretlint-helper.sh scan . json` (the example in `show_help`) prints the full contents of every scanned file.
- Secretlint's `DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS` (`secretlint/module/search.js`) contains `**/.secretlintignore*/**`, which matches directories only. The `.secretlintignore` file itself is therefore scanned, and its contents appear in JSON output.
- The CLI has no list-files or dry-run option. JSON `filePath` entries are the only record of what was scanned. Exclusions have to be worked out as candidates minus scanned.
- The source-access broker (`source_access_core.py` `ALLOWED_SUFFIXES`) correctly refuses `.secretlintignore`. It exists to put approved source into AI context, so it is the wrong tool for this.

## How

- Add a `summary` (or `scan-summary`) command to `.agents/scripts/secretlint-helper.sh`. It should:
  - run `secretlint <target> --secretlintrc .secretlintrc.json --secretlintignore .secretlintignore --format json` and pipe the output straight through `jq`, keeping only `filePath` (made relative to the repo), `messages | length` and the unique `ruleId` values. Never emit `sourceContent`, `message`, `data` or ranges.
  - compute `excluded = candidates − scanned`, with candidates from `git ls-files` (plus `rg --files --hidden` for untracked files when asked). Report the counts and the excluded path list.
  - keep the existing 0/1/2 exit-code contract. If the scanner exits 2, report a fatal error and do not print a summary that looks clean.
- In `show_help` and `.agents/tools/code-review/secretlint.md`, warn that `json` output contains file contents and point AI sessions to `summary`.
- Reference pattern: the jq-based count reading in `show_status` (`rules_count`, `ignore_count`), which already reports configuration metadata without contents.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/secretlint-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/code-review/secretlint.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-config-boundary.py`

## Acceptance

- `secretlint-helper.sh summary` on a fixture with an ignored file lists the ignored file under excluded and never includes the contents of any file, including `.secretlintignore`.
- A fixture with a synthetic finding reports the file and rule ID, and exits 1, with no secret value or masked excerpt in the output.
- Missing configuration still exits 2 without writing files (the existing `test-scan-config-boundary.py` contract).

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-config-boundary.py`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/secretlint-helper.sh`

</details>

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

title: t19208: fix(ci): scheduled shell-suite main health run classifies 156 suites red and cannot file from Actions (privacy guard)
body:
## Task


Make the scheduled main shell-suite health job produce trustworthy, filed findings. Today it (a) classifies 156 root suites as `regression` on `main`, which is implausible while PR CI on `main` is green, and (b) cannot file any issue from GitHub Actions. If (b) were "fixed" without (a), one run would open 156 auto-dispatch `red-main:` issues.

## Done when

- [ ] A `workflow_dispatch` run on `main` reports only reproducible regressions (green when `main` is green), with the TSV artifact attached.
- [ ] More than the bound of red suites produces at most one aggregated finding.
- [ ] No issue write runs inside GitHub Actions; a persistently failing scheduled run is filed by the host-side miner.
- [ ] ShellCheck/actionlint clean; miner tests pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Worker Quick-Start

1. Read `.github/workflows/shell-suite-main-health.yml` (suite run lines 46-94, filing step 96-276).
2. Read `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh` `all` mode (the `suite rc_head rc_base class` TSV and the `regression` class).
3. Read `privacy-guard-helper.sh` `privacy_guard_public_write` to see why CI writes are refused.
4. Read `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh` `select_current_workflow_failures_json` / `fetch_repo_level_runs_json` (GH#39466). This host-side miner files auto-dispatch issues for failing `schedule` runs, using the privacy inventory.

### Implementation Steps

1. Upload `suite-results.tsv` and `suite-stderr.log` as a short-retention artifact, so each red classification is inspectable.
2. Reproduce and fix the mass classification. Check exit-code distribution (124 = per-suite timeout under `--jobs 4 --timeout 180`), runner tool gaps (a suite needing a tool the runner lacks is an environment gap, not a regression), and whether `rc_base` is computed.
3. Add a storm bound: above a small threshold (for example 10 regressions), report one aggregated finding, never per-suite issues.
4. Move filing out of CI. Remove the `SYNC_PAT` filing step and let the job fail with the summary and artifact. Filing then happens where the privacy inventory exists: the gh-failure-miner on pulse hosts (GH#39466). Because a daily schedule yields one event per 24 h window, let a `schedule` workflow whose newest run failed count as systemic at threshold 1 in the miner, or document an equivalent host-side path.

### Hazards

- Never bypass, stub or disable the privacy guard in CI, and never ship a private-repo inventory to Actions.
- Never let a single run create more than one aggregated issue.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/shell-suite-main-health.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-failure-miner-signature-noise.sh`

</details>

## Origin

- Created: 2026-11-20, interactive aidevops throughput session, while verifying the systemic CI failure miner fix (GH#39466).
- Evidence: first scheduled run of `.github/workflows/shell-suite-main-health.yml` (t19150, #39307): run 44731141317, 2026-11-20 11:52Z, conclusion failure.

## What

Make the scheduled main shell-suite health job produce trustworthy, filed findings. Today it (a) classifies 156 root suites as `regression` on `main`, which is implausible while PR CI on `main` is green, and (b) cannot file any issue from GitHub Actions. If (b) were "fixed" without (a), one run would open 156 auto-dispatch `red-main:` issues.

## Why

- The run log shows `##[warning]156 red suite(s) on main` and 156 `failed to create issue for red-main: <suite>` errors.
- Each creation was blocked by `[privacy-guard][BLOCK] Private entity inventory could not be loaded.` (`privacy-guard-helper.sh` `privacy_guard_public_write`, ~line 591). A public-repo write needs the private-entity inventory from `repos.json`, which only exists on maintainer hosts. This fail-closed control is correct and must not be weakened.
- The diagnostic loop hit `diagnostic budget exhausted`, so most suites have no captured lines. The results TSV goes only to the step summary, and the run has no artifacts.

## What

After PR #39097, two independent checks decide whether an OAuth pool account can authenticate a provider:

- `_resolve_oauth_pool_available` in `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh` (model availability probe, Source 5).
- `opencode2_oauth_pool_auth_available` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh` (headless worker model selection).

Each resolves its own pool file and applies its own status rule. This task makes both call one shared implementation, so that:

1. Both read the pool file the active runtime actually authenticates from.
2. Both apply the same allowlist of runnable account states.
3. Source 5 applies only when OpenCode `auth.json` is absent, matching the headless check.

## Why

The three CodeRabbit threads on PR #39097 (resolved as deferred to this task) identify cases where availability and runtime disagree:

- **Pool-file override:** `oauth-pool-helper.sh:37` and the V1 runtime honour `AIDEVOPS_OAUTH_POOL_FILE`; `_resolve_oauth_pool_available` reads only `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE` or the default path.
- **Non-runnable statuses:** `provider-auth.mjs:286` writes `status: "billing-error"`. The availability predicate accepts it (it rejects only `auth-error` and cooling `rate-limited`), so the probe records healthy and skips HTTP. The runtime selects only `active`/`idle` accounts without an active cooldown (`provider-auth-pool.mjs:59-64`).
- **V2 root:** the generated V2 shim resolves the pool as `${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_OAUTH_POOL_FILE:-${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT:-$HOME/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2}/auth/oauth-pool.json}` (`setup/modules/tool-install.sh:1061`, `:1074`). The headless check ignores `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT`.

None of these regress V1 today, but switching the default profile to V2 (#35902) would expose the pool split to every user.

title: consolidated: share OAuth pool resolver and usability rule between model availability and headless auth
body:
_Supersedes #39352 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

**Task ID:** `t19183` | **Estimate:** `~1h20m` | **Tags:** `bug` `auto-dispatch`

## What

Share one runtime OAuth pool resolver and one usability rule between model availability (`_resolve_oauth_pool_available` in `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`, Source 5) and headless auth (`opencode2_oauth_pool_auth_available` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh`). Both must:

1. Read the pool file the active runtime actually authenticates from.
2. Apply the same allowlist of runnable account states.
3. Apply Source 5 only when OpenCode `auth.json` is absent, matching the headless check.

## Why

Review of PR #39097 (closed #39095) deferred three findings to this task; availability and runtime disagree in each:

- **Pool-file override:** `oauth-pool-helper.sh:37` and the V1 runtime honour `AIDEVOPS_OAUTH_POOL_FILE`; `_resolve_oauth_pool_available` reads only `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE` or the default path.
- **Non-runnable statuses:** `provider-auth.mjs:286` writes `status: "billing-error"`. The availability predicate accepts it (rejects only `auth-error` and cooling `rate-limited`), so the probe records healthy and skips HTTP. The runtime selects only `active`/`idle` accounts without an active cooldown (`provider-auth-pool.mjs:59-64`).
- **V2 root:** the generated V2 shim resolves `${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_OAUTH_POOL_FILE:-${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT:-$HOME/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2}/auth/oauth-pool.json}` (`setup/modules/tool-install.sh:1061`, `:1074`). The headless check ignores `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT`.

No V1 regression today, but switching the default profile to V2 (#35902) would expose the split to every user.

## How

### Implementation steps

1. Create `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-usable-lib.sh` (SPDX header and include guard modelled on `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh`) with two pure, read-only functions:
   - `oauth_pool_runtime_file`: echo the active runtime's pool file. Resolve the profile with `aidevops_opencode_profile_id` (`shared-constants.sh:247`), defaulting to `v1` if the function is undefined or fails; never read `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` directly (#39276 owns headless profile resolution). `v2` → `${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_OAUTH_POOL_FILE:-${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT:-$HOME/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2}/auth/oauth-pool.json}`; otherwise `${AIDEVOPS_OAUTH_POOL_FILE:-$HOME/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json}`.
   - `oauth_pool_has_usable_account PROVIDER POOL_FILE`: exit 0 when at least one account is runnable. Allowlist (matches `provider-auth-pool.mjs:59-64` plus expired rate-limit normalisation): status missing/active/idle with no active cooldown, or `rate-limited` whose cooldown has expired. Everything else (`auth-error`, `billing-error`, unknown) is not runnable. Missing file, missing jq, malformed JSON or a non-array provider entry return 1. Never print credential material. Every function needs explicit `return 0`/`return 1` and `local var="$1"` style.
2. `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`: source the lib next to the other `source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/..."` lines (`:502`, `:506`). `_resolve_oauth_pool_available` computes `pool_file="${MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE:-$(oauth_pool_runtime_file)}"` (override stays first) and returns `oauth_pool_has_usable_account "$provider" "$pool_file"`. In `resolve_api_key`, run Source 5 only when `${HOME}/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` does not exist.
3. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh`: source the lib; in `opencode2_oauth_pool_auth_available` keep the `[[ -f "$auth_file" ]] && return 1` gate and replace the inline pool path selection and python predicate with the two lib calls.
4. Update `.agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-oauth-pool-gate.sh` only where existing cases pin the old resolution or status behaviour.

### Complete write surface

- **Callers:** `resolve_api_key` (model-availability-helper.sh) and `provider_auth_available` (headless-runtime-provider.sh:133) are the only callers. `headless-runtime-provider.sh` is sourced by `headless-runtime-lib.sh:138` and `ai-research-helper.sh:30`; both set `SCRIPT_DIR` and load `shared-constants.sh`.
- **Writers:** none; both functions are read-only. Pool writers (`oauth-pool-helper.sh`, the plugin) are unchanged.
- **Existing tests:** `test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-oauth-pool-gate.sh`, `test-headless-provider-round-robin.sh`, `test-ai-research-helper-oauth-pool.sh`.
- **Schema:** pool JSON per `oauth-pool-storage.mjs:30` (`status` ∈ active|idle|rate-limited|auth-error; `billing-error` is written at `provider-auth.mjs:286` but is not in the typedef). No change.
- **Deployment:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`; the new lib ships with them, no manifest change.
- **Migrations:** none (no stored state changes shape). **Rollback:** revert the PR.

### Hazards and compatibility

- Read-only JSON reads; a concurrent plugin write can at worst give a malformed read, returning 1 for one probe, as today.
- Keep `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE` as highest-priority override. V1 users without override get the same path as before; V2 users without `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT` get the same path as before.
- Pure functions, idempotent. If python3 or the profile helper is missing, default to `v1`.
- Complexity: `opencode2_oauth_pool_auth_available` shrinks from ~47 to ~12 lines; no action required.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-usable-lib.sh .agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-oauth-pool-gate.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-provider-round-robin.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-ai-research-helper-oauth-pool.sh
# Production path, sandboxed HOME with no auth.json and one billing-error account:
#   model-availability-helper.sh probe anthropic --force  -> no key (not healthy)
```

Broad verification is not required.

### Scope boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change pool writers, the plugin JS, or setup's shim generation. Do not change headless profile resolution beyond calling `aidevops_opencode_profile_id` (#39276 owns that).

**AI brief owner:** maintainer interactive session that filed #39352. **Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both checks call `oauth_pool_has_usable_account` and `oauth_pool_runtime_file` from the new lib.
- [ ] With `AIDEVOPS_OAUTH_POOL_FILE` pointing at a pool with one `active` anthropic account and no `auth.json`, the availability probe reports anthropic healthy. With `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v2` and `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_ROOT=<dir>`, the headless check reads `<dir>/auth/oauth-pool.json`.
- [ ] Negative regression: each check rejects a pool whose only anthropic account is `billing-error` (any cooldown), and Source 5 is never consulted when `auth.json` exists.
- [ ] The four suites listed under Verification pass, and ShellCheck is clean on changed files.

PR conventions: leaf task, PR body uses `Resolves` with this issue's number; reference the parent with `For #35902`.

## Context & Decisions

- Allowlist, not denylist: unknown future statuses fail closed, as the runtime does (per @marcusquinn, parent brief).
- `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE` keeps priority so existing tests and operator overrides are unchanged.
- Source 5 gating on `auth.json` absence was review finding P2 on PR #39097; it aligns availability with headless selection.
- Ruled out: deriving eligibility from `opencode auth list` (OpenCode 2 store); unnecessary once both checks agree.
- Dependency #39095 is closed via PR #39097 (v3.39.248), so the target functions exist on main. The earlier hold on #39352 was a false positive of `check_terminal_blockers` Pattern 4, fixed by PR #39454 (GH#39452); per @marcusquinn, no real blocker remains.
- Fix-the-fixer classification (per @alex-solovyev, t3077): this edits `headless-runtime-provider.sh`, sourced by `headless-runtime-lib.sh:138`, so workers run with extra observability.
- Parent #35902 (OpenCode 2.x migration-readiness) is blocked on this for the V2 default-profile switch.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

### Files Scope

- NEW: .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-usable-lib.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-oauth-pool-gate.sh

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #31068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

title: t19209: fix(terminal-blocker): trigger revisit starves holds beyond the first
body:
**Task ID:** `t19209` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-20
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(terminal-blocker): trigger revisit starves holds beyond the first

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


Issue: GH#39481

## What

`terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh` never reaches most `external_trigger_pending` holds in a repository with many holds. Satisfied triggers therefore stay `status:blocked` until a human starts an interactive session to recount and close them. Make every hold get revisited: walk the candidates least-recently-checked first, and memoize ineligible hits so they stop consuming reads every pass.

## Why

Observed on one pulse runner, against a managed repository with 45 open issues that match the owner search `"Terminal blocker: reason=external_trigger_pending"`:

- The pulse stage `trigger_revisit` runs with a 72s timeout. That gives the helper a budget of about 50–62s per pass (`pulse-stage-timings.log`: 49–63s every pass, 15 passes over 20h).
- `_tbtr_repo` walks the refs in search "best match" order, which is stable from pass to pass. Every pass spends its reads on the same leading hits and hits the deadline at around position 12–20.
- Ineligible hits are re-read every pass and never recorded. These are inactive holds, holds of another reason class, and legacy observations. Each one costs an issue fetch plus a paginated comments fetch (about 2.3–2.8s measured).
- The runner's record directory had no record for 27 of the 45 holds. Since 2026-11-18, records were written only for hits at positions 20 or earlier.
- Concrete loss: one hold at position 21 had a trigger of "one day after PR X merged, then recount". That trigger was met for about 21h and the hold was never revisited. An interactive session had to verify the trigger and close the issue by hand.

## How

1. `_tbtr_issue`: after a successful read that proves the hit ineligible, write a memo record `{updated_at, next_at: now+interval, decision: "ineligible", checked_at}`. Ineligible means closed/`needs-maintainer-review`, no observation, another reason class, or hold inactive (rc 1). Transient fetch failures and rc 2 stay unrecorded.
2. Stamp `checked_at` on scheduled and ineligible records; decided records already carry `revisited_at`.
3. `_tbtr_repo` → `_tbtr_order_refs`: stable-sort the refs by `checked_at // revisited_at // 0`, oldest first.
4. `tbtr_next_due`: ignore `ineligible` memos.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh` is clean.

title: t19210: fix(terminal-blocker): external_trigger_pending holds publish dependency guidance that names a nonexistent linked blocker
body:
## Task


An `external_trigger_pending` hold publishes the wrong "why". The circuit comment pairs the hold with `Unblock label: needs-dependency` and that label's generic guidance: "Needed: the linked blocking issue must close. Owner: whoever solves that issue (usually a worker). Afterwards the dependency pass removes status:blocked and this label automatically." None of that is true for a trigger hold. There is no linked blocking issue, and the dependency pass never clears the hold. The trigger-revisit pass (`terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh`) or an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive clears it. Publish reason-accurate guidance so neither a human nor an AI reader goes looking for a blocker that does not exist.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

An `external_trigger_pending` hold publishes the wrong "why". The circuit comment pairs the hold with `Unblock label: needs-dependency` and that label's generic guidance: "Needed: the linked blocking issue must close. Owner: whoever solves that issue (usually a worker). Afterwards the dependency pass removes status:blocked and this label automatically." None of that is true for a trigger hold. There is no linked blocking issue, and the dependency pass never clears the hold. The trigger-revisit pass (`terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh`) or an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive clears it. Publish reason-accurate guidance so neither a human nor an AI reader goes looking for a blocker that does not exist.

## Why

- `blocked_needs_label_for_reason` maps `external_trigger_pending | dependency` to `needs-dependency` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:662`). `blocked_companion_guidance` (same file, around line 684) prints the dependency text for that label whatever the reason.
- In one managed repository, 19 of 259 open `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency` issues had no native blockers at all. Most of them were `external_trigger_pending` holds. A read-only audit had to classify them by hand before the label stopped looking like data corruption.
- Product aim: blocked is a label, not an instruction, and it must carry an accurate why and owner. Then no human has to read the issue to learn what unblocks it.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh` `blocked_companion_guidance`: accept an optional second argument (the reason class). For `needs-dependency` with reason `external_trigger_pending`, print trigger guidance with the same shape as the other lines (Needed / Owner / Afterwards). For example: "Needed: the awaited trigger named above. Owner: the trigger-revisit pass (no human action) checks public evidence on a schedule and posts the retry directive when the trigger is met; an OWNER/MEMBER may post it sooner. Afterwards dispatch resumes automatically." Keep the existing text for every other caller.
2. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` around line 1187: pass the reason to `blocked_companion_guidance`.
3. `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` around lines 146–157 (the GH#38360 companion-line binding): when `$r == "external_trigger_pending"` and the label is `needs-dependency`, accept the new trigger text. Keep accepting the old dependency text so existing comments still validate.
4. Keep the label itself (`needs-dependency`) unchanged. A new label would need a label-contract migration across repos and is out of scope.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` pass. Add one assertion that an `external_trigger_pending` circuit comment carries the trigger guidance, and that the snapshot accepts both the old and new text.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts.
- `rg -n "linked blocking issue must close" .agents/scripts --glob '!tests/*'` still shows the dependency text for real dependency holds only.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #31068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

title: Google Ads: propose-then-apply mutate helper (triage is proposal-only, official MCP cannot change keywords/bids)
body:
## Gap

`marketing-sales/google-ads-triage.md` and `scripts/google_ads_triage.py` produce proposals only. The bundled official Google Ads MCP (`googleads/google-ads-mcp` v0.0.6) can change only labels and assets. So agents cannot apply approved keyword, negative-keyword, bidding or budget changes, and owners have to do this tedious work by hand in the UI.

## Evidence (observed 2026-11-20 in a managed project)

- Validate-only mutates (`validate_only=true`) worked with the existing ADC login (`authorized_user`, `adwords` scope) and no developer token: a campaign negative keyword and a switch to Maximize Clicks with a CPC cap. Developer tokens were sunset on 2026-09-09; a Cloud project with Explorer access allows these mutates.
- Community MCPs checked:
  - FGRibreau/mcp-google-ads: apply has been broken since v0.12.0 (its issue #26).
  - Heyneuron fork: cannot change bidding strategy.
  - davidmosiah, LucasSantana, ConnorCallison: narrower change sets, and they need refresh-token or MCC setup.
- A project-local CLI was built and verified. It covers propose (validate_only, plan file, checksum) and apply (checksum, 24h TTL, drift check, atomic `GoogleAdsService.Mutate`, no double apply), with a JSONL audit log, customer allowlist and budget/CPC caps. Google validated a 91-operation plan.

## Proposal

Add a framework helper, e.g. `scripts/google_ads_apply.py`, plus a doc section in `marketing-sales/google-ads-triage.md`:
- Use the same propose/apply contract and guardrails.
- Read customer and limit config from a per-project file.
- Optionally consume `google_ads_triage.py` decisions as the change input.
- Keep apply behind explicit owner approval of the printed plan.

Files: `scripts/google_ads_apply.py` (new), `marketing-sales/google-ads-triage.md` (edit), `reference/domain-index.md` (edit). Paths may need adjusting.

## Verification

- `propose` against a test account returns `validate_only` success and writes a plan.
- `apply` with a wrong checksum, an expired plan, or drifted state is refused.
- ShellCheck/ruff clean.

title: Complexity guard: allow per-repo file-size exemptions for synced-record Markdown
body:
## What

The pre-push complexity guard's Markdown file-size check (500 lines, 1000 at root; `complexity-regression-helper.sh` `scan_dir_file_size`) blocks pushes in repositories whose Markdown files are synced records rather than authored docs: email archives, call transcripts, data snapshots. Those files cannot be made "more concise without losing detail", so the only path is `COMPLEXITY_GUARD_DISABLE=1` on every push, including unattended cron pushes.

## Observed

After `aidevops init` in a private knowledge-base repo (one folder per customer: synced emails, transcripts, snapshots), the first push after a data sync failed with `[complexity-guard][BLOCK] Push introduces new file-size violation(s)`: 6 synced records of 556 to 1,785 lines. The repo's nightly sync cron pushes the same way and would fail every time a long record arrives. The only exemptions in `scan_dir_file_size` are `README.md` and `_archive/` paths; there is no per-repo or per-path setting.

## Proposed

Add a per-repo exemption for the file-size check, for example a `complexity.file_size_exclude` glob list in `.aidevops.json`, or honour an existing ignore file, applied in `_filter_to_abs_paths` and `_collect_files` alongside the `_archive/` rule. Document it in the BLOCK message, so the suggested remedy is not "split or bypass" for data repos. Optionally, let `aidevops init` ask whether the repo is a data/records repo and default the exemption.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh`

## Verification

- A repo with an exclude glob for `clients/**` pushes a new 1,500-line Markdown file under `clients/` without a BLOCK; the same file outside the glob is still blocked.
- Existing tests for `complexity-regression-helper.sh` pass.
