title: t19212: fix(pulse): partial-continuation merged-PR lane prefilters list rows and walk...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19212` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-20
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): partial-continuation merged-PR lane prefilters list rows and walks incrementally so high-volume repos stop stranding in-review partials

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the partial-continuation merged-PR lane (`_pmpc_reconcile_recent_merges`) able to keep up at high merge volume, so merged `For/Ref #N` worker partials return their issue to `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` within one Pulse cycle even when another account or a person merged the PR.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-20, one private high-volume managed repo)

- 127 open `status:in-review` issues; 113 had no open PR; 112 lacked `auto-dispatch`; the newest marker on 34 of the 40 oldest was `PARTIAL_PARENT_CLOSEOUT`. These are finished worker partials that dispatch never sees again, which is the work the user ends up doing in interactive sessions.
- A dry run of the merge-time guard on one of them (PR body `Ref #N`, `origin:worker`, merged by another account) returns `returned #N to status:available`. The guard is correct, but it only runs when this Pulse performs the merge. Recovery of other merges depends on the reconcile lane.
- The lane walks every merged PR in a 7-day window, newest first: about 4,100 merged PRs, about 41 pages, so one page takes about 360s (a production run gave 68/78 decisions `no partial continuation — it closes #N`, each costing 2 GitHub reads). The Pulse gives the partial pass about 15s per repo in the 60s `stale_blocked_reconcile` stage, half of that for this lane. So it moves deeper into history while new merges on page 1 are never reached, and the in-review backstop gets about one issue per pass. The repo's completion stamp was 18 days old.

## How

1. In `_pmpc_reconcile_recent_merges` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`), drop rows that the guard would reject from data already in the list page, with no API call: a body matching `_PMPC_CLOSING_REF_PATTERN` (case-insensitive, a superset of `_extract_linked_issue`'s closing forms) or an `origin:*` label other than `origin:worker`/`origin:worker-takeover`. Same outcome as `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` (labels/closing checks at its start) for the same body/labels.
2. Make the walk incremental: persist the start epoch of each walk, and on completion set the next walk's floor to that start minus an overlap (`PULSE_PARTIAL_MERGED_OVERLAP_SECONDS`, default 3600), never older than the lookback. The in-review revisit phase stays the backstop for unreadable reads and older merges.
3. Keep the cursor format compatible (line 1 page, then pending PR numbers).

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

## Acceptance

- Closing or foreign-origin merged PRs on a list page make zero per-PR reads; candidates still go through the unchanged guard.
- After one complete walk, the next walk stops at the high-water floor (page 1 only in steady state).
- `test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean.
- Production: after deploy, high-volume repos' partial-continuation pass stamps complete within the normal cadence, and the stranded in-review count stays near zero.

title: fix: spaceship-helper.sh uses a dead API host and the wrong auth headers
body:
## What

`spaceship-helper.sh` cannot reach the Spaceship API, so nameserver and DNS automation for Spaceship-registered domains silently falls back to manual work.

## Evidence (observed 2026-11-20, interactive session)

1. **Dead API host.** `.agents/scripts/spaceship-helper.sh:25` sets `API_BASE_URL="https://api.spaceship.com/v1"`. `dig +short api.spaceship.com A @1.1.1.1` returns nothing. The official docs (https://docs.spaceship.dev/) list the server as `https://spaceship.dev/api/v1`.
2. **Wrong auth scheme.** The helper sends one header built as `"$AUTH_HEADER_PREFIX $api_key"` (`spaceship-helper.sh:102`). The documented scheme is two headers: `X-API-Key` and `X-API-Secret`.
3. **Config path depends on the caller's directory and ignores the secret store.** `CONFIG_FILE="../configs/spaceship-config.json"` (`spaceship-helper.sh:24`) is relative to the current directory, so `spaceship-helper.sh accounts` fails with "Configuration file not found" from anywhere except `scripts/`. Credentials stored with `aidevops secret set` are not read.
4. **Direct calls work.** With stored credentials injected through `aidevops secret <KEY> <SECRET> -- sh -c 'curl ...'`, `GET https://spaceship.dev/api/v1/domains/<domain>` returned HTTP 200 with `lifecycleStatus`, `nameservers.provider` and `nameservers.hosts`.
5. `.agents/scripts/dns-helper.sh:277-279` still reports "Spaceship DNS API integration not yet implemented".

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/spaceship-helper.sh` (base URL, two-header auth, endpoint paths and payloads, credential resolution)
- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/spaceship.md` (auth and storage instructions)
- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/domain-purchasing.md` (examples, if command shapes change)
- Optional follow-up, separate issue: `.agents/scripts/dns-helper.sh` Spaceship branch

## Reference pattern

- Endpoints, from the official docs: `GET /v1/domains?take=&skip=`, `GET /v1/domains/{domain}`, `PUT /v1/domains/{domain}/nameservers` with `{"provider":"custom","hosts":[...]}` (use `"provider":"basic"` and omit `hosts` for Spaceship DNS), DNS records under the "DNS records" section. Some operations return 202 with a `spaceship-async-operationid` header to poll at `/v1/async-operations/{operationId}`.
- Credential injection without exposing values: the `aidevops secret NAME -- cmd` pattern in `.agents/tools/api/cloudflare-cf-cli.md` "Auth with aidevops Secrets". Account-specific names follow `tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md` (for example `SPACESHIP_<ACCOUNT>_API_KEY` and `SPACESHIP_<ACCOUNT>_API_SECRET`).
- Resolve any config file from the script's own directory, not the caller's.

## Acceptance

- `spaceship-helper.sh domain-details <account> <domain>` returns the domain's status and nameservers from any working directory, using credentials from `aidevops secret` (JSON config may remain as a fallback).
- `spaceship-helper.sh nameservers` and `update-ns` use the documented endpoint and payload; `update-ns` supports a dry run that prints the request without sending it.
- No credential value is printed in any output or error path.
- ShellCheck passes with zero violations.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/spaceship-helper.sh`
- A read-only live call (`domain-details`) against a real account, run by a maintainer with stored credentials; write paths verified with the dry run only.

title: Dependency reconciler unblocks dependants of blockers closed not planned without a successor
body:
## What

A dependant is auto-unblocked and dispatched when its blocker is closed `NOT_PLANNED` (or `DUPLICATE`) **without** a trusted `Superseded by #N` successor comment. The closure often means the blocker's subject was abandoned, for example a duplicate catalogue record the maintainers decided not to enrich. The dependants then run work on that abandoned subject.

## Observed (managed project repo, 2026-11-20)

- The core issue for a duplicate record was closed `NOT_PLANNED` at 07:50Z, with the decision "publish nothing to this record". It had no `Superseded by #N` comment, because the canonical record's chain was already done.
- At 08:07Z the dependency reconciler removed `needs-dependency` from the media phase issue (a native `blockedBy` dependant) and set `status:available`.
- A worker claimed it at 08:34Z and published 24 videos, 25 gallery images and 6 testimonials to the abandoned duplicate. That violated the maintainer decision and needed a reviewed catalogue merge to clean up.

## Root cause

`dependency-supersession-lib.sh` `dep_supersession_outstanding()`: when the blocker reason is `NOT_PLANNED`/`DUPLICATE` and no trusted successor exists, the check `[[ "$successor" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || return 1` returns "not outstanding". `_der_live_blocker_resolved` and `_der_native_blockers_closed` (readiness mode) in `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` then treat the blocker as resolved. Closed-not-planned with no successor is ambiguous: "no longer needed, proceed" and "subject abandoned, dependants are moot" look the same.

## Proposed fix

In readiness checks only (keep completion checks unchanged):

1. A `NOT_PLANNED`/`DUPLICATE` blocker with no trusted successor returns a distinct outcome, for example `DEP_SUPERSESSION_DETAIL="blocker #N closed <reason> without a successor"`. The dependant stays blocked instead of unblocking.
2. Route the held dependant to the recovery supervisor (`needs-ai-recovery`, owner `worker-triage`). The supervisor reads the blocker's closing comment and either closes the dependant as superseded/not planned or releases it. One recovery pass per false hold is cheaper than one wrong dispatch.
3. Optional explicit release: a trusted (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) comment on the blocker whose first line is `Dependants: proceed` keeps today's unblock behaviour without a recovery pass.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-lib.sh`: `dep_supersession_outstanding`, `dep_supersession_reason_applies`
- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: `_der_live_blocker_resolved`, `_der_native_blockers_closed` (readiness callers)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`: the same readiness rule, which also sources the library
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-supersession-lib.sh`, `test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, `test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh`, `test-pulse-ready-block-audit.sh`

## Verification

- New cases in `test-dependency-supersession-lib.sh`: closed `NOT_PLANNED` with no successor keeps the dependant blocked (readiness); with `Dependants: proceed` it releases; `COMPLETED` still releases; completion checks are unchanged.
- `test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: a closure event for a `NOT_PLANNED` blocker with no successor reports `held` (not `unblocked`) and applies the recovery label.
- ShellCheck is clean on every touched script.

body:
## Observed

Launching a new site needed a Search Console property created, verified and given a sitemap. The framework's GSC guidance covers querying existing properties and bulk-adding the service account to them through the browser. It has no route for creating and verifying a new property, so the agent composed the API calls by hand.

- `.agents/seo/google-search-console.md`: setup assumes the property already exists ("GSC → Property → Settings → Users → add the service account email").
- `.agents/scripts/gsc-auth-lib.sh`: tokens always request the read-only Search Console scope, so it cannot be reused for verification or for adding a site.

## Evidence (2026-11-20, service-account credentials at `~/.config/aidevops/gsc-credentials.json`)

Token: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=<cred file> gcloud auth application-default print-access-token --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/siteverification,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters`

1. `POST https://www.googleapis.com/siteVerification/v1/token` with `{"site":{"type":"INET_DOMAIN","identifier":"example.com"},"verificationMethod":"DNS_TXT"}` returned the TXT value.
2. TXT record added at the DNS host (Cloudflare API in this case).
3. `POST https://www.googleapis.com/siteVerification/v1/webResource?verificationMethod=DNS_TXT` returned the verified resource with the service account as owner.
4. `PUT https://searchconsole.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites/sc-domain%3Aexample.com` returned 204; the site then listed with `permissionLevel: siteOwner`.
5. `PUT .../sites/sc-domain%3Aexample.com/sitemaps/<url-encoded sitemap URL>` returned 204 and the sitemap listed as pending.

The whole sequence took under two minutes and needed no browser.

- `.agents/seo/google-search-console.md`: add a "New property setup" section with the five steps, the two scopes, and how to add a human owner afterwards (`webResource` update with an `owners` list).
- `.agents/scripts/gsc-auth-lib.sh`: allow callers to pass scopes, keeping read-only as the default.
- A helper subcommand that runs steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 and prints the TXT value for step 2. The right home is not known from this session: `seo-export-gsc.sh` is export-only. Follow the function and return conventions of `.agents/scripts/seo-export-gsc.sh`.

title: fix(pulse): close measured-resolved file-size-debt held under consolidation
body:
## What

Close a generated file-size-debt issue whose cited file is measured below threshold on the remote default branch, even when the issue is held by the consolidation machinery (`needs-consolidation` / `consolidation-in-progress`). Today such an issue stays open indefinitely and churns the cross-runner consolidation lock.

## Why

Observed on #31068 (closed manually, with evidence, in an interactive session):

- PR #39388 merged at 2026-11-20T03:11Z and brought `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` to 1944 lines (threshold 2000).
- #31068 stayed open for about 16 more hours. Between 03:45Z and 17:20Z, two runners took and released `consolidation-in-progress` about 17 times without filing a child, and left a lock comment behind.
- On the maintainer runner, the pulse log shows only `Dispatch deferred for #31068 ...: consolidation child in flight` / `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=consolidated signal=consolidation_child_in_flight` after the merge. There is no resolved-debt close attempt.

Root cause:

1. The only measured resolved-debt close, `_large_file_gate_close_resolved_debt_issues` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:781`), is called only from the large-file gate inside `dispatch_with_dedup` (`pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:1563`). Consolidation deferral returns before the gate runs.
2. The consolidation preflight `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:998`) checks labels, closing PRs, NOT_PLANNED and body-ref ratios, but has no measured file-size-debt gate. Gate 3 correctly ignores PR #31069, which merged before the latest reopen. The successor's PR #39388 is not a structural closing PR of the parent, so preflight proceeds every cycle.
3. Reconcile's `_pir_file_size_debt_close_gate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`) is only consulted on merged-PR evidence for the issue itself, which does not exist after a consolidated successor delivers the split.

The cost is repeated label writes and lock comments across runners, and a solved issue that looks like live debt.

## Reproducer

Live evidence from #31068 (read-only commands):

1. `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/contents/.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh --jq .content | base64 -d | wc -l` → `1944` (below 2000) after PR #39388 merged at 03:11Z.
2. `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068/timeline --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.event=="labeled" or .event=="unlabeled") | [.created_at,.actor.login,.event,.label.name] | @tsv'` → paired `labeled`/`unlabeled consolidation-in-progress` events from `alex-solovyev` and `vladimirdulov` roughly every 40 minutes from 03:45Z to 17:20Z. No consolidation child was created, and the issue stayed open.
3. Pulse log on a maintainer runner after the merge: `rg '#31068' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows only `consolidation child in flight` deferrals. There is no `Resolved file-size debt` close.

Synthetic: give a generated file-size-debt issue `needs-consolidation`, with its cited file below threshold on the remote default branch and no structural closing PR merged after the latest reopen. Run `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved`. It returns 1 (proceed) and the issue is never closed.

## How

- In `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`), add a gate before the closing-PR gate (Gate 3). When the parent carries `file-size-debt` and its body has the `aidevops:generator=large-file-simplification-gate cited_file=... threshold=...` marker, call `_large_file_gate_close_resolved_debt_issues "$issue_number" "$repo_slug" "$body"`. Guard the call with `declare -F` because the gate library may not be sourced in every context; source `pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` on demand following the `_consolidation_load_reopen_helper` pattern in the same file. On success, return 0 (skip) and log it. The helper already measures the pinned remote default-branch blob, so stale local checkouts cannot close regrown debt.
- Also run that close in the held-issue re-evaluation path (`_pte_reevaluate_consolidation_issue` / `_reevaluate_consolidation_labels`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh`). Held issues never reach `dispatch_with_dedup`, so they still get closed once the debt is gone.
- Keep the existing reopen semantics: if the remote file regrows to the threshold or above, `_large_file_gate_reopen_debt_issue` must still reopen the canonical issue.
- Optional diagnostic, only if cheap: find out why acquire/release cycles end without a child. The candidates are `_consolidation_post_lock_dedup_skip` or the post-assembly ownership recheck in `_dispatch_issue_consolidation` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh`). Record the cause in the PR. If it needs a separate fix, file a follow-up.

**Reference pattern:** `_consolidation_skip_for_closing_pr` and `_consolidation_load_reopen_helper` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh` (on-demand sourcing plus a gate returning 0 = skip); `_large_file_gate_close_resolved_debt_issues` for the measured close.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A generated file-size-debt issue labelled `needs-consolidation` whose cited file is below threshold on the remote default branch is closed as completed by the consolidation preflight or held-issue re-evaluation, without acquiring `consolidation-in-progress`.
- [ ] A generated file-size-debt issue whose remote file is still at or above threshold is not closed, and consolidation proceeds as before.
- [ ] An unmeasurable remote count (API failure) does not close the issue. The preflight fails open as today.
- [ ] Existing suites pass: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-large-file-gate-resolved-debt-close.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-multi-runner.sh`. Extend `test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh` with the resolved/still-over cases, since it already stubs file-size-debt parents.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean and `bash -n` pass on touched scripts. `affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base` reports no regressions.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh`

## Related

**Task ID:** `t19214` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-20
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

Operator approval records for marketing action plans

## Done when

- [ ] With a valid root-owned v2 record that matches plan digest, action set, owner and binding, `apply` and `rollback` succeed exactly as before, including replay no-ops.
- [ ] A missing, user-owned, symlinked, stale, wrong-operation, wrong-digest or cancelled record is refused, and no file changes.

- [ ] `approve` refuses without euid 0, without `SUDO_USER`, or with non-TTY stdin. It shows the plan summary and requires a typed `APPROVE`.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/marketing_action_approval.py`: mint/verify/summarise approval records. Python 3.9-compatible because sudo may resolve `/usr/bin/python3`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/marketing_actions.py:175-239`: replace `_read_inherited_fd`/`verify_runtime_approval` with the record verifier. Keep `_verify_cancellation`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/marketing-action-helper.py`: add an `approve` subcommand (root+TTY only).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:2045-2067`: route `marketing-plan` in `main()` after `_require_interactive_root`.

- **Writers/mutation paths:** the new mint function writes `~<operator>/.aidevops/approval-keys/marketing-actions/{apply|rollback}-<digest>.json` (dir root 0755, file root 0644). It also writes the operator-owned 0600 cancellation file under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/marketing-action-cancellations/`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-marketing-actions.py` encodes the apply/rollback/denial contract and must keep passing with the new fixture.
- **Schemas/config:** approval schema bumps to `aidevops.marketing-action-approval/v2`; plan and receipt schemas are unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`; `rg -n marketing_action .agents/configs` finds no generated index entries.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. No v1 approval was ever produced outside tests, per `rg -n AIDEVOPS_MARKETING_APPROVAL_FD .agents`.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** a code revert of `.agents/scripts/marketing_actions.py` restores the v1 contract. Expired records in `~/.aidevops/approval-keys/marketing-actions/` (15 minutes or less) are inert and removable with sudo. File rollback stays receipt-bound in `marketing_actions.rollback_receipt`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Create `marketing_action_approval.py` (3.9-safe). It holds the record schema, a per-plan-schema binding registry (`aidevops.marketing-action-plan/v1` binds `project_root` and `worktree_identity`), `approval_dir(owner)` resolved through `pwd`, `mint()` (euid 0, `SUDO_USER` equals the plan owner, TTY confirmation, `O_EXCL` temp file then `os.replace`), and `verify()` (uid/mode/symlink checks, field equality, freshness, cancellation).
2. Swap `verify_runtime_approval` in `marketing_actions.py` to call `verify()`. Drop the pipe, HMAC and `stat` FIFO code.
3. Add `approve --plan PATH [--operation apply|rollback] [--receipt PATH]` to `marketing-action-helper.py`, and route `approval-helper.sh marketing-plan` through `_require_interactive_root`.
4. Update the test fixture and the workflow doc, then run the verification below.

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the record is written to an `O_EXCL` temp file and then `os.replace`d inside the root directory. Apply keeps its existing worktree lock and per-write cancellation checks.
- **Migration/rollback:** there is no data migration. Revert ordering is irrelevant because plans and receipts are unchanged.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** a v1 pipe approval is rejected with a clear error. No producer exists, so no caller breaks. Plan and receipt files from older versions remain valid.
- **Idempotency/retry:** re-approving the same digest replaces the record with a new nonce and cancellation file. Replay of an applied plan stays a verified no-op.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a mint failure before `os.replace` leaves no record. A crash after it is bounded by the TTL, and the operator can cancel by editing the cancellation file.


  - The `/usr/bin/python3` import covers sudo interpreter compatibility.

title: t19215: Approval-bound Google Ads account actions (validate-only plan, guarded apply,...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19215` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-20
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

Approval-bound Google Ads account actions (validate-only plan, guarded apply, rollback)

**Blocked by:** `t19214`

## Done when

- [ ] `plan` sends `validateOnly: true` and records the full operations, keyword text, before-state and inverse operations under `plan_digest`. `apply` with a valid approval sends one non-validate mutate and writes the receipt and audit line.
- [ ] Apply is refused with no write request for: a missing, stale or mismatched approval; an expired plan; a tampered digest; drifted state; a non-allowlisted customer; or values over the caps.
- [ ] Rollback restores the before-state only when the live state still equals the after-state, and a repeat rollback is a no-op.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/google_ads_actions.py`: kind registry, GAQL reads, operation builders, plan/apply/rollback, receipt and audit. Model the transport on `.agents/scripts/marketing_account_google.py:16-76`.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/google-ads-action-helper.py`: CLI `plan --input --config --output`, `apply --plan --receipt-dir`, `rollback --receipt`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/marketing_action_approval.py`: register the plan schema `aidevops.google-ads-action-plan/v1` with binding `customer_id`, plus a summary renderer.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-google-ads-actions.py`: fake-transport contract tests.
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/marketing-actions.md`: Supported Surface and Google Ads section.
- `EDIT: .agents/marketing-sales/google-ads-triage.md:6-12`: pointer from proposals to the apply path.

Transport rules:

- Use stdlib `urllib` with a fixed `googleads.googleapis.com/v25/` prefix.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer` from `GOOGLE_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN`, plus an optional `login-customer-id`.
- Never accept credentials as arguments or write them to output.
- Do not require a developer token: Google's developer-token policy page states tokens were sunset on 2026-09-09 and are ignored. Send the header only when `GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN` is set.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the CLI only. Triage output (`google_ads_triage.py`) remains proposals, and operators hand-author the action input. `rg -n handoff_only .agents/scripts` shows that local marketing-actions keeps its own exclusions.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** Google Ads REST `customers/{cid}/googleAds:mutate` (the only write endpoint) and `googleAds:search` (reads). Locally: plan output (0600, new path) and the receipt directory (0700) holding `<digest>.json` and `audit.jsonl`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-marketing-actions.py` covers the shared approval module. The new `.agents/scripts/tests/test-google-ads-actions.py` uses a fake transport, so no network is used.
- **Schemas/config:** new `aidevops.google-ads-action-input/v1`, `-config/v1`, `-plan/v1` and `-receipt/v1`. The config holds `customer_allowlist`, `max_daily_budget_micros`, `max_cpc_bid_ceiling_micros` and `max_operations`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` copies `.agents/scripts/`; `rg -n google_ads_triage .agents/configs` finds no generated registry entries.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. `rg -n "google-ads-action" .agents` finds no existing producer or consumer, and `.agents/scripts/marketing_actions.py` plan and receipt schemas are unchanged, so there is nothing to backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** account changes reverse through receipt inverse operations via `rollback`. A code revert removes the adapter, and receipts and audit logs stay as private evidence.

### Implementation Steps

1. Define the kind registry. Each kind provides a GAQL before-state read, before/after matchers, a forward operation and an inverse operation. Resource names follow `customers/{cid}/campaigns/{id}`, `adGroupCriteria/{ag}~{crit}`, `campaignCriteria/{camp}~{crit}` and `campaignBudgets/{id}`. `updateMask` values use camelCase.
2. `plan`: validate the input and config (allowlist, caps, operation count), read the before-state, refuse no-op or unsupported rollback states, run the validate-only mutate, then write the digest-bound plan (0600, exclusive create).
3. `apply`: validate the plan digest and expiry, verify the operator approval with binding `customer_id`, take the receipt lock, handle replay and resume, check for drift, write the receipt as `applying`, run the mutate, then record resource names, mark the receipt `applied` and append the audit line.
4. `rollback`: verify the rollback approval bound to the receipt digest, confirm the live state is the after-state, validate and then send the inverse operations, mark the receipt `rolled_back` and append the audit line.
5. Add the docs and tests, then run the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** one mutate with `partialFailure: false`, so all operations apply or none do. A non-blocking lock on the receipt directory prevents concurrent apply or rollback of the same plan.
- **Migration/rollback:** bidding rollback is only planned from `MANUAL_CPC`, `TARGET_SPEND` or `MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS`, with no portfolio strategy. Shared budgets are refused, so every planned change has a recorded inverse.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** these are new schemas. Local marketing-action plans keep their v1 schema and `handoff_only` exclusions unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** an applied receipt replays as a no-op. Create operations refuse when an identical negative already exists, and a repeat rollback is a no-op.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** the receipt is written as `applying` before the mutate. On resume, if everything is in before-state, apply again. If everything is in after-state, mark it applied and recover created resource names by GAQL. Anything mixed is refused.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-google-ads-actions.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-marketing-actions.py
ruff check .agents/scripts/google_ads_actions.py .agents/scripts/google-ads-action-helper.py .agents/scripts/marketing_action_approval.py
python3 .agents/scripts/google-ads-action-helper.py plan --input INPUT.json --config CONFIG.json --output PLAN.json
```

- **Surface mapping:**
  - The first test covers plan/apply/rollback, drift, caps, allowlist and approval denials (all acceptance criteria).
  - The second test covers the shared approval registry.
  - `ruff` covers the changed files.
  - The live `plan` command needs operator credentials and a test account; it proves Google accepts the payloads with validate-only.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required, because these are new files plus one registry entry.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/google_ads_actions.py`
- `.agents/scripts/google-ads-action-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/marketing_action_approval.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-google-ads-actions.py`
- `.agents/workflows/marketing-actions.md`
- `.agents/marketing-sales/google-ads-triage.md`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Add a remote Google Ads adapter to the marketing-actions contract. Only these action kinds are allowed:

- campaign negative keyword add
- ad-group negative keyword add
- keyword pause/enable
- switch a campaign to Maximize Clicks with a CPC ceiling
- change a campaign budget amount

The flow:

- `plan` reads the current state through GAQL, calls `googleAds:mutate` with `validateOnly: true`, and writes a digest-bound plan. The plan holds the full keyword text, before-state, inverse operations, config caps and a 24h expiry.
- `apply` requires the operator approval record from the prerequisite task. It re-reads state and refuses on drift, runs one atomic mutate with `partialFailure: false`, and writes a private receipt plus a JSONL audit line.
- `rollback` applies the recorded inverse operations under a fresh rollback approval, after its own drift check.

## Why

Parent #39489: triage and the official MCP are proposal-only, so owners apply approved negatives, bids and budgets by hand. `marketing_actions.py:28-41` marks these kinds `handoff_only`. This task makes them executable without weakening operator control.

## Tier

`tier:thinking`: spend-affecting writes to an external account.

title: t19216: perf(pulse): minimum-worker-floor refill rounds use normal-refill census instead of inheriting the early first wave
body:
## Task


Run the minimum-worker-floor refill rounds (`_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) with normal-refill census semantics (`_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=0`). Today they inherit the early dispatch's first-wave scope.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Run the minimum-worker-floor refill rounds (`_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) with normal-refill census semantics (`_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=0`). Today they inherit the early dispatch's first-wave scope.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-20, one pulse host)

- `_preflight_early_dispatch` sets a dynamically scoped `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=1` and calls `apply_dispatch_max`. Its `_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill` then re-runs `dispatch_max` up to `min_worker_concurrency` (6) times while active workers stay below the floor. Every one of those rounds inherits the first-wave scope:
  - a serial census (`_dispatch_census_parallelism` forces 1), here pinned at the 180s deadline across 60-70 repos;
  - no GH#38727 carry of unreached repositories' fresh last-good lists ("First waves keep their own bounds and never carry");
  - triage/enrichment prepasses deferred "to normal refill".
- Measured since 17:00Z: `preflight_early_dispatch` averaged 3,052s (two cycles). The post-label refill was then skipped with `remaining=0s` / `-2372s`, so the normal refill (parallel census, carry, prepasses) never ran.
- Round yield alternated 43-160 candidates (product backlog repo reached) and 2-6 (not reached, nothing carried). This happened while the high-volume product repo had a fresh 152-candidate last-good list on disk and 140 `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` issues. Active workers sat at 1-4 of 20.
- GH#38727 fixed exactly this alternation for full censuses; the floor refill never gets a full census.

## How

1. In `_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill`, declare `local _PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=0` before the refill loop, with a comment. The first round of early dispatch stays a first wave; its refill rounds become normal refill rounds. The non-early callers already run with 0.
2. Keep every admission gate: `_dispatch_round_budget_plan` still picks a bounded census when a full one does not fit, and candidates keep their live dispatch gates.
3. Check `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` for floor-refill/first-wave expectations; change a test only if it asserts the inherited first-wave scope.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`

## Acceptance

- Floor-refill rounds run with `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=0`; the initial early-dispatch round keeps first-wave semantics.
- Existing dispatch suites pass; ShellCheck clean.
- After deployment, `pulse.log` shows `Candidate census parallel scans` (GH#38730) during early dispatch refills, `Candidate census carried last-good candidates` (GH#38727) when a refill census stops early, and no alternation down to 2-6 candidates while a product backlog exists. `pulse-stage-timings.log` shows `preflight_early_dispatch` well below 3,000s.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`; `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`; post-deploy log checks above.

title: t19217: Google Ads readers: make the developer token optional (tokens sunset 2026-09-09)
body:
## Task


Both live Google Ads readers refuse to run without `GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN`. Google's developer-token policy page (developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/developer-token) states that developer tokens "were sunset on September 9, 2026" and are ignored by API servers. Operators without a token therefore cannot collect snapshots or demand metrics. The fix: require only the access token, and send the `developer-token` header only when one is configured.

## Done when

- [ ] With only `GOOGLE_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN` set, both adapters build a request with no `developer-token` header.
- [ ] With no access token, both adapters still refuse before any network call. With a developer token set, the header is still sent.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/marketing_account_google.py:48-61`: require only `access_token`, and build the headers dict without `developer-token` when the token is empty.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/domain_opportunity_google_ads.py:63-69,~259-268`: make `developer_token: str = ""` optional in `GoogleAdsCredentials.__post_init__`, and add the header only when set.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-domain-opportunity-google-ads.py:125-140` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-marketing-account-snapshots.py:34`: update the credential expectations.
- `EDIT: .agents/services/analytics/marketing-account-snapshots.md:19-22` and `.agents/seo/domain-opportunities.md:19`: describe the developer token as optional and legacy.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/marketing-account-snapshot-helper.py:53` and `.agents/scripts/domain-opportunity-google-ads.py:86` read the env var; both keep passing it through.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A. Both adapters are read-only (`searchStream` and keyword historical metrics).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-marketing-account-snapshots.py` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-domain-opportunity-google-ads.py` cover the credential guards.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A. Credentials never enter stored evidence (`domain_opportunity_google_ads.py:60`).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` copies `.agents/scripts/` unchanged; there is no generated output.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data references the token. It is used only for request construction in `.agents/scripts/marketing_account_google.py` and `.agents/scripts/domain_opportunity_google_ads.py`.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** a revert of `.agents/scripts/marketing_account_google.py` and `.agents/scripts/domain_opportunity_google_ads.py` restores the old guard.

### Implementation Steps

1. In both adapters, change the guard to require only the access token (plus the customer for the domain sync).
2. Build the headers as `{"Authorization": ..., "Content-Type": ...}` and add `developer-token` only if it is non-empty.
3. Update the two tests and the two docs, then run the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A. These are stateless request builders.
- **Migration/rollback:** a revert restores the stricter guard; no data is involved.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** operators who still set the token keep sending it, which Google ignores.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged. Retry logic in `domain_opportunity_google_ads.py` is untouched.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** unchanged. A missing access token still fails closed before any request.

title: fix(parent-status): a merged PR referenced in a parent body counts as an open child
body:
## What

`aidevops parent-status` counts a merged pull request that the parent body references as an open child. That holds the parent open with "N child issue(s) remain open" even though every real child is closed.

## Evidence (2026-11-20, #38332)

An intermediate edit of the #38332 body mentioned PRs #38647 and #38666 in prose. `parent-status-helper.sh 38332 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --json` then reported:

- `"children_open": 2` and `"next_action": "2 child issue(s) remain open — continue child #38647."`
- phase rows `{"child_number": 38647, "child_state": "MERGED", ...}` and `{"child_number": 38666, "child_state": "MERGED", ...}`

After those references were removed from the body, the helper reported `children_open: 0` and "close the parent issue".

## Cause

`_summarize_child_readiness` (`.agents/scripts/parent-status-helper.sh`, around line 609) treats any state other than `CLOSED`/`closed` as open. GitHub reports a merged PR's state as `MERGED`, so a PR number gathered as a child (from the body prose/Children parse in `_gather_child_nums`, around lines 536-557) is counted as open forever.

## How

- Files: `.agents/scripts/parent-status-helper.sh` (`_summarize_child_readiness`, and the child-state fetch that sets `cstate`). Check `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions-parent.sh` for the same open-state test.
- Preferred fix: drop gathered numbers that resolve to pull requests from the child set (a PR is not a child issue), or at least treat `MERGED` as terminal.
- Verify: `.agents/scripts/test-parent-status.sh` passes. A stub parent whose body lists a merged PR number must report `children_open` 0 for that entry. Existing open/closed/not-planned cases must be unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A merged PR referenced in a parent body never counts as an open child.
- An open or unmerged closed PR reference is not counted as a completed child either. It is excluded or reported as unknown, never as delivery.
- Existing `test-parent-status.sh` cases still pass.

# Decide macOS acceptance for the installed-runtime worktree lifecycle canary (seal and restore-before-removal are Linux-only)

Ref #38658 (canary that found this), Ref #35359 (rollout parent).

## What

The GH#38658 canary passes 5 of 7 items on a macOS Pulse install (3.39.250, deployed `5fceb9acc`). Two items cannot pass there by design, so no macOS matrix row can become `verified` under the current criteria:

| Item | macOS behaviour | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3. Verified completion **and sealing** | Completion is observed (`runs.state=ended`, `pid-absent`), but sealing needs the managed backend, which is Linux-only | `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-run.py:32` (`managed backend requires Linux`); `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py:387-396` records `legacy-guards` on Darwin |
| 6. Source removal **only after restore verification** | `worktree-helper.sh remove` retires after `verify-local` + fingerprint equality + `source-matches`, explicitly without a full restore | `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/preservation.py:128-145`; documented in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md:380-383` |

The 24 h restore-verified idle receipt (`worktree_lifetime_archive.py`) also requires a sealed managed generation, so it is unavailable on macOS too.

## Decision needed (maintainer)

- **A (recommended): platform-specific acceptance, doc-only.** For macOS, define `verified` in `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` "Pulse host rollout and verification" as: worker-lifecycle run identity bound (PID + start token + boot id), `ended` observation, removal gated by `verify-local` + `source-matches`, plus an independent post-removal restore matching every snapshot field. The canary evidence on #38658 already meets that definition.
- **B: full restore before every removal on the worker-lifecycle path.** This contradicts the CLEANUP.md design decision. Measured restore cost on the canary was 8-31 s per removal, on top of the 65-82 s removals.
- **C: launchd-based managed lifetime backend for macOS.** Large new backend, with no existing design.

Recommendation: A. The executor's verify-local design is deliberate, the round trip was proven independently, and B or C add cost without a demonstrated recovery failure.

## How (if A is chosen)

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`, in the "Pulse host rollout and verification" step 4 and the **Status** paragraph: add the macOS acceptance definition in at most 3 lines. Keep the file under the 500-line markdown ratchet (449 lines now).
- Then update the macOS matrix row from #38658 to `verified` only if its evidence meets the new definition.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`; markdownlint through the Code Quality workflow.
- The matrix row cites the #38658 receipts. Do not promote any other row.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decision recorded on this issue.
- [ ] If A: acceptance text merged and the macOS row re-evaluated. If B or C: an implementation brief filed and linked.

title: t19218: perf(pulse): filter launched-since-stored and known-closed issues from reused last-good census lists
body:
## Task


Give the GH#38483 timeout-reuse path for last-good candidate lists the same launched-since-stored filter that the GH#38727 carry path already applies. Then drop reused or carried candidates that the runner's own fresh prefetch cache shows are no longer launchable (closed, assigned, or without `status:available`).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Give the GH#38483 timeout-reuse path for last-good candidate lists the same launched-since-stored filter that the GH#38727 carry path already applies. Then drop reused or carried candidates that the runner's own fresh prefetch cache shows are no longer launchable (closed, assigned, or without `status:available`).

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-20, one pulse host)

- `_dispatch_census_carry_repo` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-census.sh`) removes issues launched after the list was stored, using `_dispatch_census_dispatched_index`. The timeout-reuse path, `_dispatch_census_last_good_candidates` (called from the rc=124 branch of the per-repository scan), returns the stored list unfiltered apart from the PR-backlog guardrail.
- Reused lists were up to 3,560s old (`PULSE_CENSUS_LAST_GOOD_MAX_AGE_S` default 3600). Over six floor-refill rounds in one early dispatch, these blocks hit candidates that were stale before any live gate ran: 16 `issue_closed` (`Skipping #N: state=CLOSED`), 10 `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch`, and 21 `dedup_pr_evidence`. Each still costs a dispatch-candidate stage and a live read. In one round, 56 candidates were processed for 1 launch.
- Candidates stay hints, and every live gate stays binding. This change only removes work the runner already knows cannot launch.

## How

1. In `_dispatch_census_last_good_candidates`, or at its rc=124 call site, apply the same `$launched["<slug>#<number>"] < stored_at` filter as `_dispatch_census_carry_repo`. Build the index once per census via `_dispatch_census_dispatched_index` instead of once per repository where practical; follow how the carry pass passes `index`.
2. Optional second step, only if the cache semantics support it: when `PULSE_PREFETCH_CACHE_FILE` has an entry for the repository with `last_prefetch` newer than the list's `stored_at`, drop candidates that the entry shows as closed, assigned, or missing `auto-dispatch`/`status:available`. Do not treat absence from the prefetch list as closure unless the prefetch for that repository is proven complete (not limit-truncated). Mirror the field handling in `_dispatch_first_wave_arrival_repos` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`).
3. Keep the reuse log line and add the filtered count, e.g. `count=52 filtered=9`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-census.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`

## Acceptance

- A timed-out repository scan never re-offers an issue that the local dispatch ledger shows was launched after the last-good list was stored.
- If step 2 is implemented, candidates the fresh prefetch cache proves closed or assigned are dropped. Absence alone never drops a candidate.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` passes (the GH#38483/GH#38727 cases sit near `carried last-good candidates`); ShellCheck clean.
- After deployment, `pulse.log` shows fewer `blocked:issue_closed` and `dedup_active_claim_durable_launch` benign blocks per round when `reused last-good candidates` lines appear.

## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-framework-routing-helper.sh` fails 5 cases on `main` (28 passed, 5 failed). All 5 are the `log-framework-issue` success paths:

- empty array issue-list result creates issue
- null issue-list result creates issue

This is test drift, not a product defect. body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## What

Add `worktree-lifecycle-canary.sh`, a reusable installed-runtime canary for the managed worktree lifecycle. It runs the seven GH#38658 items against **installed** scripts in a disposable HOME, bare origin, repo, worktree base, archive root and lifecycle state, and prints redacted receipts ready for the rollout matrix.

## Why

The GH#38658 canary on host-C (macOS) took ad-hoc scripts and about 90 min of manual composition: setup, launch, archive and remove, inspect, independent restore, interrupted merge, standalone `AUTO_MERGE`, snapshot diff, and registry queries. The host-A and host-B rows in `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` still say "Open: installed-runtime canary", so the same procedure must be repeated on each host.

## How

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/worktree-lifecycle-canary.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md` (one-line pointer in "Pulse host rollout and verification"; keep the file at 500 lines or fewer)

### Implementation Steps

1. Stages to reproduce (verbs from the GH#38658 receipts comment, issuecomment-7050229299):
   - baseline: deployed SHA and ancestry, plus SHA-256 of installed vs source lifecycle scripts;
   - disposable env: `HOME`, `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR`, `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR`, `WORKTREE_REGISTRY_DIR` and `WORKTREE_REGISTRY_DB`, plus a private `repos.json` pointing at a local bare origin;
   - `worktree-helper.sh add` → generation and backend row;
   - `worker-lifecycle-state.sh <bounded cmd>` → run with PID, start token and boot id;
   - `worker-registry.py reconcile` → `ended`;
   - dirty-state snapshot (HEAD, log, staged, unstaged, untracked set and content, porcelain, index stages, ORIG_HEAD, MERGE_* and AUTO_MERGE) → `worktree-helper.sh remove` → archive receipt;
   - `worktree-archive-helper.sh verify-structure`, `verify-local` and `verify`, then `restore --target` → snapshot diff;
   - a conflicted merge, and standalone `AUTO_MERGE` via `git merge-tree`/`AUTO_MERGE` write, through `archive`, `source-matches`, `restore` and diff.
2. Never touch production registries except through read-only aggregates. Run every stage under its own timeout and report `timeout` as a distinct result.
3. Emit a Markdown table (item, result, receipt) with paths replaced by `<D>`.
4. Linux: also assert the managed seal and the restore-verified idle receipt. Darwin: report those as `unavailable (Linux-only, GH#39513)`.

### Hazards

- On macOS, use the canonical `TMPDIR` (`realpath`); see GH#39524.
- The canonical-checkout git guard blocks setup when it runs from a canonical repo. Always `cd` into the disposable root first.

## Verification

- Run on macOS and on one Linux Pulse host: every stage exits within budget and output matches the GH#38658 receipt format.
- ShellCheck clean.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One command reproduces the GH#38658 receipts on macOS and Linux.
- [ ] The matrix doc points to it.

## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #39541)

The previous worker's PR #39541 (`GH#39530: fix: avoid early-exit pipe readers under pipefail in lifecycle canary`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (2 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md
.agents/scripts/worktree-lifecycle-canary.sh
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `fdfd3e3c431777ac2d575c37ea14dbac10b8b4b3`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/39541/head:recovered-39541
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick fdfd3e3c431777ac2d575c37ea14dbac10b8b4b3
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #39541's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`.

title: fix(pulse-merge): a failed zero-job rerun blocks the update-branch fallback, stranding PRs until a manual push
body:
## What

A worker PR whose required check never reports is stuck when its zero-job workflow rerun fails. The merge pass keeps choosing "rerun handled" and never reaches the bounded update-branch fallback. The PR stays unmerged until someone pushes to the branch by hand.

## Evidence (2026-11-20, one runner)

- 7 PRs in the current `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` logged `rerun request failed for zero-job workflow ... no further automatic reruns (t18926)`: #39428, #39430, #39434, #39436, #39447, #39456 and #39465.
- #39436, head `182e12628415`, run 44703029243:
  - Every merge pass logged `1 required context(s) not passing ... (1 never reported, 0 check(s) in flight)`, even though the review gate, terminal checks and approval had passed.
  - The PR opened at 08:30Z and had no new events until a manual `Merge branch 'main'` commit at 17:10Z. It merged at 17:23Z.
  - #39428 and #39434 followed the same pattern: idle until the 17:10Z update, then merged.
- Impact: aidevops worker PRs took a median 63 min from open to merge in the last 24h (p75 140, n=45). This was the largest remaining issue→merge contributor in the #38332 measurement ([comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38332#issuecomment-7049351307)).

## Cause

In `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-rest-state.sh`:

- `_pmrs_remediate_zero_job_runs` (around line 626) returns 0 ("handled; caller must not update-branch") whenever zero-job runs exist. It ignores the outcome of `_pmrs_rerun_zero_job_run`, which returns 1 when the request failed and escalated, or 2 when the run was already handled.
- The caller (around lines 770-775) then records `rerun` in its state file and returns before `_pmp_update_branch_rest`. Each later pass finds the same zero-job run, gets rc 2, and returns 0 again. The update-branch fallback and the `max_attempts` ATTENTION path (around lines 764-768) are never reached for that head.

## How

- Change `_pmrs_remediate_zero_job_runs` to return 0 only when this call newly requested at least one rerun (`_pmrs_rerun_zero_job_run` rc 0). When every candidate rerun failed (rc 1) or had already been requested on an earlier pass (rc 2), return 1. The caller then falls through to the existing bounded update-branch path, which keeps its `threshold` wait and `max_attempts` cap.
- Keep the t18926 intent: the first time a zero-job run is seen, a rerun is still preferred over update-branch.
- Model this on the GH#38624 close/reopen branch just above, which already logs and falls back to update-branch when its remediation is not permitted or fails.
- Files: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-rest-state.sh`. Update the stub in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-no-actions-suite.sh` (line 46) if its contract changes. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` covers the fallback.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-rest-state.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-no-actions-suite.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` pass.
- `.agents/scripts/affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base` shows no regressions.

## Acceptance

- **Positive:** on a head whose zero-job rerun failed, or was requested on an earlier pass with no new check reported, the next eligible pass after `threshold` requests update-branch and logs the GH#32951 line.
- **Negative:** on first discovery of a zero-job run, a rerun is requested and update-branch is not called in the same pass, as today.
- **Bound:** update-branch attempts per head stay capped by `max_attempts`, and the ATTENTION line fires when they are exhausted.

title: t19220: perf(ci): release version-bump PRs skip heavy Code Quality jobs like version/docs-only PRs
body:
## Task


Protected-main release PRs (`chore/release-v<semver>-provenance`) change only
version-reference lines, yet `Code Quality Analysis` classifies them as full
shell and substantive scope. Teach `detect-scope` to recognise a diff whose
non-documentation changes are exclusively version-reference lines, so release
PRs skip the heavy full-repository jobs exactly as version/docs-only PRs do.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Protected-main release PRs (`chore/release-v<semver>-provenance`) change only
version-reference lines, yet `Code Quality Analysis` classifies them as full
shell and substantive scope. Teach `detect-scope` to recognise a diff whose
non-documentation changes are exclusively version-reference lines, so release
PRs skip the heavy full-repository jobs exactly as version/docs-only PRs do.

## Why

Evidence (2026-11-20):

- Release PR #39535 (v3.39.251) changes `VERSION`, `package.json`,
  `sonar-project.properties`, `setup.sh` (`# Version:` comment),
  `aidevops.sh` (`# Version:` comment), `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`,
  `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Because `setup.sh`/`aidevops.sh` are `.sh`
  and the other three are not on the trivial list, it ran about 45 jobs,
  including Complexity Analysis, four Framework Validation shards, full
  ShellCheck, Bash 3.2 and SonarCloud. It was still waiting on queued jobs
  after 30 minutes.
- The last 12 release PRs took 6–38 minutes from creation to merge
  (median about 10). Releases run about six times a day; the releasing
  session waits on each one.
- Hosted runners are saturated: sampled Code Quality jobs waited 4–18 minutes
  in the queue against 0.5–9.5 minutes of execution. Release PRs add about
  45 runner jobs each to that queue, delaying worker PRs too.
- The release commit is the already-validated `main` tip plus version strings.
  `main` push CI still runs the full scope after merge.

## How

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` `detect-scope` → `Determine scope`:
  - Before `printf 'Changed files:`, capture
    `version_diff=$(git diff -U0 --no-color --no-ext-diff MERGE_BASE HEAD -- <version files> || true)`.
  - Inside the classification block, add a strict parser: header lines only
    `diff --git`, `index`, `--- a/`, `+++ b/` before the first `@@`; every hunk
    line must be `+`/`-` content matching that file's pattern. Reject mode
    changes, new/deleted files, renames, `\ No newline`, or anything else.
  - Patterns: `VERSION` `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`; `package.json` and
    `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` `^ *"version": "X.Y.Z",?$`;
    `sonar-project.properties` `^sonar\.projectVersion=X.Y.Z$`;
    `setup.sh`/`aidevops.sh` `^# Version: X.Y.Z$`.
  - When every non-trivial file is a version-reference file and the parser
    accepts the diff, report `shell=false` and `substantive=false`.
    Any doubt keeps the current full-scope result.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-runner-routing.mjs`: the test already runs
  the real block with a `changed` env; add cases with `version_diff` for an
  accepted release bump, a code line in `setup.sh`, a mode change, and a
  version file mixed with real source.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-runner-routing.mjs`

## Acceptance

- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-runner-routing.mjs` passes,
  including the new cases.
- Existing docs-only, planning, shell, workflow and Python classifications
  are unchanged.
- The next release PR's `Detect PR scope` log prints the version-reference
  message, and Complexity Analysis / Framework Validation report skipped
  (which satisfies the required contexts, as for docs-only PRs).

## Out of scope

Other workflows' own path filters, branch protection, runner routing.

</details>

title: t19221: perf(ci): worker lifecycle contract spends 112-251s before its first test in required Complexity Analysis
body:
## Task


The `Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract` step in the required
`Complexity Analysis` job (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`) spends
112–251 s before its first test result appears. The 546 contract tests then
take about 4 minutes. Find where the start-up time goes, remove it, and keep
the contract's guarantees (separate non-root fixture UID, real `/proc`
census, no weakened production guard).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The `Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract` step in the required
`Complexity Analysis` job (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`) spends
112–251 s before its first test result appears. The 546 contract tests then
take about 4 minutes. Find where the start-up time goes, remove it, and keep
the contract's guarantees (separate non-root fixture UID, real `/proc`
census, no weakened production guard).

## Why

`Complexity Analysis` is a required check and the last one to finish on most
PRs. In sampled runs it executed for 459–569 s; this one step took 499 s of
that. Hosted runners are saturated (Code Quality jobs waited 4–18 minutes in
the queue on 2026-11-20), so every runner-minute removed from a per-PR job
shortens the queue for all PRs and shortens each PR's required-check path.

Evidence:

- Run `44815442914`, job `136565983203`: the step began at 21:19:49.85; the
  first unittest line (`test_access_failure_is_not_absence_or_archive_failure
  ... ok`) arrived at 21:24:01.13, a 251 s gap. The next 14 tests in the same
  class took 0.05–0.3 s each.
- Run `44812337799`, job `136556566039`: the same gap was 112.6 s.
- Local reproduction in a `node:22-bookworm` container (non-root UID, repo
  mounted read-only, Python 3.11): discovery 0.3 s, first test at 0.3 s, all
  546 tests in 236 s. The start-up gap did not reproduce, so it is specific to
  the hosted runner path: `sudo useradd --create-home`, the `sudo chmod o+x`
  loop, `sudo -H -u lifecycle-contract env ...`, Python 3.12 from the
  hostedtoolcache, or the first test's work under that user on the runner VM.
- unittest `-v` prints a test's line only when the test ends, so the gap
  covers useradd, the chmod loop, sudo start-up, discovery and the first test.

## How

1. Instrument the step once: print `date +%s.%N` (or use `time`) around
   `useradd`, the chmod loop and the `sudo -H -u` launch, and run discovery
   with a small timer, e.g. `python3 -X importtime` or a pre-flight
   `python3 -c 'import time; ...'` under the same `sudo -u`. Push, read the
   job log, and attribute the gap.
2. Fix the identified cause at its source, for example by avoiding a slow
   account-creation or PAM path, or by moving one-off work out of the first
   test. Do not run the contracts as root, drop the separate UID, skip the
   census, or move the step out of a required job.
3. Remove the temporary instrumentation, or keep one compact timing line if
   it is cheap and useful.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_absence.py`

## Acceptance

- On the fix PR's own Code Quality run, the gap between the step start and the
  first test line is under 15 s, and the step is under 300 s.
- All contract tests still pass in CI, with the same user separation.
- PR body records the measured cause and before/after step durations.

</details>

title: fix(runtime): interactive Fable sessions stall on empty turns and argument-less tool calls with no cause note
body:
## What

Interactive OpenCode sessions on `claude-fable-5-2` return control to the user mid-task with nothing said, so the owner has to type "continue" repeatedly. Detect these dead turns and either continue once automatically or tell the model why it stopped.

## Why

Observed first-hand in one interactive session on 2026-11-20 (aidevops v3.39.249, OpenCode v1.19.6, model `claude-fable-5-2`, session `ses_e05d2f785ffeQCSKEcsvcfBK8Y`). The owner typed "continue" four times in an hour (21:37Z, 22:06Z, 22:14Z, 22:35Z) and reported that "these fable sessions keep stalling without continuing".

Three distinct dead turns, in order:

1. **Turn ends straight after tool results.** After a context compaction, the turn ran one batch of four tool calls (two Read, pre-edit check, memory recall). All four returned successfully. No text and no further tool call followed; control went back to the user.
2. **Completely empty assistant turn.** The next "continue" (22:06Z) produced an assistant message with no text and no tool calls.
3. **Write call with no arguments.** The next "continue" (22:14Z) ran several tool batches, then emitted a `Write` call with no `filePath` and no `content`. The result was `Tool execution aborted` and the turn ended. The model had been planning one large new file (a canvas renderer) in its reasoning just before.

For item 3, the GH#39151 output-limit note ("Your previous response hit the configured output-token limit...") was **not** visible to the model on the following turn. So either the finish reason was not `length`, or `createOutputLimitNotice()` did not fire.

Unverified hypothesis: reasoning tokens count toward the per-response output cap. A long planning pass can use the whole cap before any visible text or tool argument is emitted, which would explain both the empty turn (2) and the argument-less Write (3). GH#39151 covers only `finish === "length"` and advises sectioned writes; it does not cover a response whose budget went on reasoning, or a turn that ends empty for another reason.

## Reproducer

Not yet reduced. Start from the session above:

**Symptom command:** `sqlite3 -readonly <data>/opencode.db "select datetime(time_created/1000,'unixepoch') t, data->>'finish' finish, data->>'$.tokens.output' out_tok, data->>'$.tokens.reasoning' reason_tok, (select count(*) from part p where p.message_id = message.id) parts from message where session_id = 'ses_e05d2f785ffeQCSKEcsvcfBK8Y' and data->>'role' = 'assistant' and time_created > 1795210000000 order by time_created"`

**Expected:** every assistant message that ends a turn has visible text or a completed tool call, or the next turn carries a note that says why it did not.

**Actual:** not captured. From inside the live session, `sqlite3 -readonly` printed the schema once and then failed three times with `unable to open database file (14)` on the live database, so the finish reasons and token counts for the three dead turns still need to be read from outside the session. Check the `part` table and column names against the schema before running.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-turn-state.mjs` (`createOutputLimitNotice`, about line 205)
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` (where the notice is observed and injected)
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-output-limit-notice.mjs`
- Other paths cannot be known until step 1 identifies the finish reasons.

1. Read the three dead turns from the session database and record finish reason, output tokens, reasoning tokens and part count for each. This decides the rest.
2. Extend the one-shot notice to every dead-turn shape found: an assistant message that finishes with no text part and no completed tool call, and a tool part aborted with empty input. The note should name the cause and the remedy: plan in smaller steps, then write files in sections of under ~120 lines.
3. If the data shows reasoning used the whole output cap, say so in the note. Consider whether the cap or the reasoning budget for this model needs changing in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs`.
4. Consider one bounded automatic continuation for an interactive session whose todo list still has an `in_progress` item, following the keepalive relay pattern. Never more than one per user turn, so a broken model cannot loop.

Reference pattern: the GH#39151 implementation in the same files.

## Verification

- The symptom command, run for a session that reproduces the problem, shows a note injected on the turn after each dead turn.
- `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-output-limit-notice.mjs` passes with new cases for an empty assistant message and an aborted tool part with empty input.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
