title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #38918 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #38918

**Parent issue:** #38918 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** consolidated: cut remaining git/sudo subprocess fan-out in worktree archive lifecycle (#38675 targets)
**Parent labels:** `enhancement,auto-dispatch,status:blocked,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidated,consolidation-in-progress,needs-ai-recovery`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #38918 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#38918 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 38918 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:blocked,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:blocked` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:blocked` — the parent carries `status:blocked`, which records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership, so the successor keeps it and stays held until that blocker is resolved. Keep the blocker text in the merged body. Never copy the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #38918, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 38918 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 38918 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 38918 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 38918 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38918" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #38918 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #38918.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

_Supersedes #38824 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Continue the subprocess fan-out reduction from #38675, which closed before its verification targets were met (PR #38813 used `Resolves` on a self-declared partial; root cause tracked in #38823). Merged so far: #38681 (procfs cwd fan-out), #38780 (canonical-git probe short-circuit), #38805 (git shim `dirname`, per-pass platform lookup), #38813 (single `rev-parse` in `fetch_preservation`), #38841 (reuse resolved admin dir in archive restore, partial), #38898 (shim inode self-skip and per-classification guard probe memo; tracked under #38896, `Ref #38824`), #38913 (`capture_bundle` in `worktree_archive_git.py` resolves object format, objects path and HEAD in one `rev-parse`, 3 spawns to 1).

Remaining repeats recorded in PR #38805: per-path `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` / `--git-common-dir` / `config` (about 15 each per case) in `worktree_archive_git.py` / `worktree_archive_snapshot.py`, and about 106 `sudo` inspector calls per scan on hosts with many unreadable pids.

Remaining after #38913 (per @vladimirdulov): caller-module git call reductions (state/fingerprint/runtime_config/administration/objects), sudo inspector fan-out, shim cost tracked in #38896. The <300 s target is not yet met.

## Why

Parent goal: archive fixture timeouts resolved (see #38658 canary acceptance and `todo/research/archive-fixture-timeouts-gh38659.md`). Without this the 183-test archive suite still runs well over 300 s. PR #38841 profiled the suite (2126 s; 278 `worktree-archive-helper.sh` calls account for 1189 s): in-scope Python repeats are about 2% of wall time; the cost is the number of `git` calls made by `worktree-archive-helper.sh` and the state/fingerprint/runtime_config/administration/objects modules, multiplied by per-call shim cost.

## How

- Re-profile one case first (`AIDEVOPS_RECOVERY_TIMING_LOG`, see `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_timing.py`, or strace execve) to confirm the current top repeats after the merged PRs.
- Remove repeats by caching within one invocation only. Reference pattern: #38813's single `rev-parse` for admin and common dir in `worktree_archive_git.py`, and #38913's single `rev-parse` in `capture_bundle`.
- Cut `git` calls in `worktree-archive-helper.sh` and the `worktree_archive_state` / `_fingerprint` / `_runtime_config` / `_administration` / `_objects` modules with the same per-invocation caching rule (for example one `rev-parse` with several flags, reuse of an already resolved admin/common dir, one `diff --cached --raw` per pass).
- Then address the `sudo` inspector fan-out (about 106 calls per scan) in `worktree-process-providers.sh` / `worktree_process_proc.py`.
- Keep the canonical Git shim and guard (`.agents/scripts/git`, `canonical-git-command-guard.py`, `canonical_git_*.py`, `runtime-env.sh`) **out of scope here**; their per-call cost is tracked in #38896 with its own verdict-preserving constraints.
- If the targets still are not met after the caller reduction, deliver with `For #<this issue>`, include the before/after table, and state what remains for #38896.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`.
- Environment note (per @vladimirdulov on #38913): 3 canonical-restore cases error at `restore-proof:unsafe-archive` when the tmpdir is symlinked (resolve check in `RestorationProof.__init__`); use a non-symlinked tmpdir when measuring.

## Constraints

Keep private-ref, process, source-drift and retirement guards and unknown/tracked content protection. Never cache across a guard re-check. Do not raise timeouts as the fix. Do not edit the canonical Git shim or guard files in this issue. If one PR cannot meet the targets, link it with `For #<this issue>` and record what remains. Do not close with `Resolves` unless every target below is met.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` finishes in under 300 s on the same machine, with before/after timing table in the PR.
- [ ] The 3 slowest cases each run under 10 s.
- [ ] `test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `test-worktree-archive-helper.sh` and `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` still pass.

title: t19223: full-loop: runtime-pending held-PR route for Critical/High runtime risk; merge helper re-checks runtime evidence
body:
## What

Give headless workers a legitimate route for "implemented, but the runtime check needs a capability this runner lacks", and close the merge-time gap that let an unverified Critical change get through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`.

1. `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --testing-level runtime-pending --testing "<runtime check still needed and why this runner cannot run it>"` opens the PR. The PR body gets `- **Verification:** runtime-pending — <reason>` and the `hold-for-review` label is added at creation. CI and review bots run, the issue keeps an open linked PR so it is not re-implemented, and the Pulse merge pass already refuses `hold-for-review` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh` `_pulse_merge_live_state_gate`).
2. The existing refusal "<Risk> runtime risk requires runtime-verified evidence; PR body generation blocked." names both routes: run the check and record it as `runtime-verified`, or open a held PR with `runtime-pending`.
3. `full-loop-helper.sh merge` refuses a PR whose `## Runtime Testing` section declares `Verification: runtime-pending`, or declares Critical/High risk without `runtime-verified`. In headless sessions it also refuses a PR carrying `hold-for-review` or `needs-maintainer-review`.

## Why

Evidence from 2026-11-20 (`~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl`, fingerprint `0738181c7fb715c10ad8e589`):

- In a private managed plugin repository, an issue about deposit order display was implemented three times: 17:21Z, 19:13Z and 21:10Z. Each attempt pushed the same commit and ended `runner_capability_unmet`, because commit-and-pr classifies the payment/billing diff as Critical and the runner has no review copy with Stripe test mode. The classifier rightly refuses explicit downgrades, so there was no legitimate route.
- The fourth attempt (22:24Z) bypassed commit-and-pr with `gh-write-helper.sh pr create --draft`. The runtime continuation prompt ("MUST post the MERGE_SUMMARY ... continue through review, merge") then led the worker to run `gh pr ready` and `full-loop-helper.sh merge`. That merge passed every helper gate and failed only on a shell timeout. The Pulse merge pass was waiting on CI. A maintainer session applied `hold-for-review` to stop it.
- 14 worker excerpts since 2026-09 hit this refusal. Most recovered by recording test evidence as runtime-verified.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

## How

- `full-loop-helper-risk.sh`: add the `runtime-pending` testing level and the clearer refusal message.
- `full-loop-helper.sh`: add `hold-for-review` to the extra labels when the testing level is runtime-pending; update the help text.
- `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: add the runtime-evidence refusal and the headless hold-label refusal, reusing the closure metadata read.
- `test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh`: add the runtime-pending cases. `full-loop.md`: add one line to the Runtime Testing Gate section.
- Reference pattern: `_merge_check_closing_guards` / `_merge_check_parent_task_keywords` in `full-loop-helper-merge.sh` (a merge-time recheck of creation-time invariants for PRs opened outside commit-and-pr, GH#37690). Parse the `## Runtime Testing` section with the same regexes as `_inherit_pr_runtime_metadata` in `full-loop-helper-commit.sh`.
- PRs without a `## Runtime Testing` section stay mergeable. 131 of 200 merged worker PRs in a high-volume app repository and 37 of 200 in this repository in the last 14 days have no section, because other helpers create them, so a missing section is not evidence of risk.
- The verifier unblocks by re-running commit-and-pr with `--testing-level runtime-verified --testing "<evidence>"` (this refreshes the Verification line) and removing `hold-for-review`.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` passes, with new cases: runtime-pending is accepted for Critical/High with a reason, refused without a reason, and the body carries `runtime-pending`.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge` refuses a PR body that declares runtime-pending, and refuses a headless merge of a PR with `hold-for-review`.

body:
_Supersedes #38918 — this issue is the consolidated spec._
Lineage: #38918 itself superseded #38824.

## What

Finish the subprocess fan-out reduction in the worktree archive lifecycle (originally #38675) so the archive suite meets its timing targets. Two partial deliveries since the last consolidation, plus earlier ones, are merged:

- Earlier: #38681 (procfs cwd fan-out), #38780 (canonical-git probe short-circuit), #38805 (git shim `dirname`, per-pass platform lookup), #38813 (single `rev-parse` in `fetch_preservation`), #38841 (reuse resolved admin dir in archive restore), #38898 (shim inode self-skip, guard probe memo), #38913 (`capture_bundle` single `rev-parse`), #38919, #38930, #38931, #38935, #38944, #38961 (caller modules share one resolved admin/common dir per pass), #39002 (shim/guard split).
- #39301: retirement-guard evidence batched (one claim check, one registry spawn, one `git worktree list`, one process snapshot). `safety-guards` stage median 1951 to 805 ms; suite 472.2 s OK.
- #39333 (`6ca1192ee6`): all unresolved protected same-user PIDs inspected with one read-only `sudo ... --cwds PID...` call (106 calls of about 3.9-4.2 s became 1 call of about 0.28-0.40 s). Older inspector, refused/timed-out/malformed response falls back to per-PID; unresolved links stay degraded (fail closed).
- #39453 (`3cefbf0e5d`): one `index_dirs` / `ls-files --stage` read per pass; intent-to-add `git diff` pair only when an empty-blob entry exists (`intent_to_add_differs`, keeping the #39465 always-compare rule); `administration(dirs=...)` reuses resolved dirs; one `rev-parse` probe in `worktree-archive-helper.sh`. Compact lifecycle case 239 to 190 git spawns (-20%).
- #39528 (`8505cc2b5d`): one `rev-parse` for admin and common dirs in `worktree_lifetime_owner.py`; scratch bundle setup uses `init --initial-branch` plus one `update-ref --stdin`; admin dir passed to `auto-merge-capture` and `runtime_config capture`; AUTO_MERGE `cat-file` skipped only for the exact OID validated by `administration()` in the same pass; merge capture reads one `ls-files -v --stage`. Shimmed-git spawns over 34 tests: 2807 to 2563 (-8.7%).

Still open (not started, per @marcusquinn 2026-11-20T18:40Z):

- Per-path `rev-parse`/`config` in `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_git.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py` (around L58-61, L143-149, L169-197).
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-recovery.sh` around L93 per-path call.
- Callers: `worktree_archive_merge_capture.py` around L45-61, `worktree_archive_unsealed.py` around L111-116, `worktree_archive_objects.py` around L65, `worktree_archive_local_verify.py` around L50/104/122.
- Per-test fixture setup (bare repo + clone + worktree creation) dominates remaining time: shared class-level fixtures, or `git` plumbing in place of porcelain helpers (non-security candidates).
- Spawn-level remainders recorded earlier: per-path `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` / `--git-common-dir` / `config` repeats; 15x `config --path --get core.worktree` guard probes; helpers outside the original scope (`canonical-recovery-helper.sh`, `scratch-worktree-helper.sh`) doing separate `--git-dir` / `--git-common-dir` / `--show-toplevel` calls.

## Why

Parent goal: archive fixture timeouts resolved (see #38658 canary acceptance and `todo/research/archive-fixture-timeouts-gh38659.md`). PR #38841 profiled the suite (2126 s; 278 `worktree-archive-helper.sh` calls account for 1189 s): in-scope Python repeats are about 2% of wall time; the cost is the number of `git` calls made by `worktree-archive-helper.sh` and the state/fingerprint/runtime_config/administration/objects modules, multiplied by per-call shim cost.

## How

- Re-profile one case first (`AIDEVOPS_RECOVERY_TIMING_LOG`, see `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_timing.py`, or strace execve) to confirm the current top repeats after the merged PRs. Measure with a paired base/head run on a quiet host; before attributing a regression check the slowest-test log in `worktree_archive_*` restore/verify paths (`seed_base` fetch, `verify_imported_base` fsck, `base_graph_missing` rev-list).
- Remove repeats by caching within one invocation only. Reference patterns: #38813's single `rev-parse` for admin and common dir in `worktree_archive_git.py`, #38913's single `rev-parse` in `capture_bundle`, #39453's `administration(dirs=...)`, #39528's reuse of same-pass evidence.

- Then evaluate fixture sharing in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` (shared class-level fixtures, or `git` plumbing instead of porcelain). Test fixtures must not weaken what each case proves.
- Root `sudo` CWD inspection batching is DONE (#39333; maintainer-approved 2026-11-19 with constraints: read-only, fail closed with `process-unavailable` per path, canonical validated absolute worktree paths only, no more process detail than the single-path inspector). Do not reopen it here; #39335 tracks batch timeout degradation and 4096-PID chunking, and #39344 tracks eight shell suites failing on `main`.
- Keep the canonical Git shim and guard (`.agents/scripts/git`, `canonical-git-command-guard.py`, `canonical_git_*.py`, `runtime-env.sh`) **out of scope**; shim/guard cost was handled under #38896 and #39002 with verdict-preserving constraints.
- Coordination: #39525 (worker branch `feature/gh38918-remeasure`) changes `fetch_preservation`/`verify_administration`, which do not overlap.
- If the targets still are not met after the reduction, deliver with `For #<this issue>`, include the before/after table, and state what remains.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`.
- Environment note (per @vladimirdulov on #38913): 3 canonical-restore cases error at `restore-proof:unsafe-archive` when the tmpdir is symlinked (resolve check in `RestorationProof.__init__`); use a non-symlinked tmpdir when measuring.

title: release status blocks >180s in worker-lifecycle retirement retry after printing its report
body:
## Observed

`aidevops release status <PR>` printed its full report (lane, executor, receipt, tag discovery, publication fields) and then blocked for over 180 seconds after this line:

```
[worker-lifecycle] relinquished the run of this session; retrying retirement once
```

The interactive Bash tool killed it at its 180 s timeout. The report had already printed, so the hang came from session-retirement cleanup after the read, not from the status read itself.

Related evidence from the same session (`aidevops release reconcile` / `release patch`, aidevops v3.39.250, macOS):

- `[worker-lifecycle] retirement-refused status=unavailable reason=OperationalError detail=database-locked rc=2`
- `[worker-lifecycle] retirement-refused status=unavailable reason=ValueError detail=not-enrolled rc=2`

Other `release reconcile` runs finished the retry in a few seconds (`"status": "retired"`). The slow case looks like the retry waiting on a locked lifecycle DB with no short bound.

## Expected

A read-only command such as `release status` should not block on worker-lifecycle retirement. Either skip retirement on read-only subcommands, or bound the retry (for example, a few seconds of SQLite `busy_timeout`, then give up with a one-line warning).

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/` worker-lifecycle retirement path: search `rg -n "retrying retirement once" .agents/scripts/`
- The `aidevops release status` entry point: search `rg -n "release status|cmd_status" .agents/scripts/release*`

## Verification

- With another process holding the lifecycle DB write lock, `time aidevops release status <PR>` returns within about 10 s and prints a warning, not an indefinite wait.
- An unlocked `aidevops release status <PR>` output is unchanged.

title: fix(seo): Bing Webmaster guide names the wrong credential and lacks new-site setup and IndexNow steps
body:
## What

The Bing Webmaster guide covers reporting and URL submission but not first-time setup of a new site, and the framework has no IndexNow guidance at all. Setting up a new site today needed a hand-written script. The guide also names a credential that the framework's own scripts do not read.

## Evidence (interactive session, 2026-11-20, aidevops v3.39.249)

A new site was added to Bing Webmaster, verified and submitted entirely through the API, with no browser sign-in. Calls and responses, with `example.com` standing in for the real domain:

| Step | Call | Response |
|------|------|----------|
| List sites | `GET GetUserSites` | `{"d":[{"Url","IsVerified","DnsVerificationCode","AuthenticationCode"},...]}` |
| Add site | `POST AddSite` `{"siteUrl":"https://example.com/"}` | HTTP 200 `{"d":null}` |
| Get DNS code | `GET GetUserSites` | new entry with `IsVerified:false` and `DnsVerificationCode` of the form `<32 hex>.example.com` |
| DNS | CNAME `<32 hex>.example.com` to `verify.bing.com` (not proxied) | resolves |
| Verify | `POST VerifySite` `{"siteUrl":"https://example.com/"}` | HTTP 200 `{"d":true}` |
| Sitemap | `POST SubmitFeed` `{"siteUrl","feedUrl"}` | HTTP 200 `{"d":null}` |

IndexNow, same session: a 32-character hex key in `/<key>.txt` at the site root, then `POST https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow` with JSON `{"host","key","keyLocation","urlList"}` returned HTTP 202 (received, key check pending; 200 means accepted).

Gaps found by search:

- `rg -n -i "AddSite|VerifySite|GetUserSites" .agents/seo/bing-webmaster-tools.md` returns nothing.
- `rg -n -i "indexnow" .agents --glob "*.md" --glob "*.sh"` returns nothing.
- `.agents/seo/bing-webmaster-tools.md` lines 20 and 26 name the credential `BING_API_KEY`. `.agents/scripts/seo-export-bing.sh` (lines 42-46, 237-247) and `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-webmaster.sh` (lines 170-181) read `BING_WEBMASTER_API_KEY` and account-suffixed forms of it. An agent following the guide looks for a secret that is not there.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/seo/bing-webmaster-tools.md`
  - Rename the credential to `BING_WEBMASTER_API_KEY` (and mention the `BING_WEBMASTER_API_KEY_<ACCOUNT>` form) to match the two scripts above. Show it used through `aidevops secret <NAME> -- <command>`, not by sourcing `credentials.sh`.
  - Add a "New site setup" section with the six steps in the table above.
  - Add a short "IndexNow" section: key file at the site root, the POST body, and what 200, 202, 403 and 422 mean.
- Follow the existing section pattern in the same file (`### Submit URL`, `### Sitemap Submit`): one heading, one `curl` block, placeholders only.
- Paths that cannot be known in advance: whether `.agents/seo/bing-webmaster-tools/SKILL.md` is generated from the guide or needs the same edit by hand. Check how it is produced before editing it.

## Out of scope

- A new helper script. The calls are single `curl` commands; a doc section is enough unless a second user of the flow appears.

## Verification

- `rg -n "BING_API_KEY\b" .agents/seo/` returns nothing.
- `rg -n -i "AddSite|VerifySite|indexnow" .agents/seo/bing-webmaster-tools.md` returns the new sections.
- Run the repository's markdown lint on the edited file.
- The API calls themselves need a real Bing key and a domain, so they cannot be re-run in CI. The responses above are the evidence for them.

title: cross-review returns no results on the OpenCode backend: text extraction does not match the runner's JSON event stream
body:
## What happened

`compare-models-helper.sh cross-review` returned no results on three attempts in one interactive OpenCode session (OpenCode v1.19.6). Each ended with:

```text
[WARNING] Only 0 model(s) returned results. Need at least 2 for comparison.
```

The same model, prompt and timeout through `runner-helper.sh run` directly returned a full answer in 116 seconds. So the models and credentials were fine; the cross-review path lost the answers.

## Evidence

| Attempt | Models | How it was run | Result |
|---------|--------|----------------|--------|
| 1 | `google/gemini-pro-latest,google/gemini-flash-latest` | `aidevops_bounded_operation` | exit 1 after 3.9 s; each `<model>.json` is 0 bytes; error logs stop after the `Model:` line. No Google credential is configured (`opencode auth list` shows OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenCode, OpenCode Go), and nothing said so |
| 2 | `opencode/gemini-4-neon,opencode/gemini-4-argon` | `aidevops_bounded_operation` | exit 1 after 2.0 s; same empty files |
| 3 | same as 2 | Bash tool, `--timeout 240` | ran the full 240 s; `<model>.json` held one line, a `step_start` event stamped 218 s after the run ID; no text event |
| Control | `opencode/gemini-4-neon` | `runner-helper.sh create`, then `run ... --timeout 240 --format json` with `--workdir` set to a small temp directory | answer in 116 s (a one-word test prompt took 11 s) |

Three separate causes look likely:

1. **The text extraction does not match the output format.** `.agents/scripts/compare-models-cross-review-lib.sh:605` runs `jq -r '.parts[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text'`. `runner-helper.sh run --format json` on the OpenCode backend prints one JSON event per line, with the text at `.part.text` on lines where `.type == "text"`:

   ```json
   {"type":"text","timestamp":1795218655236,"sessionID":"...","part":{"type":"text","text":"OK"}}
   ```

   `.parts[]?` matches nothing in that stream, so `<model>.txt` is empty and line 613 marks the model failed even when the model answered. Not confirmed end to end, because attempt 3 timed out before a text event arrived.
2. **Slow start inside cross-review.** In attempt 3 the first event arrived 218 s after dispatch; the control run started in seconds. Differences: cross-review defaults `--workdir` to `pwd` (here the aidevops checkout) and runs two models at once. Cause not established.
3. **Fails in about 2 s under `aidevops_bounded_operation`.** The helper dispatches each model in a background subshell; the bounded operation reported `post_exit_descendants_terminated: true`. The helper may be exiting before its children, or the children may be refused. Cause not established.

Also: a model whose provider has no credential fails with no message naming the cause (attempt 1).

## Expected

- A model that answers is counted as a result.
- A missing credential, a timeout and an empty answer are reported as different failures, by name, in the summary line.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/compare-models-cross-review-lib.sh`

## How

- Lines 577-615 (`_cross_review_dispatch_one`): extract text from the event stream (`select(.type == "text") | .part.text`), keeping the old `.parts[]` shape as a fallback if another backend still produces it. Check lines 172-194 (judge path) for the same assumption.
- Lines 625-640 (result collection): say why a model failed (timeout, no text event, runner error) using the error log and the JSON file.
- Reference only, do not edit: `.agents/scripts/runner-helper.sh` line 958 (`--format json` handling) shows the output shape actually produced.

## Verification

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh cross-review \
  --prompt "Reply with the single word OK." \
  --models "<two configured models>" --timeout 120 \
  --workdir "${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}"
```

Passes when both models are listed with their text and the "Only 0 model(s)" warning does not appear. Run it once from the Bash tool and once through `aidevops_bounded_operation`; if the second still fails in a few seconds, cause 3 is real and needs its own fix or a documented limit. Add one unit-level check that feeds a saved event-stream file through the extraction.

## Workaround used

`runner-helper.sh create <name> --model <model> --workdir <small dir>`, then `runner-helper.sh run <name> "<prompt>" --model <model> --timeout 240 --format json`, then `jq -r 'select(.type=="text") | .part.text'`, then `runner-helper.sh destroy <name> --force`.

title: fix(terminal-blocker): trigger revisit never releases holds whose awaited merge already happened
body:
## What happens

`terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh` (GH#38353) never releases a hold whose awaited trigger is the merge of a named same-repository issue or PR, even after that trigger has verifiably happened. Holds wait until a human posts `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` by hand.

Two independent defects cause this.

### 1. `_tbtr_decide` discards correct `trigger_met` verdicts

The validator accepts `trigger_met` only when the model's whole `evidence` string is an exact substring of the bundle's string values joined with newlines (`$haystack | contains($e)`). The linked-issue facts the model must cite are short separate tokens (`"closed"`, `"completed"`, a `closed_at` timestamp), so any useful sentence fails the check. The helper then records the failure branch (`decision=still_pending`, `attempts` unchanged, `next_at = now + 3600`) and posts nothing.

Reproduction on a managed private repo (placeholders used): hold on issue A with `Trigger awaited: Merge of builder fix issue #B ...`; issue B was closed as completed by a merged PR. Rebuilding the bundle with the helper's own `_tbtr_evidence` and calling `ai-research-helper.sh` with the helper's prompt returned:

```
{"decision":"trigger_met","evidence":"Linked issue #B shows \"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"closed_at\":\"<ts>\", titled \"...\", which is after the hold observed at <ts>."}
```

`_tbtr_decide` on the same bundle returned rc 1, and the per-issue record showed the 3600-second failure backoff.

### 2. Linked PR refs carry no merge state

`_tbtr_evidence` projects each referenced number with `gh api repos/<slug>/issues/<n> --jq '{number, title, state, state_reason, closed_at}'`. For a PR, the issues endpoint returns `state: closed` and `state_reason: null` whether or not it merged, so a trigger such as `PR #N ... merged to develop` cannot be confirmed. The model answers `still_pending`, and the backoff doubles up to 7 days. The same endpoint already returns `pull_request.merged_at`; the projection drops it.

## Impact observed

One pass over 221 open `needs-dependency` issues in one managed repo found 13 holds that name a trigger issue or PR in their comments. Four had verifiably met triggers (three issues closed as completed by merged PRs, one merged PR). They had been held for 3 to 60 hours, and one blocked four dependants. All four were released by hand with the helper's own `_tbtr_post_retry`, after checking the hold with `terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active`. Holds whose trigger also needs a deployment, a migration contract phase or a maintainer decision correctly stayed pending.

## Suggested fix

Files: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh`, tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`.

1. In `_tbtr_evidence`, add `merged_at: (.pull_request.merged_at // null)` and `is_pull_request: (.pull_request != null)` to the linked-ref projection.
2. In `_tbtr_decide`, keep the exact-quote rule but apply it to a short `quote` field instead of the free-text `evidence`. Ask for `{"decision", "quote", "evidence"}`, require `quote` (8+ characters) to equal one string value outside `trigger` (for example a `closed_at` or `merged_at` timestamp), and post that quote as the public evidence line. This keeps the anti-fabrication property while accepting real verdicts.
3. Optional fast path, no AI: when the trigger's only same-repo refs are all merged PRs, or issues closed with `state_reason: completed`, and the trigger text names nothing else (no deployment, release, date or maintainer decision), decide `trigger_met` deterministically with evidence built from the bundle. Leave every other trigger to the model.

## Verification

- Unit tests for `_tbtr_decide`: a paraphrased `evidence` plus an exact `quote` timestamp is accepted; a fabricated `quote` is rejected; `still_pending` and `not_external` behave as before.
- A unit test confirming a merged PR ref includes `merged_at` in the bundle.
- On a repo with a hold awaiting a merged PR: `terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh run <slug>` (with `AIDEVOPS_TRIGGER_REVISIT_INTERVAL_S` small) prints `TRIGGER_REVISIT ... decision=trigger_met`, and the issue receives the retry directive.

title: canonical write policy: allow file-tool writes to allowlisted gitignored runtime paths (scheduled tasks)
body:
## Problem

The Claude Code hook `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py` sends every direct file-tool write to `.agents/scripts/canonical-write-policy-helper.py`, and `check_write` denies any target classified `canonical` ("canonical checkouts are read-only session mirrors"). There is no exemption for gitignored runtime output.

On a project hub that is used as an operations workspace, this breaks unattended Claude Code scheduled tasks. Those tasks run in the canonical checkout and write their daily output into gitignored folders (for example `<hub>/automation/logs/<task>/<date>.md` and `<hub>/finance/<area>/runs/<date>/*.facts`). After aidevops was installed:

- A daily billing report lost one processor's data on three days because its facts file could not be written; one day produced no report at all. A real failed payment was missing from the alert.
- Two other daily tasks (closeout report, reply prep) have written no report since the install.
- The shell policy also refuses redirection and heredocs, so the agent cannot fall back to writing through Bash.

Worktrees are the wrong fit for these files: they are gitignored runtime state that other jobs read from the canonical path (launchd jobs, scripts and later runs), so writing them in a linked worktree hides them from every reader.

## Proposal

Add a per-repo allowlist of canonical paths that file tools may write, limited to paths that are gitignored, for example in `.aidevops.json`:

```json
{ "canonical_write_allow": ["automation/logs/", "finance/ar/runs/"] }
```

`check_write` would allow a canonical target only when both are true:
1. The repo-relative path starts with an allowlisted prefix (after realpath resolution, no `..` and no symlink escape).
2. `git check-ignore` reports the path as ignored, so tracked files stay protected.

Every other canonical write keeps the current deny and action.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-write-policy-helper.py` (`check_write`)
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_write_policy_paths.py` (classification helpers)
- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_guard.py` (no change expected; it calls the helper)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh` or a new helper test: allowlisted and ignored allows; allowlisted and tracked denies; not allowlisted denies; symlink escape denies

## Verification

In a repo with `canonical_write_allow: ["logs/"]` and `logs/` in `.gitignore`:
- `canonical-write-policy-helper.py` check-write for `logs/x.md` → allow.
- Same for a tracked file under `logs/` → deny.
- `src/x.py` → deny, as today.

## Workaround in use

The affected task now writes outside the checkout and a project script copies the file in after validating it. This works, but every task needs its own copy step.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: t19224: fix(claim-task-id): blob-less isolated counter fetches so large repos stop timing out at counter discovery
body:
## Task


Make `claim-task-id.sh` counter discovery and CAS in the isolated Git context
(canonical `--repo-path`) transfer only commits and trees, never the whole
branch tip's blobs, so filing an issue in a large repository completes within
`CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30 s).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make `claim-task-id.sh` counter discovery and CAS in the isolated Git context
(canonical `--repo-path`) transfer only commits and trees, never the whole
branch tip's blobs, so filing an issue in a large repository completes within
`CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30 s).

## Why

Interactive filing in a large managed repository fails before allocation:

```text
Using isolated Git context for canonical counter discovery and CAS
git timed out after 30s on HTTPS — retrying via SSH
SSH fallback also timed out after 30s — both transports unavailable
COUNTER_BRANCH_DISCOVERY_ERROR: unable to validate task-id-counter against origin/develop; CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S=30
```

`git ls-remote` to the same remote answered in 1.2 s. The failing step is
`resolve_implicit_counter_branch` fetching the default branch at `--depth=1`
(`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:768-770`) only to read the one-line
`.task-counter`. Measured on 2026-11-21 against that repository (~39,800 files
at the tip):

| Fetch into an empty repo | Time | Transfer |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch --depth=1 --no-tags origin +refs/heads/develop:...` (current) | 48.5 s | 162 MB |
| same plus `--filter=blob:none` | 1.6 s | trees only |
| then `git show origin/develop:.task-counter` (lazy one-blob fetch) | 0.8 s | 1 blob |

Retrying with `CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S=150` allocated normally, confirming the
cause is transfer size, not transport. This is the third round of the same
class: #32692, #32953 and #33154 shallowed these fetches; tips have since
outgrown depth 1.

## Tier

tier:thinking — dispatch-path script (`claim-task-id*`), every repository's
allocation depends on it; partial-clone semantics need care.

## How (Approach)

Constraint that rules out the naive change: the CAS builds commits with
`ls-tree <tip> | sed | git mktree` (`:635`, `:1087`, `:1412`, `:1587`).
`git mktree` verifies every entry exists locally and does not lazy-fetch, so a
blob-less tip of a counter-on-default-branch repository makes it die
("object ... is unavailable"). Also, the first `fetch --filter` registers
`remote.<name>.promisor=true` and `remote.<name>.partialclonefilter`, so every
later fetch in the same isolated repository is filtered too.

Recommended design (isolated context only; linked worktrees and unmanaged
repos keep their shared object store and current behaviour, which must never
become a partial clone):

1. Add one helper beside `_counter_context_is_isolated` (`:175`) that prints
   the isolated fetch args: `--depth=1 --no-tags --filter=blob:none`. Use it at
   every isolated fetch: `:596-606` (`sync_counter_branch`), `:705-708`,
   `:746-749`, `:768-770`, `:953-956` (`_cas_fetch_counter_branch`),
   `:1004-1006`, `:1680-1688`. Keep the explicit refspecs.
2. Make the CAS tree builders tolerate absent unchanged entries in the
   isolated context only: pass `--missing` to the `git mktree` calls listed
   above when `_counter_context_is_isolated`. Entries come from `ls-tree` of a
   real tip, so types are known; only the new `.task-counter` blob is written
   locally (`hash-object -w`).
3. `git show <ref>:.task-counter` / `:TODO.md` now lazily fetch one blob over
   the network. Route those reads in the isolated context through
   `_run_git_with_ssh_fallback "${CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S:-30}"` so a credential
   stall cannot hang them (pattern: the fetch calls at `:747-749`), keeping the
   existing `2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]' || true` handling.
4. Servers that do not support filters print a warning and send the full tip,
   which is today's behaviour; no extra fallback is needed. Confirm the push of
   the CAS commit from the partial context succeeds (it sends only the new
   tree and blob; unchanged entries are reachable from the advertised parent).

If step 2 or 4 cannot be shown safe, the alternative is a second throwaway
bare "tip probe" repository under `${_CLAIM_COUNTER_CONTEXT_ROOT}` for the
read-only default-branch reads (`:712`, `:775`, `:1008`, `:1045`, `:1704`,
`:1710`, `:1738`), leaving the CAS repository unfiltered; document which was
chosen and why in the PR.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-protected-counter-branch.sh`

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Never shallow or filter the shared object store of a canonical checkout or
  linked worktree (see the comments at `:743-745`, `:1002-1003`).
- Do not raise `CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S`, the CAS retry budget or wall timeout to
  hide the transfer; that is the throttle the policy forbids.
- Bash 3.2 compatibility and the existing `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` patterns stay.
- The isolated-context fixtures live in
  `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-protected-counter-branch.sh`
  (canonical-path claims asserting "Using isolated Git context ...", around
  `:485-490`); extend those. File-backed fixture remotes need
  `git config uploadpack.allowFilter true` to honour filters.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no change to counter semantics, CAS retry policy, issue
creation, or non-isolated contexts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An online `--dry-run` claim against a canonical checkout of a large
  repository (tip over ~100 MB) completes discovery with the default 30 s
  timeout; record the elapsed time in the PR.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-protected-counter-branch.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guarantee: a fixture whose counter lives on the default branch
  (no dedicated branch) still allocates through the isolated context, and the
  pushed commit changes only `.task-counter`.
- [ ] Linked-worktree and non-canonical claims make no partial-clone or shallow
  changes to the shared repository config (`remote.*.promisor`,
  `partialclonefilter`, `shallow` file absent afterwards).
- [ ] Existing claim-task-id suites pass unchanged
  (`git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*claim-task-id*'`).

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:166-179` — `_counter_git`, `_counter_context_is_isolated`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:245-292` — isolated context creation
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:378-450` — `_run_git_with_ssh_fallback`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:729-790` — `resolve_implicit_counter_branch` (the observed failure)
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:949-957` — `_cas_fetch_counter_branch`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh:1570-1600` — CAS commit construction

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: orphan recovery opens a duplicate PR when the worker's own PR create races it
body:
## What

Stop `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` in `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` from leaving a duplicate PR open when the worker's own `gh pr create` lands in the same window.

## Observed (2026-11-21, private managed project repo)

- Two open PRs to `develop` had the same head branch `feature/auto-<ts>-gh<N>` and the same head commit. Both were created at `00:24:01Z`.
- One was the worker's PR (`GH#<N>: fix: ...`, closing reference). The other was the orphan-recovery PR (`GH#<N>: chore: auto-recover orphaned worker branch`, body marker `aidevops:orphan-recovery worker_branch_orphan session=issue-<N>`).

## Why

`_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` re-checks for an existing PR before creating one (`_pr_handoff_state_for_branch_or_issue`, t3195/GH#21889), but that is check-then-act. When the worker's PR creation is still in flight, the probe returns `absent`, and both creates succeed.

## How

- In `_create_orphan_recovery_pr` (or immediately after it returns 0 in `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr`), list open PRs for `--head <branch>` against the same base. If any open PR other than the recovery PR exists, close the recovery PR with a short "duplicate of #X" comment, keep the branch, and return 0 so the caller records the worker PR as the handoff.
- Keep the existing pre-check; the post-create reconcile only closes the window.
- Add a case to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-orphan-recovery-pr-base.sh` (or a sibling test) where the `gh pr list --head` stub returns a second open PR after creation, asserting the recovery PR is closed and the branch is not deleted.

title: t19226: canonical write policy: paths inside .git/ classify as outside and allow direct file-tool writes
body:
## Task


The canonical write policy classifies paths inside a repository's `.git/` directory as `outside` a Git worktree, so it allows them. A direct file-tool write to `<canonical>/.git/hooks/pre-commit` or `<canonical>/.git/config` is allowed today.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The canonical write policy classifies paths inside a repository's `.git/` directory as `outside` a Git worktree, so it allows them. A direct file-tool write to `<canonical>/.git/hooks/pre-commit` or `<canonical>/.git/config` is allowed today.

## Evidence

Found while implementing GH#39573. On `main`:

```text
canonical-write-policy-helper.py check-write --cwd <canonical> --path <canonical>/.git/hooks/pre-commit
→ "decision": "allow", "reason": "write target is outside canonical worktrees",
  "target": {"classification": "outside", "reason": "path is outside a Git worktree"}
```

`classify_location` (`.agents/scripts/canonical_write_policy_paths.py:68-79`) runs `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, which returns `false` inside the Git directory. The result becomes `outside`. The same applies to a linked worktree's shared common dir and to case-folded spellings such as `.GIT/` on case-insensitive filesystems.

## Why

Git metadata (hooks, config, refs) is more sensitive than tracked content. File-tool writes there bypass the canonical guard and the hook-integrity guidance in `workflows/pre-edit.md` "Git Hook Status Without External-Directory Access".

## How

In `classify_location`, or in `check_write` before the outside branch, detect a target whose probe sits inside a Git directory. Use `git rev-parse --is-inside-git-dir`, or compare the realpath against the absolute `--git-dir`/`--git-common-dir` of the containing repository. Return a `deny` with a dedicated reason and action, for example `git metadata is not writable through file tools`. Keep the legitimate outside-Git writes allowed: temp dirs and `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_write_policy_paths.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-write-policy-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `check-write` for `<canonical>/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, `<canonical>/.git/config` and `<linked-worktree common dir>/hooks/x` returns `deny`.
- [ ] `check-write` for a path outside any Git repository (for example under `$TMPDIR`) still returns `allow`, and linked-worktree writes remain allowed.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs
python3 -m py_compile .agents/scripts/canonical_write_policy_paths.py .agents/scripts/canonical-write-policy-helper.py
```

title: t19227: fix(pulse): stampless interactive auto-release leaves status:claimed on unassigned issues and skips the audit log
body:
## Task


`_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` handles `status:in-review`, `status:in-progress` and `status:queued` by moving the issue to `status:available` through `set_issue_status`. Any other label set, including `status:claimed` (the label `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` applies), falls through to a bare raw call at line ~997:

```bash
elif gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$slug" --remove-assignee "$runner_user" ...
```

That call removes the owner but leaves `status:claimed`, producing an **unassigned, claimed** issue. It also bypasses `gh_issue_edit_safe`, so the unassign has no `gh-audit.log` record. `_PIR_STATUS_CLAIMED` is already defined at line 83 but is unused here; GH#35035 added the active-status reset for in-progress/queued ("otherwise the reassign pass re-claims it") and missed `claimed`.

## Done when

- [ ] A stampless, origin:interactive, open issue assigned to the runner with `status:claimed` and older than the threshold is transitioned to `status:available` with the runner unassigned in a single `set_issue_status` call; `status:claimed` is not left on the issue.
- [ ] The remaining bare-unassign branch no longer calls raw `gh issue edit` (uses `gh_issue_edit_safe`).
- [ ] Negative guarantee: issues with a live interactive claim stamp, issues within the age threshold, and `status:in-review` issues with an open PR are still left untouched (existing test cases keep passing).
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` is clean; `affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base` shows no regressions.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — in `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` (around lines 976-1000):
  1. Include `$_PIR_STATUS_CLAIMED` in the active-status branch (currently `"$_PIR_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS"` / `"$_PIR_STATUS_QUEUED"`), so a stale stampless `status:claimed` is reset to `status:available` with `--remove-assignee "$runner_user"` in one `set_issue_status` call. Match labels as comma-delimited tokens (`",${labels_csv},"` == `*",status:claimed,"*`) like the in-review branch, not substring matching.
  2. Route the remaining bare-unassign branch through the audited `gh_issue_edit_safe` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:725`) instead of raw `gh issue edit`, so it records an `issue_edit` audit entry. Keep `>/dev/null 2>&1` / return-code semantics unchanged.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh` — add one case modelled on "Stampless aged release of an in-progress issue resets it to available" (lines 220-240), with labels `origin:interactive` + `status:claimed`, asserting the edit includes `--add-label status:available` and `--remove-label status:claimed` (or the `set_issue_status` equivalent). Part 5 (t2148, lines 305-344) covers the bare-unassign branch with a `gh` stub that only answers `issue list`/`issue edit`; `gh_issue_edit_safe` takes before/after snapshots, so adjust that stub only as needed to keep its assertion meaningful.

### Reference pattern

The in-progress/queued branch directly above (`set_issue_status "$issue_num" "$slug" "available" --remove-assignee "$runner_user"`), and `_normalize_clear_status_labels` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:67-78`.

### Hazards

- Do not change the 1 h `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD` default, the stamp check, the open-PR guard on the in-review branch, or `_filter_non_task_issues`.
- Do not touch `no-auto-dispatch`, `hold-for-review`, `needs-*` or `origin:interactive` labels.
- Out of scope (note in PR only if observed): whether "no stamp" can be wrong when the same GitHub login runs interactive sessions on a second device (claim stamps are per-host under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/`); `set_issue_status` itself not writing audit records (documented in `reference/gh-audit-log.md` "Verified lifecycle policy").

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` handles `status:in-review`, `status:in-progress` and `status:queued` by moving the issue to `status:available` through `set_issue_status`. Any other label set, including `status:claimed` (the label `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` applies), falls through to a bare raw call at line ~997:

```bash
elif gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$slug" --remove-assignee "$runner_user" ...
```

That call removes the owner but leaves `status:claimed`, producing an **unassigned, claimed** issue. It also bypasses `gh_issue_edit_safe`, so the unassign has no `gh-audit.log` record. `_PIR_STATUS_CLAIMED` is already defined at line 83 but is unused here; GH#35035 added the active-status reset for in-progress/queued ("otherwise the reassign pass re-claims it") and missed `claimed`.

## Why (observed evidence, 2026-11-15..19, private repo issue numbers withheld where needed)

- On the alexey runner, the pulse log line `Stampless interactive auto-release: unassigned alex-solovyev from #28534 in <private repo> (>3600s old, no stamp)` matches the GitHub timeline: `status:claimed` added 07:45:46; unassigned 09:35:16 with **no label change**; owner closed it at 12:47 and removed `status:claimed` from the unassigned issue. - Consequence 3: audit-trail gap: the unassign is invisible in `gh-audit.log`.

## Context

Found while triaging GH audit alerts #38638 and #38641 (both closed as expected). Related: GH#35035 (churn fix that added the in-progress/queued reset), #39334/t19179 (24 h orphaned-status healing, which repairs this state after the fact but not at its source).

title: t19228: fix(full-loop): non-required check snapshot keeps the generic 15s read budget...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19228` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-21
**Tags:** `bug` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(full-loop): non-required check snapshot keeps the generic 15s read budget and defers merges under transport pacing

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` defers every attempt with `non-required check snapshot read exit 124` while local REST pacing is active, even though all required checks pass and the API is healthy. Give the non-required check snapshot the same merge read timeout every other merge read already uses (GH#38535).

## Why

Observed 2026-11-21 on PR #39569 (all 5 required checks passed, merge state CLEAN):

- Three consecutive `full-loop-helper.sh merge 39569` attempts failed in 55–100s with `Merge deferred by GitHub read admission: non-required check snapshot read exit 124; preserve the PR and retry`.
- With `LOGFILE` captured, both the first read and the retry failed at the check-runs fetch:
  `pre-merge snapshot: check-runs fetch failed for head 9b411f1f102e ... transient check-set read rc=124 ...; retrying once with 10s timeout ... check-runs fetch failed`.
- The same `_pmrc_snapshot_checks_json` call run standalone (same head, same minute) succeeded in 3s: two check-run pages (101 runs, 369 KB raw) plus the commit status.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` showed the merge-window `commits/:id` page taking 9,039 ms for a 304, compared with 0.5–0.9 s outside the merge. Local transport demand was about 164 attempts/min, and the core pacing interval was about 0.56 s, so paced admission used most of the budget.
- Setting `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT=60` on the same command merged the PR in 4 minutes (merge SHA `0143138431`), confirming that the budget, not a CI or API failure, blocked the merge.

Root cause: `_full_loop_enforce_nonrequired_check_gate` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`) calls `_pmrc_snapshot_checks_with_retry`, which reads through `_pmrc_gh_read` → `_gh_with_timeout read`. That path never goes through `_flm_gh_read_once`, so it keeps the generic `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT` default of 15s (`shared-gh-wrappers.sh:293`). The retry is capped at `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 10s). GH#38535 documented that pacing can take up to 10s inside a read timeout and raised all `_flm_gh_read` merge reads to 60s; this snapshot path was missed. A paginated two-page read plus the status read cannot fit in 15s/10s while pacing is engaged, so every interactive and worker merge defers under load and must be re-run manually.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` `_full_loop_enforce_nonrequired_check_gate`, resolve the merge read timeout with `_flm_merge_read_timeout` (from `full-loop-helper-merge-transport.sh`; fall back to 60 if undeclared or invalid). Invoke `_pmrc_snapshot_checks_with_retry` with `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT=<merge timeout>` and `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30` (the helper's accepted maximum) scoped to that call only.
- Do not change `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` defaults; the pulse merge pass has its own deadline (`_PMP_MERGE_PASS_DEADLINE_EPOCH`) and must keep its bounds.
- Keep fail-closed semantics: a snapshot that still fails defers the merge exactly as now.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`

## Acceptance

- `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR>` with passing required checks no longer defers with `non-required check snapshot read exit 124` when local pacing adds several seconds per page.
- A genuinely failing snapshot read still defers (fail closed), and terminal non-required failures still block.
- Pulse merge-pass bounds are unchanged.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-planning.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-remote-evidence.sh`, and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` pass.
- Runtime: merge this fix's own PR through the worktree's `full-loop-helper.sh merge` without any `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT` override while pacing is active, then confirm in `LOGFILE` that no `check-runs fetch failed` line appears.

</details>

fix(opencode-agent): signed comments match the /opencode trigger gate and run-level concurrency cancels genuine /oc runs

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop aidevops-signed comments from matching the OpenCode `/oc` / `/opencode` trigger gate, in the framework workflow and in every template it ships. Move the global serialization from the workflow level to the mutating job so unrelated comments can no longer cancel a genuine pending `/oc` run.

## Why

Evidence (2026-11-21, `marcusquinn/aidevops`):

- The gate in `.github/workflows/opencode-agent.yml` is `contains(github.event.comment.body, '/oc') || contains(github.event.comment.body, '/opencode')`. Every aidevops signature footer contains `[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)`, and `//opencode.ai` contains `/opencode`, so every signed pulse/worker/interactive comment passes it. The in-script rule (`/(^|\s)\/(oc|opencode)\b/m`) then rejects the comment after Security Validation, Audit Log and Security Block Notification have already used runners.
- `OpenCode AI Agent` created 1,450 runs in about 24h. In a 50-run sample, 30 were `cancelled`, 12 `skipped`, 8 `success`. Cancelled run 44851503197 (triggered by `sonarqubecloud[bot]`) has **zero jobs**. The run-level `concurrency: { group: opencode-agent, cancel-in-progress: false }` keeps one running and one pending run, so each new comment run replaces the pending one before any job `if:` is evaluated. A genuine `/oc` command waiting in the pending slot is therefore cancelled by the next unrelated comment.
- Templates are worse: `configs/mcp-templates/opencode-github-workflow.yml`, the `cmd_create_workflow` heredoc in `.agents/scripts/opencode-github-setup-helper.sh`, and both snippets in `.agents/tools/git/opencode-github.md` run `anomalyco/opencode/github` **directly** behind the same `contains()` gate with `contents: write`. In a repo that uses them, every aidevops-signed comment starts a paid agent run. The documented "hardening" (`author_association` OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) does not help, because signed comments are posted by the owner account.
- A managed downstream repo carrying a copy of this workflow measured about 2,500 runs/day on its self-hosted runner pool from the same gate; it is tracked separately in that repo. This issue fixes the framework source and templates.

## How

- Replace each `contains(body, '/oc') || contains(body, '/opencode')` gate with a whitespace-anchored approximation of the script rule, using GitHub expressions only:
  `startsWith(body, '/oc') || startsWith(body, '/opencode') || contains(body, ' /oc') || contains(body, ' /opencode') || contains(body, fromJSON('"\n/oc"')) || contains(body, fromJSON('"\n/opencode"'))`
  (`fromJSON` decodes the newline; `\r\n` bodies still match `\n/…`). `//opencode.ai` no longer matches because it is preceded by `/`, not whitespace or line start. Keep the in-script regex as the authoritative check.
- `.github/workflows/opencode-agent.yml`: remove the workflow-level `concurrency` block and add job-level `concurrency: { group: opencode-agent, cancel-in-progress: false }` to the `opencode-agent` job only. The global group still serializes repository-mutating runs; Security Validation and Audit Log run unserialized and cheap.
- Update the comment above the old concurrency block, which currently says no-op comments are filtered "before they enter this queue"; that was never true for run-level concurrency.
- Apply the same gate to `configs/mcp-templates/opencode-github-workflow.yml`, the `opencode-github-setup-helper.sh` heredoc, and `.agents/tools/git/opencode-github.md` (basic and hardening snippets).

## Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/opencode-agent.yml`
- `configs/mcp-templates/opencode-github-workflow.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-github-setup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/git/opencode-github.md`

## Acceptance

- A comment whose body starts with `/oc …` or contains ` /opencode …` mid-line still runs Security Validation.
- A signed comment with no command (only the `[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)` footer) creates a run whose jobs are all skipped.
- No `OpenCode AI Agent` run is cancelled by concurrency before its jobs are evaluated; only the `opencode-agent` job serializes.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-agent-workflow-security.sh`, `actionlint` (if installed) and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-github-setup-helper.sh` pass.

## Verification

- After merge: `gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/workflows/opencode-agent.yml/runs?created=>=<merge time>&per_page=50" --jq '[.workflow_runs[].conclusion] | group_by(.) | map({c: .[0], n: length})'` shows `skipped` instead of `cancelled` and `success` for signed comments.

</details>

title: fix(gh-failure-miner): stop hourly refiling of closed already-satisfied systemic CI signals
body:
## What

`gh-failure-miner-helper.sh` refiles the same systemic-CI issue every hour for one old failed run that a merged PR already fixed. Several runners also file it at the same moment. Make the miner skip a signal when:

1. a recently closed issue with the same signal tag already records the failure as fixed or already satisfied; or
2. every failed run behind the cluster started before that closure, so it adds no new evidence.

Also stop two runners from filing the same signal within seconds of each other.

## Why

Evidence from public issues in this repo:

- Signal tag `gh-failure-miner:58e541a9500f` (`Shell Suite Main Health`, `grep: write error: Broken pipe`) comes from one scheduled run, 44731141317, started 2026-11-20T12:33Z.
- PR #39476 removed that pipeline step and merged 2026-11-20T16:40Z.
- After the merge, the miner still filed #39497, #39514, #39540, #39552, #39566, #39575, #39587 and #39588. Each issue cites only that pre-fix run. Each cost a worker dispatch that closed it as `already_satisfied` with `evidence_pr: 39476`.
- #39592 (runner vladimirdulov) and #39593 (runner alex-solovyev) were filed 4 seconds apart at 2026-11-21T02:15Z, each with the same body and tag.

Root cause: `issue_already_exists()` at `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh:1295` searches only `--state open`. Once a worker closes the issue, the next hourly pass finds no open match, and the old run is still inside the lookback window. Cross-runner duplicates come from GitHub search-index lag between two runners filing at the same time.

## How

Files to modify:

- `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh`: `issue_already_exists()` (line ~1295) and its caller `create_or_preview_issue()` (line ~1327).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-failure-miner-signature-noise.sh`: extend the existing signature-noise test (reference pattern from PR #39476) with a closed-issue suppression case.

Approach:

1. Also look up closed issues with the same signal tag, for example `--state all` with the newest `closedAt`. If one closed after the newest failed event in the cluster, skip filing and log `suppressed: closed_after_newest_event`. A new failure after the closure must still file.
2. To stop the cross-runner race, re-check for an open issue with the same tag right after creating one. If an older one exists, close the newer one as a duplicate of it, using the existing wrapper or comment path. Alternatively, use the existing dispatch-claim or lock primitive if the miner already has one; check before inventing a new one.

## Acceptance

- With a closed `already_satisfied` issue whose closure is newer than every failed run in the cluster, the miner files nothing.
- A failed run newer than the closure still files a new issue.
- Two miner passes in a row against the same open signal create at most one open issue.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh` reports no findings, and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-failure-miner-signature-noise.sh` passes.

title: t19230: perf(gh-transport): refund the primary pacing slot for free 304 revalidations
body:
## Task


Local REST primary pacing charges a full schedule slot for every admitted GET, including conditional revalidations that GitHub answers with `304 Not Modified` at zero primary-quota cost. Refund the pacing slot when a completed response is free, so free revalidations stop pushing paid and latency-sensitive reads (merge gates, check snapshots, app-token reads) past their read timeouts.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Local REST primary pacing charges a full schedule slot for every admitted GET, including conditional revalidations that GitHub answers with `304 Not Modified` at zero primary-quota cost. Refund the pacing slot when a completed response is free, so free revalidations stop pushing paid and latency-sensitive reads (merge gates, check snapshots, app-token reads) past their read timeouts.

## Why

Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log`, trailing hour, 2026-11-21 ~02:20 UTC, single host:

- 8,452 REST core attempts. 3,576 (42.3%) were `304`; the log's cost column records `0` for 3,772 attempts and `1` for 4,522. Paid spend was about 4,876 points/h, close to the 5,000/h window, so pacing correctly engages.
- 68 transport timeouts in the same hour: `github-app-auth-helper.sh` 23, `shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` 14, `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` 14 (the pre-merge check snapshot, so Pulse merges of finished worker PRs defer), `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` 7, `pulse-merge-rest-state.sh` 4.
- `gh_transport_capacity.primary_wait` spaces admissions at `interval = (reset - now) / available` and advances `pacing.retry_at` by one interval for every admission. `gh_transport_budget.Budget.finish` updates `quota` and `reservation` but never touches `pacing`, so a 304 permanently consumes a slot. At a 42% free share, the schedule admits about 42% fewer paid-equivalent requests than the remaining balance allows early in each window, and queued reads wait longer than necessary.
- Concrete impact: a merge-time check-run snapshot page took 9,039 ms for a 304 under pacing versus 0.5–0.9 s unpaced (see GH#39590).

## How

- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py` `run()` already parses `status` from `included_headers(output)`. Pass it to `_finish_budget(...)` and on to `Budget.finish(...)` as a keyword argument (for example `free=status == 304`), defaulting to "not free" so other callers are unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py` `Budget.finish`: when the response is free and observed headers are valid, call a new helper in `gh_transport_capacity.py` inside the same transaction. The helper moves `pacing.retry_at` back by one current interval (`(reset - now) / max(available, 1)`) for the same scope/resource and window (`pacing.reset == quota.reset`), clamped to `now`. Never move it before `now`, never create a pacing row, never touch secondary-ceiling accounting (`admission_history`) or reservations.
- Keep fail-closed behaviour: invalid or missing headers mean no refund. Cooldowns, exhaustion, concurrency and the 900 points/min secondary ceiling are unchanged.
- Read GH#37570 (delivery class) and the GH#38566 conditional-cache notes in `gh-transport-governor.py` before editing. The refund must not let delivery-class reads, or 304 bursts, exceed the secondary ceilings, which `capacity_wait` enforces separately.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`

## Acceptance

- A 304 response on an eligible GET returns its pacing slot: after admission plus a free finish, the next admission's `retry_at` equals the value before the free admission (within float tolerance), clamped to `now`.
- A paid (200) response, an error, or a response without valid rate-limit headers leaves pacing exactly as today.
- Secondary-ceiling counts, reservations, cooldowns and exhaustion handling are unchanged.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py` passes.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`
- Runtime, after deploy: rerun the trailing-hour timeout breakdown from `gh-api-calls.log` (rows with kind `timeout`, grouped by caller) at comparable load, and compare against the 68/h baseline above. Expect `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` and `shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` timeouts to fall.

title: fix(dispatch-dedup-stale): superseded CANCELLED check runs misclassify green PRs as ready_failed and unassign their issue
body:
## What

`_stale_recovery_find_open_pr()` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` (lines ~385-396) labels a PR `ready_failed` if any entry in its `statusCheckRollup` is `CANCELLED`, `STALE`, `FAILURE`, and so on. It does not reduce entries to the latest run per check name first. Concurrency-group workflows (for example `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`) leave several superseded `CANCELLED` runs next to a later `SUCCESS` run. A green PR then gets labelled terminally failed.

The escalation that follows (`_stale_recovery_escalate_pr_checkpoint`) removes the issue's assignee. That makes the maintainer assignee gate fail for real ("Issue #N has no assignee"). The misclassification becomes true and the green PR stays blocked.

## Why

Observed on #39539 / PR #39543:

- The PR rollup held 7 `CANCELLED` and 3 `SUCCESS` runs of `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` at the same head. All other required checks passed.
- At 2026-11-21T00:00:54Z, stale recovery unassigned the issue and applied `status:blocked` with `kind=ready_failed`. The gate re-ran and failed with "Issue #39539 has no assignee".
- A later pass returned the issue to `status:available` but did not restore the assignee. The PR stayed `BLOCKED` until a supervisor pass re-assigned the PR author. The gate then passed and the PR merged as-is (merge sha 2655d1ed).
- Meanwhile #39539 was again a `status:available` dispatch candidate while a ready PR existed, so a duplicate implementation was possible.

## How

Files to modify:

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`: in the `terminal_failure` jq definition inside `_stale_recovery_find_open_pr()`, group rollup entries by check identity (`.name // .context`, plus workflow name where present). Keep only the newest by `completedAt // startedAt // createdAt`, then test that entry's conclusion. Treat `CANCELLED` as terminal only when it is the newest result for that check.
- Look for an existing test that covers stale-PR checkpoint classification (search `tests/` for `ready_failed`) and add a case: CANCELLED-then-SUCCESS for the same check name classifies as `ready`. If no such test exists, verify with a jq fixture run in the PR description rather than new test infrastructure.

Optional, smaller scope: for `ready_failed` PRs whose only failing check is the assignee gate, do not remove the PR author's assignment.

## Acceptance

- A non-draft PR whose newest run of each check is SUCCESS classifies as `ready`, even with older CANCELLED runs of the same check.
- A PR whose newest run of a check is FAILURE or CANCELLED still classifies as `ready_failed`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` reports no findings.
