title: t19231: fix(worker-blocker-log): lock wait budget of ~100 ms drops blocker events under load (flaky parallel-appenders test)
body:
## Task


`test-worker-blocker-log.mjs` "parallel appenders recover after a stale reclaim lock" fails intermittently under host load. The cause is in production code: `acquireWorkerBlockerLock` waits at most about 100 ms (`LOCK_RETRIES = 25` × `LOCK_RETRY_MS = 4`, `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-lock.mjs:21-22`). When the wait runs out, `appendWorkerBlockerEvent` returns `false` and the CLI exits 1 with empty stderr. Under contention this drops worker blocker events without any signal, not just in tests.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`test-worker-blocker-log.mjs` "parallel appenders recover after a stale reclaim lock" fails intermittently under host load. The cause is in production code: `acquireWorkerBlockerLock` waits at most about 100 ms (`LOCK_RETRIES = 25` × `LOCK_RETRY_MS = 4`, `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-lock.mjs:21-22`). When the wait runs out, `appendWorkerBlockerEvent` returns `false` and the CLI exits 1 with empty stderr. Under contention this drops worker blocker events without any signal, not just in tests.

## Evidence

- Failed twice in the full plugin suite (`npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`) on macOS at load averages of 17–38: once during GH#39573 validation, and once in the `commit-and-pr` validator for GH#39582 (1482/1483 pass, `Error: blocker logger exited 1:` with empty stderr, `tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs:406`).
- Passes alone: `node --test --test-name-pattern="parallel appenders" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs` → 1/1 in 246 ms.
- The test spawns 12 concurrent appender subprocesses after planting a stale `.lock.reclaim` file. Under load, one holder plus the stale-reclaim pass can exceed the ~100 ms total wait.

## How

Replace the fixed retry count with a wall-clock deadline that tolerates scheduler delay, for example a 2–5 s total budget with capped jittered backoff. Keep it synchronous (`Atomics.wait`) and best-effort, and keep the existing stale/owned-lock semantics in `worker-blocker-lock.mjs`. Optionally write a one-line reason to stderr when the lock cannot be acquired, so a dropped event is diagnosable. Change `worker-blocker-log.mjs` only for that stderr reason. Do not weaken the test's assertion that all 12 events land.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-lock.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-log.mjs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` passes the "parallel appenders" and "concurrent appenders" cases under concurrent load (for example with the suite run twice in parallel).
- [ ] An uncontended append still returns promptly, and a permanently held fresh lock still returns `false` within the new bounded deadline (no hang).

## Verification

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs
npm --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops run test
```

Pulse ran 10-14 of 20 worker slots while 100+ issues were runnable; launch ceremony p50 was 274 s, about 30 serial REST calls under pacing.

Two defects keep the advisory off:

1. `advisory_due()` in `.agents/scripts/github_auth_usage.py` requires `min_remaining == 0` or `< AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REST_CORE_BUDGET_HARD_FLOOR`. That floor defaults to `0` (`_cb_rest_core_bounds`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`), so only exhaustion qualifies. The transport governor paces requests to avoid exhaustion, so consumption pins near `limit - reserve` (4,543 of 5,000 points per hour here) and the signal never appears.
2. `_pulse_github_app_advise_maybe()` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh` runs only after a progress-stage deferral. Pacing makes those rare (5 in the retained `pulse.log`, all with REST mode `unknown`).

## How

- `github_auth_usage.py`: read the authoritative REST-core `limit` offline from the Pulse cache (`AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REST_CORE_CACHE`, default `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-rest-core.json`; same path as `_CB_REST_CORE_CACHE_FILE`). Compute known quota cost per hour from the report window. Report `rest_core_limit`, `known_quota_cost_per_hour` and `rest_core_saturation`. Treat saturation of at least 0.8 as due, alongside the existing exhaustion and floor tests. If the limit is missing, keep today's behaviour.
- `pulse-budget-priority.sh`: call `_pulse_github_app_advise_maybe` from the cycle-start (non-quiet) `_pulse_set_rest_core_budget_priority`. The existing 6h stamp and background/fail-open contract still bound it.
- `.agents/reference/github-auth.md` "Local usage": document the saturation criterion and the cycle-start refresh.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh`

- With no limit cache, the result equals the previous exhaustion/floor logic.

title: repos migrate-layout plan stalls on multi-GB OpenCode session databases (whole-database PRAGMA integrity_check)
body:
## Observed

`aidevops repos migrate-layout plan` did not finish on a machine with large OpenCode session databases, so the guarded move of one repository could not be planned.

Command (placeholders for the workspace, plan file and repository):

```
aidevops repos migrate-layout plan --workspace <workspace> --output <plan.json> --include-registered-paths --source <workspace>/<repo>
```

- Run 1: hit a 180-second tool timeout with no output.
- Run 2: under a bounded operation, no output and no plan file after about 11.6 minutes (696 s); cancelled. Total time to completion was not measured.
- While run 2 was going, `lsof -p <pid>` showed the Python process holding one isolated per-project `opencode.db` open read-only.
- Database sizes on this machine: that isolated per-project `opencode.db` is 90.3 GB (22,037,522 pages of 4096 bytes, freelist 0); the default OpenCode `opencode.db` is 80.2 GB. The planner inspects both.

## Likely cause (from reading the code, not profiled)

`sqlite_consumer()` in the SQLite inspection module:

- the row lookups read only `project.worktree` and `session.directory` by exact value, which is cheap;
- it then runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the whole database, for every consumer database, on every plan.

A full integrity check reads every page, so its cost grows with total database size rather than with the two small tables the migration uses.

The same function is called again from `validate_database_consumer()` in the main migration module, so validation repeats the full check.

Related, main migration module: `update_database()` runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and before `commit`. For a database that has matching rows, that would hold the write lock on a live session database for the length of a full check.

## Effect

The audited route for moving a canonical checkout is not usable in an interactive session on a machine with a long session history. The fallback is a manual directory rename plus `git worktree repair`, which skips the journal, rollback and consumer retargeting the tool exists to provide.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate-sqlite.py`
- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`

## Proposed fix

Functions: `sqlite_consumer` (SQLite inspection module); `update_database` and `plan_consumers` (main migration module).

Options, implementer to choose and justify:

1. Scope the check to the tables the migration reads and writes: `PRAGMA integrity_check(project)` and `PRAGMA integrity_check(session)`. Table-scoped checks need SQLite 3.33 or later; confirm the version of the `sqlite3` module in use and keep a fallback.
2. Skip the integrity check at plan time for a database with no matching rows, since nothing will be written to it.
3. In `update_database()`, run the scoped check, not a whole-database check, inside the write transaction.
4. Print one `AIDEVOPS_PROGRESS:` line per database inspected so a bounded operation shows progress instead of looking hung.

Reference pattern: the existing fixed allow-list in `validated_sql_target()` already names the only two tables and columns in scope.

## Verification

- `aidevops repos migrate-layout plan` with one `--source` writes a plan in seconds when the OpenCode databases are tens of gigabytes and hold no rows for the source path.
- A database with matching rows still gets a check covering `project` and `session` before and after the update, and a corrupted table in scope still fails the plan.
- Existing migrate-layout tests pass. Test file paths not checked; find them with `git ls-files '*repo*layout*'`.

title: t19234: perf(relay): steering relay and issue-watch reads use stable per-issue URLs so unchanged issues revalidate as free 304s
body:
## Task


Make the Pulse steering relay and issue-watch reads revalidate for free. Replace the per-repo `issues?since=<moving timestamp>` listing, whose URL changes on every run, with stable per-issue reads, so the transport governor's conditional cache (GH#38566) gets `304 Not Modified` at zero primary-quota cost when nothing changed.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the Pulse steering relay and issue-watch reads revalidate for free. Replace the per-repo `issues?since=<moving timestamp>` listing, whose URL changes on every run, with stable per-issue reads, so the transport governor's conditional cache (GH#38566) gets `304 Not Modified` at zero primary-quota cost when nothing changed.

## Why

Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` on one host, 2026-11-21, about 2.2h window:

- `worker-bus-relay-helper.sh` made 460 attempts: 440 paid `200` (cost 1 each) and 20 free `304`, a 4% free share. Host-wide REST traffic in the same period was about 42% free `304`.
- Trailing hour: the relay was the 9th-largest REST cost caller at 182 points on 188 attempts. That is about 5% of the 3,800-point logged REST-core hour on a PAT budget the governor already holds near saturation (see GH#39611).
- Cause: `_relay_repo` (`.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh:399-422`) lists `repos/{repo}/issues?state=all&since=${since_iso}...`, where `since` is `min(checked) - 60`. `checked` advances every run (`WORKER_BUS_RELAY_MIN_INTERVAL`, default 120 s; run every 2 min by `worker-watchdog.sh` and at each Pulse cycle), so the URL never repeats and `gh_conditional_cache` never holds a validator for it. The watch pass (`.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh:345`) has the same pattern.
- `repos/{repo}/issues/{n}` has a stable URL. An unchanged issue returns `304` (free), and `comments` and `updated_at` in the body already tell the relay whether to read comments (`_relay_worker`, lines 349-372).

## How

- In `_relay_repo` / `_relay_worker`, read each due worker's issue with `_relay_get "repos/${repo}/issues/${issue_number}"` (stable URL, conditional-cache eligible) instead of filtering a moving `since` listing. Keep the existing comment-count and `updated_at >= started` gate before any comments read, and the `delivery` admission class.
- Apply the same change to the issue-watch pass in `.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh` (listing at line 345).
- Keep the single-runner lock, REST-core deferrable gate, stop flag and failure handling. A failed or deferred read leaves state unchanged, as today.
- Request count per run becomes one per due worker or watch instead of one per repo. That stays far below secondary limits at current scale (tens per run). Note the trade-off in `.agents/reference/session-bus.md` "Pulse steering relay" and in the helper header (lines 16-22).
- Before editing, read the GH#38566 notes in `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py` (lines 1-30) to confirm `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}` through the shim is an eligible conditional GET.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh`
- `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`

## Acceptance

- After deploy, with unchanged watched issues, relay attempts in `gh-api-calls.log` are mostly `304` with cost `0`, not `200` with cost `1`.
- Steering still arrives. A new comment, a steering label added after start, and issue closure each produce exactly one relay message, as before.
- Existing relay tests pass: `rg -l "worker-bus-relay" .agents/scripts/tests` lists them; run each with `bash`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh`
- The relay tests found above.
- Runtime, after deploy: tabulate the last hour of `worker-bus-relay-helper.sh` rows in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log`, grouped by field 15 (HTTP status) and field 17 (quota cost). Compare against the 440/20 baseline.

title: t19235: fix(gh-api-report): count HTTP 304 not-modified attempts as successful, not failed, in the usage aggregator
body:
## Task


Stop counting HTTP `304 Not Modified` attempts as failures in the GitHub API usage report. Callers that send their own `If-None-Match` get a free `304`. Native `gh` exits non-zero on it, so the attempt row records `outcome=error`, and `gh-api-aggregate.awk` adds it to `failed_attempts`. Report these as successful not-modified reads, with their own counter, so `failed_attempts` shows only real failures.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop counting HTTP `304 Not Modified` attempts as failures in the GitHub API usage report. Callers that send their own `If-None-Match` get a free `304`. Native `gh` exits non-zero on it, so the attempt row records `outcome=error`, and `gh-api-aggregate.awk` adds it to `failed_attempts`. Report these as successful not-modified reads, with their own counter, so `failed_attempts` shows only real failures.

## Why

Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` on one host, 2026-11-21, about one hour:

- `pulse-wrapper.sh` and `pulse-merge-routine.sh` had 107 attempt rows with field 14 `error`, field 15 `304` and field 17 quota cost `0`. These are intended free revalidations, not failures.
- Callers that set `If-None-Match` themselves (`rg -l "If-None-Match" .agents/scripts --glob '*.sh'`) include `pulse-events-tickle.sh`, `pulse-repo-dormancy.sh`, `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` and `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`.
- `gh-api-aggregate.awk:458-464` treats every outcome other than `success` as failed. `aidevops github auth usage` and the pulse diagnostics therefore report inflated failure counts: about 25% of the `pulse-wrapper.sh` failures in that hour. That sends diagnosis toward phantom failures, which happened during the session that filed this issue.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/gh-api-aggregate.awk`, in the attempt rule around lines 440-464, treat `http_status == "304"` as a successful attempt whatever `outcome` says. Add a `not_modified_attempts` metric through `metric_add_dimensions`, emitted beside `successful_attempts` and `failed_attempts` (lines 103 and 525 show the emit pattern). Leave `metric_add("outcome", ...)` unchanged, so raw outcome counts still show what was logged.
- Do not change the writer (`gh-api-instrument.sh` / governor). Historical rows must classify correctly too, and an aggregator-only fix covers them.
- If a consumer of the JSON relies on the exact key set, update it. To find consumers, run `rg -n "failed_attempts" .agents/scripts` and `rg -n "successful_attempts" .agents/scripts`.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-aggregate.awk`

## Acceptance

- On a log containing `error`/`304`/cost-`0` attempt rows, those rows count in `successful_attempts` and `not_modified_attempts`, not in `failed_attempts`.
- `404`, `422`, `5xx` and transport errors still count as failed.
- Existing aggregator tests pass. To find them: `rg -l "gh-api-aggregate" .agents/scripts/tests`.

## Verification

- The tests found above, each run with `bash`.
- Runtime: `aidevops github auth usage --since 1h` (or the `usage` subcommand of `.agents/scripts/github_auth_cli.py`) before and after. `failed_attempts` for `pulse-wrapper.sh` drops by about the count of its `error`/`304` rows in the same window.

title: t19236: fix(wait-checks): end early with a rebase instruction when required checks are missing because the PR conflicts with its base
body:
## Task


Make `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait` (and `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks`, which calls it) end early when required checks are missing because the PR conflicts with its base. GitHub does not start `pull_request` workflows for a PR whose merge ref cannot be built, so those required contexts never appear. Today the waiter polls until its timeout (1800 s interactive, 200 s headless) and then reports a pending timeout. It should report the conflict and the rebase step instead.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait` (and `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks`, which calls it) end early when required checks are missing because the PR conflicts with its base. GitHub does not start `pull_request` workflows for a PR whose merge ref cannot be built, so those required contexts never appear. Today the waiter polls until its timeout (1800 s interactive, 200 s headless) and then reports a pending timeout. It should report the conflict and the rebase step instead.

## Why

Evidence from marcusquinn/aidevops PR #39617, 2026-11-21:

- Head `407ca8d4` was pushed while `TODO.md` conflicted with `main` (`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` gave `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in TODO.md`). `pull_request_target` gates ran. No `pull_request` workflow run was created for that head in more than 20 minutes (`gh run list --event pull_request` showed 0). `wait-checks` stayed in heartbeat with `missing=Complexity Analysis, Framework Validation, Qlty Regression Gate` for about 23 minutes, until the session diagnosed the conflict by hand.
- After a rebase, head `63160baf` had 21 `pull_request` runs within about a minute.
- `TODO.md` conflicts are common because planning lines land on `main` all the time (PR #39596 hit the same conflict in the same session). Every interactive or worker wait on such a PR loses its whole timeout and then needs manual diagnosis.

## How

- Model on `classify_draft_stall` (`.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh:789-812`), which ends a stalled draft wait with `WAIT_CHECKS=draft-required-missing` and exit 9. Add a sibling `classify_conflict_stall`, called from `wait_for_checks` next to the draft check (around lines 907-910).
- Trigger: `required_only` is set, `missing_contexts` is non-empty, `elapsed >= _GCW_EMPTY_REQUIRED_SETTLE_SECONDS` (line 25, default 90 s), and one PR read (`gh pr view <n> --repo <r> --json mergeable,baseRefName`) returns `mergeable == "CONFLICTING"`. `UNKNOWN` while GitHub computes is not a conflict; keep waiting. Read it at most once per heartbeat interval, not every poll, to limit REST cost.
- On trigger: re-verify the head as the draft path does (`verified_head_sha`; a changed head restarts observation), print `WAIT_CHECKS=conflict-required-missing: PR <n> conflicts with <base>; rebase onto origin/<base>, push, then wait again`, and return a new distinct exit code (10). Document it in the usage text (lines 57-60).
- Fixture mode: follow how `read_draft_state` reads fixtures under `AIDEVOPS_GH_CHECKS_FIXTURE_DIR`, so a fixture can supply `mergeable`.
- Check `full-loop-helper.sh` `cmd_wait_checks` (around line 507) and any caller that switches on waiter exit codes (`rg -n "gh-checks-wait-helper.sh\" wait|wait-checks" .agents/scripts`). Treat 10 like 9: actionable and non-terminal, not a CI failure.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- With required contexts missing, `mergeable=CONFLICTING`, and elapsed past the settle window, the waiter prints the `WAIT_CHECKS=conflict-required-missing` line and exits 10 within one heartbeat interval.
- `mergeable=UNKNOWN` or `MERGEABLE` with missing contexts keeps the current pending behaviour.
- Draft, zero-job, failure, success and head-change paths are unchanged.
- Existing waiter tests pass: `rg -l "gh-checks-wait-helper" .agents/scripts/tests`, then run each with `bash`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- The waiter tests found above.
- Runtime: on a scratch PR that conflicts with its base, `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks <PR> --repo <owner/repo>` exits 10 with the rebase line in about 90-210 s instead of timing out.

title: canonical Git guard: no way to mend linked worktrees after a checkout moves; blocks read-only git archive and stash list
body:
## What

After a canonical checkout is moved or renamed on disk, its linked worktrees stop working and there is no allowed way to mend them. The canonical Git guard also refuses three commands that change nothing in the checkout.

## Observed (interactive session, macOS, v3.39.249 to v3.39.253)

1. A canonical checkout with eight linked worktrees was moved (`mv <old-path> <new-path>`) to free the path for a new repository of the same name. Each worktree's `.git` file still pointed at `<old-path>/.git/worktrees/<name>`, so every Git command inside those worktrees failed with `fatal: not a git repository`.
2. The owner ran `git -C <new-path> worktree repair` in their own terminal. Result: `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git worktree'`. The block message offers `fast-forward-current` and `sync-mirror`, neither of which mends worktree pointers. `canonical-recovery-helper.sh` has no command for it either.
3. `aidevops repos migrate-layout plan`, the route `canonical-recovery-helper.sh` points to for layout moves, did not finish (tracked separately in #39613).
4. Read-only commands were blocked in a canonical checkout:
   - `git -C <canonical> archive --format=tar HEAD -- <paths>` (writes only to stdout): `canonical worktree mutation via 'git archive'`.
   - `git -C <canonical> stash list`: `canonical worktree mutation via 'git stash'`.

Workarounds used: `git ls-files` plus `tar -T` instead of `git archive`; `git --git-dir=<canonical>/.git/worktrees/<name> --work-tree=<worktree> status` to prove the stranded worktrees were clean. The worktrees are still stranded.

## Expected

- A sanctioned, audited way to mend linked-worktree pointers after a canonical checkout moves, for example `canonical-recovery-helper.sh repair-worktrees --repo PATH --confirm REPAIR_WORKTREE_POINTERS`, which runs `git worktree repair`, logs to the canonical recovery audit file and prints each pointer it rewrote. The guard's block message for `git worktree repair` should name it.
- `git archive` without `--output`/`-o` (or with an output path outside the checkout) and `git stash list` / `git stash show` are treated as read-only in a canonical checkout. `git stash push|pop|apply|drop|clear` stay blocked.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py` (block message)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_readonly.py` (archive/stash checks moved here: canonical_git_policy.py hit the Qlty file-complexity ratchet)

## How

- `canonical_git_policy.py`: `READ_ONLY` (line 26) and `_classify_canonical_operation` (line 253). Model the new argument-aware checks on the existing `CANONICAL_CHECKS` entries and on `_is_linked_worktree_remove_for_canonical`.
- `canonical-recovery-helper.sh`: add the repair command beside `repair-upstream`; the confirmation token, audit log call and usage text follow that command's pattern.
- `test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: cases for `archive` to stdout (allowed), `archive -o <path inside checkout>` (blocked), `stash list` (allowed), `stash push` (blocked), `worktree repair` (blocked, message names the helper).
- The guard's block-message text may live in another file: find it with `rg -n "fast-forward-current" .agents/scripts/` and add that file to the change if so.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` passes with the new cases.
- In a throwaway repository with one linked worktree: move the main checkout, confirm Git fails inside the worktree, run the new helper command, confirm `git -C <worktree> status` works again and the audit log has one new entry.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the edited shell files.

title: full-loop finalize-receipt: misleading marker-mismatch error when run outside a Git worktree
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh finalize-receipt <PR> <REPO>` reports the wrong cause when it is run from a directory that is not a Git worktree.

## Observed (interactive session, macOS, v3.39.253)

1. PR merged through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`; `record-no-release <PR> <REPO>` succeeded from a directory outside any repository.
2. `finalize-receipt <PR> <REPO>` from that same directory failed with: `Finalization blocked: legacy cleanup marker does not match the exact finalized owner contract`.
3. The marker and the receipt were both correct. Running the same command from the PR's linked worktree succeeded: `Cleanup receipt finalized for merged PR #N (release:not-requested)`.

Cause: `_full_loop_retire_finalized_cleanup_marker` starts with `worktree=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || return 1`. Outside a worktree that returns 1, and `cmd_finalize_receipt` prints the marker-mismatch message for every failure of that function. The explicit `REPO` argument suggests the command works from anywhere, as `record-no-release` does.

## Expected

Either of these, whichever is smaller:

- Outside a Git worktree, resolve the worktree from the cleanup receipt (it records `.worktree`) and retire the marker there; or
- Fail with a message that names the cause and the fix: run the command from the PR's worktree, with the path from the receipt.

The marker-mismatch message stays for real mismatches.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`

## How

- `_full_loop_retire_finalized_cleanup_marker` and `cmd_finalize_receipt` in that file. Give the "not in a worktree" case its own return code or its own check before the marker comparison, so the caller can print a different message.
- Reference pattern: `_full_loop_hint_finalize_receipt` in the same file already prints a cause plus the exact command to run.
- Add the case to the existing finalize-receipt test if one covers this function: find it with `rg -l "finalize-receipt" .agents/scripts/tests/`. The path is not known in advance.

## Verification

- From a directory outside any repository, `finalize-receipt` for a merged PR with a valid receipt and marker either succeeds or prints the new message; it no longer prints the marker-mismatch message.
- From the PR's worktree, behaviour is unchanged.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the edited file.

title: t19238: fix(test): repo-layout prune dry-run races apply within the same second (retention-days 0)
body:
## Task


Fix a timing race in `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` `test_prune_removes_expired_database_backups_and_blocks_rollback`. On a fast host it fails with `IndexError: list index out of range` at line 375, because `dry_run["pruned"]` is empty.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Fix a timing race in `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` `test_prune_removes_expired_database_backups_and_blocks_rollback`. On a fast host it fails with `IndexError: list index out of range` at line 375, because `dry_run["pruned"]` is empty.

## Why

- The test runs `apply`, then right away runs `prune --retention-days 0` as a dry run (lines 371-375) and expects one receipt to prune.
- `prune_reason()` prunes only when `item["finished"] < cutoff` (`.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py:1867`), with `cutoff = int(time.time()) - days * 86400` (`:1911`). With `days=0`, when `apply` and the dry run fall in the same second, `finished == cutoff`, so nothing is pruned.
- The existing `time.sleep(1.1)` at line 378 comes only before the later `--apply` prune. It does not cover the dry run.
- Seen 2026-11-21 on macOS, SQLite 3.54.1, run with `uv run --no-project --with pyyaml python3 -B tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`. The test fails identically on `main` (`2940293aa1`) and on PR #39615's head. The other 16 tests pass. This is a test defect. The production retention rule is correct.

## How

- In `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`, move `time.sleep(1.1)` from before the `--apply` prune (line 378) to before the dry-run prune (line 371). Both retention-0 calls then see `finished < cutoff`. Leave the `fresh` default-retention assertion (line 368) before the sleep.
- Do not change `prune_reason()` or the cutoff arithmetic.

## Files Scope

- `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`

## Acceptance

- `test_prune_removes_expired_database_backups_and_blocks_rollback` passes on a fast local host 3 times in a row.
- The other 16 tests in the file still pass.

## Verification

`uv run --no-project --with pyyaml python3 -B tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` shows `OK` for 17 tests. PyYAML is a test-only dependency; `uv run --with pyyaml` supplies it without installing it globally.

</details>

title: t19239: fix(full-loop): runtime-pending PRs need a verifier route that works when the verifier is not the PR author
body:
## Task


Give runtime-pending PRs a verifier route that works when the verifier is not the PR author. Add `full-loop-helper.sh verify-runtime <PR> --repo <owner/repo> --testing "<evidence>"`. It records `runtime-verified` evidence in the PR's generated `## Runtime Testing` section, then removes `hold-for-review` when runtime verification was the hold's only scope. Point the documented remedy at the new command.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Give runtime-pending PRs a verifier route that works when the verifier is not the PR author. Add `full-loop-helper.sh verify-runtime <PR> --repo <owner/repo> --testing "<evidence>"`. It records `runtime-verified` evidence in the PR's generated `## Runtime Testing` section, then removes `hold-for-review` when runtime verification was the hold's only scope. Point the documented remedy at the new command.

## Why

- GH#39558 introduced `--testing-level runtime-pending`. The PR opens under `hold-for-review`, and the documented remedy is that "a verifier reruns `commit-and-pr` on this branch with `--testing-level runtime-verified --testing "<evidence>"` and removes the hold" (`.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:159`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh:600`).
- That rerun refuses any verifier whose GitHub login differs from the PR author. `issue_open_pr_guard_check()` returns continuation (rc 3) only when the current actor equals the PR author (`.agents/scripts/issue-open-pr-guard.sh:118-120`). Otherwise `commit-and-pr` exits with "Issue #N already has open PR #M; continue branch ... or use an explicit audited replacement" (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:143`).
- Worker PRs are authored by worker logins, and maintainer verifiers use their own login, so the documented route fails for the main case. Seen 2026-11-21 on PR #39615 (GH#39613, Critical risk): it was held about 2 hours. A maintainer session verified it on real 80 GB databases, then could only finish by hand-editing the body's `- **Verification:**` line and removing the label (PR #39615 comment 7058150378).
- `hold-for-review` also has a second scope, "trusted PR-only scope" (`_apply_pr_only_hold`, `full-loop-helper.sh:418-439`). That scope is printed but never recorded on the PR, so a verifier cannot tell which holds it may lift.
- No pulse stage handles runtime-pending PRs (`rg -ln "runtime-pending" .agents/scripts --glob 'pulse*'` is empty), so every such hold waits for a person.

## How

1. In `_apply_pr_only_hold()` (`full-loop-helper.sh:423`), record the hold scope durably: post one marker comment (for example `<!-- aidevops:hold-scope:runtime-pending -->`) or write a body marker. Use the existing safe-write helpers (`gh_pr_edit_safe`, the signed comment path).
2. Add a `verify-runtime` subcommand next to `cmd_wait_checks` (`full-loop-helper.sh:507`). Wire it into `show_help` and the command dispatcher. Before any write it must check (mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary`):
   - the caller has write, maintain or admin permission (reuse the collaborator-permission helper used by `pulse-macos-verification.sh`);
   - the PR is open and same-repository;
   - the local `HEAD` equals the PR `headRefOid`, so evidence binds to the exact head;
   - `_runtime_evidence_is_substantive` accepts the `--testing` text (`full-loop-helper-risk.sh`).
3. Rewrite only the generated `- **Verification:** runtime-pending — ...` line to `runtime-verified — <evidence>`. Re-parse the result with `_runtime_testing_metadata_from_body`, and require `_runtime_testing_merge_refusal` to accept it before `gh pr edit --body-file`. Fail closed when there is not exactly one such section.
4. Remove `hold-for-review` only when the recorded scope is runtime-pending alone. A PR-only scope or an unrecorded scope keeps the label and reports why. Post one audit comment with the head SHA and verifier login.
5. Update `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:159` and the remedy text at `full-loop-helper-risk.sh:600` to name `verify-runtime`.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

## Out of scope

Making pulse route runtime-pending PRs to a capable verifier host (an analogue of `pulse-macos-verification.sh`) is a follow-up that depends on this command.

## Acceptance

- A maintainer whose login differs from the PR author verifies a runtime-pending worker PR with one `verify-runtime` call. The body then passes the merge-time recheck and the hold is gone.
- Callers without write permission, a head mismatch, a fork head, bare or empty evidence, and a PR-only hold scope all refuse without writing anything.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge` still refuses a runtime-pending body.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh` is clean.
- Existing full-loop tests pass: `rg -l "runtime-pending|_runtime_testing_merge_refusal" .agents/scripts/tests`.
- Run `verify-runtime` once against a disposable same-repo test PR, or document a dry run that prints the planned body diff and label change.

</details>
